answer:
Treat the saved inventory as the truth and the Tools as a view of it: tool templates live in ServerStorage, and a `sync` function makes the Backpack plus character hold exactly one Tool per owned weapon, cloning missing ones and removing ones not owned. Run it on every spawn and after any inventory change.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.ToolSync
local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")

local ToolSync = {}

local function templates(): Folder?
	local folder: Folder? = ServerStorage:FindFirstChild("ToolTemplates")
	return folder
end

-- owned is the server's set of weapon ids, e.g. { WoodSword = true, Bow = true }.
function ToolSync.sync(player: Player, owned: { [string]: boolean })
	local backpack = player:FindFirstChildOfClass("Backpack")
	local folder = templates()
	if backpack == nil or folder == nil then
		return
	end
	local present: { [string]: boolean } = {}
	local containers: { Instance } = { backpack }
	if player.Character then
		table.insert(containers, player.Character)
	end
	for _, container in containers do
		for _, child in container:GetChildren() do
			if child:IsA("Tool") then
				if not owned[child.Name] or present[child.Name] then
					child:Destroy() -- not owned anymore, or a duplicate
				else
					present[child.Name] = true
				end
			end
		end
	end
	for id in owned do
		local template = folder:FindFirstChild(id)
		if not present[id] and template and template:IsA("Tool") then
			local tool = template:Clone()
			-- A dropped Tool leaves the Backpack, so the next sync would hand out another copy.
			tool.CanBeDropped = false
			tool.Parent = backpack
		end
	end
end

return ToolSync
```

Hook it up where you load data: `player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function() ToolSync.sync(player, profile.weapons) end)`, and call `sync` again after buying, selling or trading a weapon.

- Templates in ServerStorage cannot be read or cloned by clients, so the only way to get a Tool is through `sync`.
- Checking both Backpack and Character covers an equipped tool, which is parented to the character while held. `CanBeDropped = false` closes the other gap: a dropped Tool sits in Workspace, where `sync` would not see it, so another player could pick it up while its owner gets a fresh copy.
- The Tool's name is its id here; if you rename display names, store the id in an attribute and compare that instead.

answer:
Model the trade as a server object. Each side's offer is a list of item counts; any change to either offer clears both acceptances (the classic last-second swap scam). When both have accepted, the server checks again that each player still owns every offered item, and only then moves everything in one step.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.TradeSession
export type Bag = { [string]: number }
export type Side = { bag: Bag, offer: Bag, accepted: boolean }
export type Trade = { a: Side, b: Side, done: boolean }

local MAX_KINDS_PER_OFFER = 8

local TradeSession = {}

function TradeSession.new(bagA: Bag, bagB: Bag): Trade
	return {
		a = { bag = bagA, offer = {}, accepted = false },
		b = { bag = bagB, offer = {}, accepted = false },
		done = false,
	}
end

local function owns(bag: Bag, offer: Bag): boolean
	for id, n in offer do
		if (bag[id] or 0) < n then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

-- Set one item count in a side's offer (0 removes it). Any change resets both accepts.
function TradeSession.setOffer(trade: Trade, side: Side, id: unknown, countArg: unknown): boolean
	if trade.done or type(id) ~= "string" or type(countArg) ~= "number" then
		return false
	end
	if countArg % 1 ~= 0 or countArg < 0 or countArg > (side.bag[id] or 0) then
		return false
	end
	local kinds = 0
	for _ in side.offer do
		kinds += 1
	end
	if side.offer[id] == nil and countArg > 0 and kinds >= MAX_KINDS_PER_OFFER then
		return false
	end
	side.offer[id] = if countArg > 0 then countArg else nil
	trade.a.accepted, trade.b.accepted = false, false
	return true
end

local function move(from: Bag, to: Bag, offer: Bag)
	for id, n in offer do
		local left = (from[id] or 0) - n
		from[id] = if left > 0 then left else nil
		to[id] = (to[id] or 0) + n
	end
end

-- Returns "waiting", "completed" or "failed" (ownership changed; offers cleared).
function TradeSession.accept(trade: Trade, side: Side): string
	if trade.done then
		return "failed"
	end
	side.accepted = true
	if not (trade.a.accepted and trade.b.accepted) then
		return "waiting"
	end
	if not owns(trade.a.bag, trade.a.offer) or not owns(trade.b.bag, trade.b.offer) then
		trade.a.offer, trade.b.offer = {}, {}
		trade.a.accepted, trade.b.accepted = false, false
		return "failed"
	end
	move(trade.a.bag, trade.b.bag, trade.a.offer)
	move(trade.b.bag, trade.a.bag, trade.b.offer)
	trade.done = true
	return "completed"
end

return TradeSession
```

- The final ownership check matters because items can leave a bag during the trade (sold, dropped, used in another trade); without it, one sword can be traded to two people.
- These bags have no capacity limit; if yours do, also check that each side has room for what it receives before the two `move` calls, and fail the trade otherwise.
- Show both offers to both clients after every change and add a short delay (2-3 s) before Accept is clickable again, so a changed offer is actually seen.
- Save both players' data right after `completed` (and log the trade); a crash before saving would otherwise roll back only one side.

answer:
Every drop gets a server-side registry entry keyed by a GUID: item, count and the world part. Dropping removes the item from the dropper's inventory first; picking up checks the id exists, the player is close, then deletes the registry entry before granting, so the second request finds nothing. Unclaimed drops despawn after a while.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.WorldDrops
local HttpService = game:GetService("HttpService")

export type Bag = { [string]: number }
type Drop = { itemId: string, count: number, part: BasePart }

local PICKUP_RANGE = 10
local DESPAWN_SECONDS = 60

local drops: { [string]: Drop } = {}
local WorldDrops = {}

local function rootOf(player: Player): BasePart?
	local character = player.Character
	if character == nil then
		return nil
	end
	local root: BasePart? = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	return root
end

function WorldDrops.drop(player: Player, bag: Bag, itemId: unknown, countArg: unknown): string?
	local root = rootOf(player)
	if root == nil or type(itemId) ~= "string" or type(countArg) ~= "number" then
		return nil
	end
	local have = bag[itemId] or 0
	if countArg % 1 ~= 0 or countArg < 1 or countArg > have then
		return nil
	end
	bag[itemId] = if have - countArg > 0 then have - countArg else nil

	local id = HttpService:GenerateGUID(false)
	local part = Instance.new("Part")
	part.Name = "Drop"
	part.Size = Vector3.new(1, 1, 1)
	-- Unanchored, the part would be network-owned by the nearest client, which could move it into its range.
	part.Anchored = true
	part.Position = root.Position + root.CFrame.LookVector * 3
	part:SetAttribute("DropId", id)
	part:SetAttribute("ItemId", itemId)
	part.Parent = workspace
	drops[id] = { itemId = itemId, count = countArg, part = part }

	task.delay(DESPAWN_SECONDS, function()
		local entry = drops[id]
		if entry then
			drops[id] = nil
			entry.part:Destroy()
		end
	end)
	return id
end

function WorldDrops.pickup(player: Player, bag: Bag, dropId: unknown): boolean
	if type(dropId) ~= "string" then
		return false
	end
	local entry = drops[dropId]
	local root = rootOf(player)
	if entry == nil or root == nil then
		return false
	end
	if (root.Position - entry.part.Position).Magnitude > PICKUP_RANGE then
		return false
	end
	drops[dropId] = nil -- claim first: a second request for the same id now fails
	entry.part:Destroy()
	bag[entry.itemId] = (bag[entry.itemId] or 0) + entry.count
	return true
end

return WorldDrops
```

- The part only carries the id for the client to point at; what the drop contains is read from the registry, so editing the part's attributes changes nothing.
- Registry first, then destroy, then grant: the order makes double pickups impossible even if two requests arrive in the same frame.
- If your inventory has capacity limits, check room before claiming and leave the drop on the ground when it does not fit.

answer:
`writeVault` yields, and while it waits the same remote can fire again: the second call passes the ownership check because the pet is not removed yet, so the pet is stored twice. Remove (reserve) the item before any yield, put it back if the slow step fails, and allow only one request in flight per player.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.PetStorage
export type Pets = { [string]: boolean }

local PetStorage = {}
local busy: { [Player]: boolean } = {}

-- save is the slow part (a DataStore write); it returns true on success.
function PetStorage.store(player: Player, pets: Pets, petId: unknown, save: (petId: string) -> boolean): boolean
	if type(petId) ~= "string" or busy[player] or not pets[petId] then
		return false
	end
	busy[player] = true
	pets[petId] = nil -- take it out before yielding: a second request can no longer see it
	local ok, saved = pcall(save, petId)
	if not (ok and saved) then
		pets[petId] = true -- the save failed, give the pet back
	end
	busy[player] = nil
	return ok and saved == true
end

return PetStorage
```

- The general rule: mutate server state before the first yield (DataStore, `task.wait`, `WaitForChild`, `InvokeClient`), never after; every yield is a window for a duplicate request.
- `busy` makes concurrent requests from one player fail fast instead of queueing; clear it on `PlayerRemoving` if your saves can outlive the player.
- `pcall(save, ...)` guarantees the `busy` flag is cleared and the pet restored even if the save throws.

answer:
Your code cannot tell "new player" (`ok` and `data == nil`) apart from "the load failed" (`ok == false`), so a failed load becomes defaults that overwrite the real save on leave. Retry the load, and if it still fails, mark the session as not saveable: the player can keep playing on temporary data, but nothing is ever written for them.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.Sessions
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")

local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("PlayerData")

export type Session = { data: { coins: number, level: number }, canSave: boolean }

local sessions: { [Player]: Session } = {}
local Sessions = {}

local function keyFor(userId: number): string
	return "player_" .. userId
end

local function loadWithRetry(userId: number): (boolean, any)
	for attempt = 1, 3 do
		local ok, saved = pcall(function()
			return store:GetAsync(keyFor(userId))
		end)
		if ok then
			return true, saved
		end
		task.wait(attempt)
	end
	return false, nil
end

function Sessions.start(player: Player): Session
	local ok, saved = loadWithRetry(player.UserId)
	local session: Session = { data = { coins = 0, level = 1 }, canSave = ok }
	if ok and type(saved) == "table" then
		session.data.coins = tonumber(saved.coins) or 0
		session.data.level = tonumber(saved.level) or 1
	end
	if player.Parent ~= nil then -- a player who left during the load would leave a stale entry behind
		sessions[player] = session
	end
	return session
end

function Sessions.get(player: Player): Session?
	return sessions[player]
end

function Sessions.save(player: Player): boolean
	local session = sessions[player]
	if session == nil or not session.canSave then
		return false -- never overwrite a save we could not read
	end
	local ok = pcall(function()
		store:SetAsync(keyFor(player.UserId), session.data, { player.UserId })
	end)
	return ok
end

function Sessions.stop(player: Player)
	Sessions.save(player)
	sessions[player] = nil
end

return Sessions
```

- When `canSave` is false, tell the client ("Your data could not load; progress this session will not be saved") so the player can rejoin instead of grinding for nothing.
- `ok == true` with `saved == nil` is the only case that means a new player; that path is safe to save.
- If you prefer, kick instead of guest mode; both are fine, the bug is only ever saving defaults over a read you could not do.

Use a MemoryStore sorted map entry per cooldown name and claim it with `UpdateAsync`: the transform refuses while the stored expiry is in the future, otherwise writes a new expiry. MemoryStore updates are atomic across servers, so exactly one server wins each window. Fail closed: if MemoryStore is unreachable, nobody summons.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.GlobalCooldown
local MemoryStoreService = game:GetService("MemoryStoreService")

local map = MemoryStoreService:GetSortedMap("GlobalCooldowns")

type Claim = { expiresAt: number, jobId: string }

local GlobalCooldown = {}

-- Returns true when this server won the cooldown. Otherwise false and the seconds left (-1 when unknown).
function GlobalCooldown.tryClaim(name: string, seconds: number): (boolean, number)
	local now = DateTime.now().UnixTimestamp
	local jobId: string = game.JobId
	local claimed = false
	local remaining = -1
	local ok = pcall(function()
		map:UpdateAsync(name, function(old: Claim?): Claim?
			if old and old.expiresAt > now then
				claimed, remaining = false, old.expiresAt - now
				return nil
			end
			claimed, remaining = true, 0
			return { expiresAt = now + seconds, jobId = jobId }
		end, seconds + 60)
	end)
	if not ok then
		return false, -1
	end
	return claimed, remaining
end

return GlobalCooldown
```

Usage in the purchase handler:

```lua
--!strict
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")
local GlobalCooldown = require(ServerScriptService.GlobalCooldown)

local function trySummon(spawnBoss: () -> ()): (boolean, string)
	local won, left = GlobalCooldown.tryClaim("WorldBoss", 600)
	if won then
		spawnBoss()
		return true, "The world boss has been summoned!"
	elseif left > 0 then
		return false, string.format("Another server summoned it. Try again in %d:%02d.", left // 60, left % 60)
	end
	return false, "Summoning is unavailable right now."
end

return trySummon
```

- The entry's expiration (`seconds + 60`) lets MemoryStore clean up by itself; the stored `expiresAt` is what decides, so clock drift of a few seconds between servers only shifts the window slightly.
- Charge the item only after `tryClaim` returns true, or refund on failure, so a busy cooldown never eats a purchase.
- `jobId` in the entry tells you which server owns the current boss, handy for a "boss is live in another server, join?" button.
request: Players can buy a "summon world boss" item, and the boss should spawn in only one server, at most once every 10 minutes across the whole game. How do I make a cooldown that every server respects at the same time?

answer:
Each lobby adds a ticket to a MemoryStore queue. A matching loop reads exactly 4 tickets with `allOrNothing`, reserves the arena with `ReserveServerAsync` (which returns the access code immediately), removes the tickets and publishes the match. Every lobby then teleports its own matched players into that reserved server.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.Matchmaker
local MemoryStoreService = game:GetService("MemoryStoreService")
local MessagingService = game:GetService("MessagingService")
local TeleportService = game:GetService("TeleportService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local INVISIBLE_SECONDS = 30 -- read tickets stay hidden from other matchers this long
local TICKET_TTL = 120
local MATCH_TOPIC = "ArenaMatch"

local queue = MemoryStoreService:GetQueue("Arena4", INVISIBLE_SECONDS)
-- userId -> time its ticket expires, so a ticket lost to TTL or a failed publish does not block requeueing
local queuedUntil: { [number]: number } = {}

local Matchmaker = {}

function Matchmaker.enqueue(player: Player): boolean
	local userId: number = player.UserId
	local now = os.clock()
	if (queuedUntil[userId] or 0) > now then
		return false
	end
	local ok = pcall(function()
		queue:AddAsync({ userId = userId }, TICKET_TTL)
	end)
	if ok then
		queuedUntil[userId] = now + TICKET_TTL
	end
	return ok
end

function Matchmaker.tryMatch(size: number, arenaPlaceId: number): { number }?
	local ok, tickets, readId = pcall(function()
		return queue:ReadAsync(size, true, 0)
	end)
	if not ok or type(tickets) ~= "table" or #tickets < size then
		return nil
	end
	-- Reserve before removing: if reserving fails, the tickets reappear after INVISIBLE_SECONDS.
	local reserved, code = pcall(function()
		return TeleportService:ReserveServerAsync(arenaPlaceId)
	end)
	if not reserved then
		return nil
	end
	local removed = pcall(function()
		queue:RemoveAsync(readId)
	end)
	if not removed then
		return nil
	end
	local userIds: { number } = {}
	for _, ticket in tickets do
		table.insert(userIds, ticket.userId)
	end
	local published = pcall(function()
		MessagingService:PublishAsync(MATCH_TOPIC, { placeId = arenaPlaceId, code = code, users = userIds })
	end)
	if not published then
		warn("match publish failed; these players can requeue when their tickets expire")
	end
	return userIds
end

-- Every lobby (the matcher's included) teleports the matched players it hosts.
local function onMatch(message: { Data: any })
	local data = message.Data
	local mine: { Player } = {}
	for _, userId in data.users do
		local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(userId)
		if player then
			queuedUntil[userId] = nil
			table.insert(mine, player)
		end
	end
	if #mine == 0 then
		return
	end
	local options = Instance.new("TeleportOptions")
	options.ReservedServerAccessCode = data.code
	local ok, err = pcall(function()
		TeleportService:TeleportAsync(data.placeId, mine, options)
	end)
	if not ok then
		warn("arena teleport failed:", err)
	end
end

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player)
	queuedUntil[player.UserId] = nil
end)

task.spawn(function()
	for attempt = 1, 5 do
		local ok = pcall(function()
			MessagingService:SubscribeAsync(MATCH_TOPIC, onMatch)
		end)
		if ok then
			return
		end
		task.wait(2 ^ attempt)
	end
	warn("matchmaker could not subscribe; this lobby cannot receive matches")
end)

return Matchmaker
```

Run `tryMatch` from a loop every 2-3 seconds in each lobby server; `allOrNothing` reads mean two matchers never split one group.

- A ticket from a player who left stays until its TTL and can end up in a match; have the arena start with whoever arrives within 20 seconds, and requeue the rest from their lobbies.
- Reserving before `RemoveAsync` means a failed reservation loses nobody: the hidden tickets become readable again.
- Keep messages tiny (user ids and a code); a MessagingService message is limited to 1 KB.

answer:
The admin's server filters the text, then publishes it on one topic; every server subscribes to that topic at startup and forwards the message to its own players through a RemoteEvent. Publishing and subscribing both go in `pcall`, and the receiving side validates the payload because anything on a topic is just data.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.Announcements
local MessagingService = game:GetService("MessagingService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local TextService = game:GetService("TextService")

local TOPIC = "Announcements"
local MAX_LENGTH = 200

local banner = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
banner.Name = "AnnouncementBanner"
banner.Parent = ReplicatedStorage

local Announcements = {}

local function onMessage(message: { Data: any, Sent: number })
	local data = message.Data
	if type(data) ~= "table" or type(data.text) ~= "string" or #data.text > MAX_LENGTH then
		return
	end
	banner:FireAllClients(data.text, if type(data.from) == "string" then data.from else "Staff")
end

-- Call only after your admin check. Returns false if filtering or publishing failed.
function Announcements.send(admin: Player, text: string): boolean
	if #text == 0 or #text > MAX_LENGTH then
		return false
	end
	local ok, filtered = pcall(function()
		return TextService:FilterStringAsync(text, admin.UserId):GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync()
	end)
	if not ok or type(filtered) ~= "string" then
		return false
	end
	local published = pcall(function()
		MessagingService:PublishAsync(TOPIC, { text = filtered, from = admin.Name })
	end)
	return published
end

local subscribed, err = pcall(function()
	return MessagingService:SubscribeAsync(TOPIC, onMessage)
end)
if not subscribed then
	warn("announcements unavailable in this server:", err)
end

return Announcements
```

- The publishing server also receives its own message through the subscription, so there is one code path for showing the banner everywhere.
- Filter once before publishing, with the admin as the author; receivers then show the already-filtered broadcast text.
- Delivery is best effort and usually under a second; for something that must reach every server (a forced update), combine it with a DataStore or MemoryStore flag that new servers read at startup.
request: I want admins to type an announcement in one server and have it show as a banner in every server of my game. How do I do this with MessagingService?

answer:
Publish a start time instead of a command: an event id plus `startsAt` in Unix seconds from `workspace:GetServerTimeNow()`, which has sub-second precision (`os.time()` is whole seconds, so two servers could fire up to a second apart). Each server schedules the event with `task.delay(startsAt - now)`, so small delivery differences do not matter. Remember ids already scheduled so a repeated message is ignored, and drop messages whose start time is long past.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.GlobalEvents
local MessagingService = game:GetService("MessagingService")
local HttpService = game:GetService("HttpService")

local TOPIC = "GlobalEvents"
local LATE_TOLERANCE = 10 -- seconds; a message older than this is ignored

export type Handler = (eventName: string) -> ()

local GlobalEvents = {}
local handlers: { [string]: Handler } = {}
local scheduled: { [string]: boolean } = {}

function GlobalEvents.on(eventName: string, handler: Handler)
	handlers[eventName] = handler
end

local function onMessage(message: { Data: any })
	local data = message.Data
	if type(data) ~= "table" or type(data.id) ~= "string" or type(data.name) ~= "string" or type(data.startsAt) ~= "number" then
		return
	end
	local handler = handlers[data.name]
	if handler == nil or scheduled[data.id] then
		return
	end
	local delay = data.startsAt - workspace:GetServerTimeNow()
	if delay < -LATE_TOLERANCE then
		return
	end
	scheduled[data.id] = true
	task.delay(math.max(0, delay), handler, data.name)
end

-- Schedules eventName in every server `leadSeconds` from now.
function GlobalEvents.schedule(eventName: string, leadSeconds: number): boolean
	local payload = { id = HttpService:GenerateGUID(false), name = eventName, startsAt = workspace:GetServerTimeNow() + leadSeconds }
	local ok = pcall(function()
		MessagingService:PublishAsync(TOPIC, payload)
	end)
	return ok
end

task.spawn(function()
	for attempt = 1, 5 do
		local ok = pcall(function()
			MessagingService:SubscribeAsync(TOPIC, onMessage)
		end)
		if ok then
			return
		end
		task.wait(2 ^ attempt)
	end
	warn("GlobalEvents could not subscribe; this server will miss global events")
end)

return GlobalEvents
```

Usage: `GlobalEvents.on("MeteorShower", startMeteors)` in every server, and an admin command calls `GlobalEvents.schedule("MeteorShower", 60)`.

- Server clocks are synchronised closely enough for gameplay events; a 60-second lead also covers slow message delivery.
- Servers that start after the message was sent never see it; if late joiners matter, also store the next event time in a MemoryStore key that new servers read on startup.
- Show a countdown to players using the same `startsAt` and `workspace:GetServerTimeNow()` on the client, which estimates server time, so every UI agrees.

answer:
A message must stay under 1 KB once encoded, topic names are limited to 80 characters, and each server has a publish budget per minute that grows with its player count (check the current numbers on the MessagingService limits page). A small helper can check size and topic length up front, keep a per-server token bucket that stays below that budget, and report why a publish was refused instead of erroring.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.SafePublish
local HttpService = game:GetService("HttpService")
local MessagingService = game:GetService("MessagingService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

export type Result = "ok" | "too large" | "bad topic" | "rate limited" | "error"

local MAX_BYTES = 1000 -- a little under the 1 KB limit for safety
local MAX_TOPIC = 80

local SafePublish = {}

local DOCUMENTED_BASE = 150 -- per-minute limit from the MessagingService limits page when this was written
local DOCUMENTED_PER_PLAYER = 60
local SAFETY = 0.8 -- stay under the limit so retries and other scripts have headroom

local tokens = math.floor(SAFETY * DOCUMENTED_BASE)
local updated = os.clock()

local function budgetPerMinute(): number
	return math.floor(SAFETY * (DOCUMENTED_BASE + DOCUMENTED_PER_PLAYER * #Players:GetPlayers()))
end

local function takeToken(): boolean
	local now = os.clock()
	local capacity = budgetPerMinute()
	tokens = math.min(capacity, tokens + (now - updated) * capacity / 60)
	updated = now
	if tokens < 1 then
		return false
	end
	tokens -= 1
	return true
end

function SafePublish.size(message: any): number
	local ok, encoded = pcall(HttpService.JSONEncode, HttpService, message)
	return if ok then #encoded else math.huge
end

function SafePublish.publish(topic: string, message: any): Result
	if #topic == 0 or #topic > MAX_TOPIC then
		return "bad topic"
	end
	if SafePublish.size(message) > MAX_BYTES then
		return "too large"
	end
	if not takeToken() then
		return "rate limited"
	end
	local ok = pcall(function()
		MessagingService:PublishAsync(topic, message)
	end)
	return if ok then "ok" else "error"
end

return SafePublish
```

- Send ids, not objects: a trade feed message like `{ s = sellerId, i = "ruby_blade", p = 500 }` is a few dozen bytes; receivers look up names and details themselves.
- When "rate limited" comes back, batch: collect events for a second or two and publish one message with a short list, which also cuts receive costs in every server.
- A message that `JSONEncode` cannot encode makes `size` return `math.huge`, so it is refused before it reaches the service; re-check the two documented numbers against the limits page, since they can change.
request: My cross-server trade feed sometimes stops working and I see MessagingService errors about size and request limits. What are the limits I need to respect, and can you write a publish helper that checks them before sending?

answer:
Yes. Each server can hold only a limited number of subscriptions (it scales with player count), and every `SubscribeAsync` returns a connection that stays alive until you `Disconnect` it. Keep the connection per player, disconnect it on `PlayerRemoving`, and check that the subscription actually succeeded.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.Whispers
local MessagingService = game:GetService("MessagingService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local whisper = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
whisper.Name = "Whisper"
whisper.Parent = ReplicatedStorage

local subscriptions: { [Player]: RBXScriptConnection } = {}

local Whispers = {}

local function topicFor(userId: number): string
	return "whisper_" .. userId
end

local function subscribe(player: Player)
	local ok, connection = pcall(function()
		return MessagingService:SubscribeAsync(topicFor(player.UserId), function(message: { Data: any })
			local data = message.Data
			if type(data) == "table" and type(data.from) == "string" and type(data.text) == "string" then
				whisper:FireClient(player, data.from, data.text)
			end
		end)
	end)
	if not ok then
		warn("whisper subscription failed for", player.UserId)
		return
	end
	if player.Parent == nil then
		connection:Disconnect() -- left while we were subscribing
		return
	end
	subscriptions[player] = connection
end

local function unsubscribe(player: Player)
	local connection = subscriptions[player]
	if connection then
		subscriptions[player] = nil
		connection:Disconnect()
	end
end

-- text must already be filtered for the recipient; fromName is the sender's name.
function Whispers.send(toUserId: number, fromName: string, text: string): boolean
	return (pcall(function()
		MessagingService:PublishAsync(topicFor(toUserId), { from = fromName, text = text })
	end))
end

function Whispers.count(): number
	local n = 0
	for _ in subscriptions do
		n += 1
	end
	return n
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(subscribe)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(unsubscribe)
for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
	task.spawn(subscribe, player)
end

return Whispers
```

- Without `unsubscribe`, a busy server accumulates one dead subscription per player who ever joined and eventually hits the limit, which is exactly the failure you saw.
- The `player.Parent == nil` check covers a player who leaves while `SubscribeAsync` is still yielding.
- Whisper text between users must be filtered for the recipient (`GetChatForUserAsync` or TextChatService); this example assumes the caller did that.

answer:
Publish one message with the restart time; each server shows the countdown to its players and, when the time arrives, kicks them with the update message, which runs `PlayerRemoving` saves. Guard against duplicate or late messages, and let a second message with `cancel = true` call it off.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.RestartNotice
local MessagingService = game:GetService("MessagingService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local TOPIC = "RestartNotice"
local KICK_MESSAGE = "The game is updating. Rejoin in a minute for the new version!"

local notice = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
notice.Name = "RestartNotice"
notice.Parent = ReplicatedStorage

local RestartNotice = {}
local pendingAt: number? = nil
local restarting = false

local function restartNow(at: number)
	if pendingAt ~= at then
		return -- cancelled or replaced by a newer notice
	end
	restarting = true -- this old server can still receive joins until it closes; send those players off too
	for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
		player:Kick(KICK_MESSAGE)
	end
end

local function onMessage(message: { Data: any })
	local data = message.Data
	if type(data) ~= "table" or type(data.at) ~= "number" then
		return
	end
	if data.cancel == true then
		pendingAt = nil
		notice:FireAllClients(nil)
		return
	end
	if pendingAt == data.at or data.at < os.time() - 5 then
		return
	end
	pendingAt = data.at
	notice:FireAllClients(data.at) -- clients count down to this Unix time
	task.delay(math.max(0, data.at - os.time()), restartNow, data.at)
end

function RestartNotice.announce(minutes: number): boolean
	return (pcall(function()
		MessagingService:PublishAsync(TOPIC, { at = os.time() + math.floor(minutes * 60) })
	end))
end

function RestartNotice.cancel(): boolean
	return (pcall(function()
		MessagingService:PublishAsync(TOPIC, { at = os.time(), cancel = true })
	end))
end

-- Players who join during the countdown see it too; players who join after the restart are kicked.
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player: Player)
	if restarting then
		player:Kick(KICK_MESSAGE)
	elseif pendingAt then
		notice:FireClient(player, pendingAt)
	end
end)
for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
	if pendingAt then
		notice:FireClient(player, pendingAt)
	end
end

task.spawn(function()
	for attempt = 1, 5 do
		local ok = pcall(function()
			MessagingService:SubscribeAsync(TOPIC, onMessage)
		end)
		if ok then
			return
		end
		task.wait(2 ^ attempt)
	end
	warn("RestartNotice could not subscribe; this server will not get restart notices")
end)

return RestartNotice
```

- Kicking runs each player's `PlayerRemoving` save while the server is still healthy, instead of relying on the 30-second `BindToClose` window during a forced shutdown.
- Publish the update first so new servers run the new version; players who rejoin after the kick land in fresh servers.
- Sending the Unix time (not "5 minutes") keeps every server's countdown identical despite delivery delays.

answer:
Give each player a mailbox key. Senders append to it with `UpdateAsync` (capped in size), and the owner takes everything out with one `UpdateAsync` that returns the mail and empties the box in the same atomic step. Each gift carries a unique id so the receiving code can ignore anything it has already granted.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.Mailbox
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local HttpService = game:GetService("HttpService")

local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("Mailboxes")
local MAX_MAIL = 50

export type Gift = { id: string, from: number, itemId: string, sentAt: number }

local Mailbox = {}

local function keyFor(userId: number): string
	return "mail_" .. userId
end

-- itemId must already be validated and removed from the sender's inventory by the caller.
function Mailbox.send(fromUserId: number, toUserId: number, itemId: string): (boolean, string?)
	local gift: Gift = { id = HttpService:GenerateGUID(false), from = fromUserId, itemId = itemId, sentAt = os.time() }
	local full = false
	local ok = pcall(function()
		store:UpdateAsync(keyFor(toUserId), function(box: { Gift }?): { Gift }?
			local mail = box or {}
			if #mail >= MAX_MAIL then
				full = true
				return nil
			end
			full = false
			table.insert(mail, gift)
			return mail
		end)
	end)
	if not ok then
		return false, "error"
	elseif full then
		return false, "full"
	end
	return true, nil
end

-- Takes every gift out of the mailbox atomically. Returns nil when the read failed (try again later).
function Mailbox.takeAll(userId: number): { Gift }?
	local taken: { Gift } = {}
	local ok = pcall(function()
		store:UpdateAsync(keyFor(userId), function(box: { Gift }?): { Gift }?
			taken = box or {}
			if #taken == 0 then
				return nil
			end
			return {}
		end)
	end)
	return if ok then taken else nil
end

return Mailbox
```

- If `send` fails, give the item back to the sender; the mailbox write is the moment ownership transfers.
- Call `takeAll` after the player's profile has loaded and save the profile soon after granting; store granted gift ids in the profile for a while if you want a crash between take and save to be detectable.
- The cap keeps one key far from the 4 MB limit and stops a spammer from filling someone's box with junk.

answer:
Submit with `UpdateAsync` on the OrderedDataStore and return `nil` when the new score is not higher, which cancels the write. Read the top N by walking the pages until you have enough rows or the pages run out, with every call in `pcall`.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.HighScores
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")

local board = DataStoreService:GetOrderedDataStore("HighScores")
local PAGE_SIZE = 100

export type Row = { userId: number, score: number, rank: number }

local HighScores = {}

-- Ordered stores hold integers only; keep the best score per player.
function HighScores.submit(userId: number, score: number): boolean
	if score ~= score or score == math.huge or score < 0 then
		return false
	end
	local value = math.floor(score)
	local ok = pcall(function()
		board:UpdateAsync(tostring(userId), function(old: number?): number?
			if old and old >= value then
				return nil -- not a new best: cancel the write
			end
			return value
		end)
	end)
	return ok
end

function HighScores.top(count: number): { Row }
	local rows: { Row } = {}
	local ok, pages = pcall(function()
		return board:GetSortedAsync(false, math.min(count, PAGE_SIZE))
	end)
	if not ok then
		return rows
	end
	while #rows < count do
		for _, entry in pages:GetCurrentPage() do
			local userId = tonumber(entry.key)
			if userId and #rows < count then
				table.insert(rows, { userId = userId, score = entry.value, rank = #rows + 1 })
			end
		end
		if pages.IsFinished or #rows >= count then
			break
		end
		local advanced = pcall(function()
			pages:AdvanceToNextPageAsync()
		end)
		if not advanced then
			break -- show what we have rather than nothing
		end
	end
	return rows
end

return HighScores
```

- Refresh the board on a timer (every 60-120 seconds) and cache the rows; every viewer reading the store directly would burn the sorted-read budget.
- Keys are plain UserIds, so `tonumber(entry.key)` recovers the player; resolve names with `Players:GetNameFromUserIdAsync` in a `pcall` and cache them.
- For a weekly board, put the week number in the store name (`"HighScores_W" .. week`) and the old weeks simply stop being read.

answer:
Queue each change as a transform function per key. The first change writes right away; changes arriving inside the 6-second window wait and are applied together, in order, inside one `UpdateAsync`. A failed write puts its batch back at the front of the queue and tries again after the gap.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.KeyWriteQueue
export type Transform = (current: any) -> any
export type Queue = {
	update: (key: string, transform: Transform) -> (),
	pending: (key: string) -> number,
	flushAll: () -> (),
}

type KeyState = { transforms: { Transform }, lastWrite: number, scheduled: boolean }

local MIN_GAP = 6 -- seconds between writes to the same key

local KeyWriteQueue = {}

function KeyWriteQueue.new(store: DataStore): Queue
	local states: { [string]: KeyState } = {}
	local schedule: (key: string) -> ()

	local function flush(key: string)
		local state = states[key]
		state.scheduled = false
		if #state.transforms == 0 then
			return -- already written by flushAll
		end
		local batch = state.transforms
		state.transforms = {}
		state.lastWrite = os.clock()
		local ok = pcall(function()
			store:UpdateAsync(key, function(current: any): any
				local value = current
				for _, transform in batch do
					value = transform(value)
				end
				return value
			end)
		end)
		if not ok then
			local merged = batch
			for _, transform in state.transforms do
				table.insert(merged, transform)
			end
			state.transforms = merged
		end
		if #state.transforms > 0 then
			schedule(key)
		end
	end

	schedule = function(key: string)
		local state = states[key]
		if state.scheduled then
			return
		end
		state.scheduled = true
		task.delay(math.max(0, state.lastWrite + MIN_GAP - os.clock()), flush, key)
	end

	local function update(key: string, transform: Transform)
		local state = states[key]
		if state == nil then
			state = { transforms = {}, lastWrite = -math.huge, scheduled = false }
			states[key] = state
		end
		table.insert(state.transforms, transform)
		schedule(key)
	end

	local function pending(key: string): number
		local state = states[key]
		return if state then #state.transforms else 0
	end

	-- For BindToClose: write every pending batch now instead of waiting for its gap.
	local function flushAll()
		local keys: { string } = {}
		for key, state in states do
			if #state.transforms > 0 then
				table.insert(keys, key)
			end
		end
		for _, key in keys do
			flush(key)
		end
	end

	return { update = update, pending = pending, flushAll = flushAll }
end

return KeyWriteQueue
```

Usage: `queue.update("guild_" .. guildId, function(bank) bank = bank or { gold = 0 }; bank.gold += amount; return bank end)`.

- Transforms receive the freshest stored value each time, so deposits from other servers are never overwritten.
- Each transform must return the new value; returning `nil` from the whole chain cancels that write.
- Call `game:BindToClose(queue.flushAll)` so deposits still waiting for their gap are written before the server closes.

answer:
Put a small read-through cache in front of the store: keep each loaded profile summary with a timestamp, serve it from memory while it is fresh, and share one in-flight request between callers asking for the same user at once. Only a public summary is cached and returned, never the whole save.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.ProfileViews
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")

local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("PlayerData")
local TTL = 120
local MAX_ENTRIES = 500

export type Summary = { level: number, wins: number, title: string }
type Entry = { summary: Summary?, fetched: number }

local cache: { [number]: Entry } = {}
local count = 0
local inFlight: { [number]: { thread } } = {}

local ProfileViews = {}

local function summarize(saved: any): Summary?
	if type(saved) ~= "table" then
		return nil
	end
	return {
		level = tonumber(saved.level) or 1,
		wins = tonumber(saved.wins) or 0,
		title = if type(saved.title) == "string" then saved.title else "",
	}
end

local function remember(userId: number, summary: Summary?)
	if cache[userId] == nil then
		if count >= MAX_ENTRIES then
			table.clear(cache) -- simple and bounded; a lobby rarely needs more than a few hundred
			count = 0
		end
		count += 1
	end
	cache[userId] = { summary = summary, fetched = os.clock() }
end

-- Returns the summary (nil for players with no save) and whether the lookup succeeded.
function ProfileViews.get(userId: number): (Summary?, boolean)
	local entry = cache[userId]
	if entry and os.clock() - entry.fetched < TTL then
		return entry.summary, true
	end
	local waiting = inFlight[userId]
	if waiting then
		table.insert(waiting, coroutine.running())
		return coroutine.yield()
	end
	inFlight[userId] = {}
	local ok, saved = pcall(function()
		return store:GetAsync("player_" .. userId)
	end)
	local summary = if ok then summarize(saved) else nil
	if ok then
		remember(userId, summary)
	end
	local waiters = inFlight[userId]
	inFlight[userId] = nil
	for _, thread in waiters do
		task.spawn(thread, summary, ok)
	end
	return summary, ok
end

return ProfileViews
```

- Failures are not cached, so a brief outage does not show "no profile" for two minutes.
- Callers who arrive while a read is running wait for that read instead of starting their own, which is what stops a spam-clicked button from multiplying requests.
- For players in the same server, read the live session data instead; the cache is for everyone else, and two minutes of staleness is fine for a profile card.
request: My lobby has a "view profile" button that shows any player's stats, including offline friends. Each click does a GetAsync and people spam it, burning my read budget. How can I cache these reads?

answer:
Reconcile the loaded data against a template recursively: copy in any key that is missing, recurse into nested tables, and replace values whose type no longer matches the template. Arrays are treated as single values so a player's list is never merged with the default list.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.Reconcile
local Reconcile = {}

local function copy(value: any): any
	if type(value) ~= "table" then
		return value
	end
	local out = {}
	for k, v in value do
		out[k] = copy(v)
	end
	return out
end

local function isArray(t: { [any]: any }): boolean
	return next(t) == nil or t[1] ~= nil
end

-- Mutates data in place. Returns the paths it fixed, which is useful for logging.
function Reconcile.apply(data: { [string]: any }, template: { [string]: any }, path: string?): { string }
	local fixed: { string } = {}
	local prefix = if path then path .. "." else ""
	for key, default in template do
		local current = data[key]
		local here = prefix .. key
		if current == nil or type(current) ~= type(default) then
			data[key] = copy(default)
			table.insert(fixed, here)
		elseif type(default) == "table" and not isArray(default) then
			for _, nested in Reconcile.apply(current, default, here) do
				table.insert(fixed, nested)
			end
		end
	end
	return fixed
end

return Reconcile
```

One server module owns every cooldown: a config table of action names to seconds, and a per-player table of when each action was last used. The handler asks `try(player, action)` before doing anything; unknown actions are refused, and the remaining time comes back so the client can sync its UI.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.Cooldowns
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

export type Cooldowns = {
	try: (player: Player, action: string) -> (boolean, number),
	reset: (player: Player, action: string) -> (),
}

local Cooldowns = {}

function Cooldowns.new(durations: { [string]: number }): Cooldowns
	local used: { [Player]: { [string]: number } } = {}

	Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player)
		used[player] = nil
	end)

	-- Returns true and starts the cooldown, or false and the seconds left (math.huge for unknown actions).
	local function try(player: Player, action: string): (boolean, number)
		local duration = durations[action]
		if duration == nil then
			return false, math.huge
		end
		local mine = used[player]
		if mine == nil then
			mine = {}
			used[player] = mine
		end
		local now = os.clock()
		local last = mine[action]
		if last and now - last < duration then
			return false, duration - (now - last)
		end
		mine[action] = now
		return true, 0
	end

	-- For effects such as a cooldown-reset power-up; still decided by server code only.
	local function reset(player: Player, action: string)
		local mine = used[player]
		if mine then
			mine[action] = nil
		end
	end

	return { try = try, reset = reset }
end

return Cooldowns
```

Name checks break when you rename and are easy to get wrong; check the sender's UserId against a server-side allowlist instead, on every request, because anyone can fire the remote even if the panel is hidden. Then parse the command, look it up in a server table, validate every argument and log what was done.

```lua
--!strict
-- Script: ServerScriptService.AdminCommands
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

-- Real UserIds only; names can change.
local ADMIN_IDS: { [number]: boolean } = {}
-- In a group-owned experience game.CreatorId is the group's id, which could match some unrelated user.
if game.CreatorType == Enum.CreatorType.User then
	ADMIN_IDS[game.CreatorId] = true
end
local MAX_COINS = 100_000

local adminCommand = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
adminCommand.Name = "AdminCommand"
adminCommand.Parent = ReplicatedStorage

local function findPlayer(name: unknown): Player?
	if type(name) ~= "string" or #name > 20 then
		return nil
	end
	local wanted = string.lower(name)
	for _, candidate in Players:GetPlayers() do
		if string.lower(candidate.Name) == wanted then
			return candidate
		end
	end
	return nil
end

type Command = (admin: Player, target: Player, arg: unknown) -> boolean

local COMMANDS: { [string]: Command } = {
	kick = function(_admin: Player, target: Player, _arg: unknown): boolean
		if ADMIN_IDS[target.UserId] then
			return false -- admins cannot kick each other from the panel
		end
		target:Kick("Removed by a moderator.")
		return true
	end,
	coins = function(_admin: Player, target: Player, arg: unknown): boolean
		if type(arg) ~= "number" or arg % 1 ~= 0 or arg < 1 or arg > MAX_COINS then
			return false
		end
		local stored: unknown = target:GetAttribute("Coins")
		local current = if type(stored) == "number" then stored else 0
		target:SetAttribute("Coins", current + arg)
		return true
	end,
}

local function onCommand(admin: Player, nameArg: unknown, targetArg: unknown, extra: unknown)
	if not ADMIN_IDS[admin.UserId] then
		print("[admin] refused command from non-admin", admin.UserId)
		return
	end
	if type(nameArg) ~= "string" then
		return
	end
	local command = COMMANDS[nameArg]
	local target = findPlayer(targetArg)
	if command == nil or target == nil then
		return
	end
	local done = command(admin, target, extra)
	local adminId: number, targetId: number = admin.UserId, target.UserId
	print(string.format("[admin] %d ran %s on %d: %s", adminId, nameArg, targetId, tostring(done)))
end

adminCommand.OnServerEvent:Connect(onCommand)
```

- Hide the panel for non-admins as a convenience only; the `ADMIN_IDS` check on the server is the actual protection.
- `COMMANDS[nameArg]` is a plain table lookup on a table with no metatable, so strings like "__index" find nothing.
- For group-owned games, swap the table check for `player:GetRankInGroup(game.CreatorId) >= rank` (in `pcall`, cached per player).

answer:
Each validator takes the raw `unknown` argument and returns the typed value when it passes, or `nil`. Handlers then read like a list of requirements, and NaN, infinity, invalid UTF-8 and wrong Instance classes are rejected in one place.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.Check
local Check = {}

function Check.finite(value: unknown): number?
	if type(value) == "number" and value == value and value ~= math.huge and value ~= -math.huge then
		return value
	end
	return nil
end

function Check.number(value: unknown, min: number, max: number): number?
	local n = Check.finite(value)
	if n and n >= min and n <= max then
		return n
	end
	return nil
end

function Check.integer(value: unknown, min: number, max: number): number?
	local n = Check.number(value, min, max)
	if n and n % 1 == 0 then
		return n
	end
	return nil
end

function Check.text(value: unknown, maxLength: number): string?
	if type(value) == "string" and #value <= maxLength and utf8.len(value) ~= nil then
		return value
	end
	return nil
end

-- allowed is a server-owned set such as { Red = true, Blue = true }.
function Check.option(value: unknown, allowed: { [string]: boolean }): string?
	if type(value) == "string" and allowed[value] == true then
		return value
	end
	return nil
end

function Check.vector3(value: unknown, maxMagnitude: number): Vector3?
	local kind = typeof(value)
	if kind ~= "Vector3" then
		return nil
	end
	local v = value :: any
	if Check.finite(v.X) and Check.finite(v.Y) and Check.finite(v.Z) and v.Magnitude <= maxMagnitude then
		return v
	end
	return nil
end

function Check.instance(value: unknown, className: string): Instance?
	local kind = typeof(value)
	if kind == "Instance" and (value :: any):IsA(className) then
		return value :: any
	end
	return nil
end

return Check
```

The client sends an emote name, never an animation id. The server keeps the emote list: each name maps to an Animation object stored in ServerStorage and an optional game pass. The server checks the name, ownership (cached), the cooldown and a living character, then plays the animation through the character's Animator.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.Emotes
local MarketplaceService = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

export type EmoteDef = { animation: Animation, passId: number? }
export type Result = "ok" | "unknown" | "locked" | "cooldown" | "no character"

local COOLDOWN = 1.5

local Emotes = {}

function Emotes.new(defs: { [string]: EmoteDef }): (player: Player, name: unknown) -> Result
	local lastPlayed: { [Player]: number } = {}
	local tracks: { [Player]: AnimationTrack } = {}
	local ownsCache: { [Player]: { [number]: boolean } } = {}

	Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player)
		lastPlayed[player], tracks[player], ownsCache[player] = nil, nil, nil
	end)

	-- A purchase made in this session must unlock the emote now, not after a rejoin.
	MarketplaceService.PromptGamePassPurchaseFinished:Connect(function(player: Player, passId: number, purchased: boolean)
		local cache = ownsCache[player]
		if purchased and cache then
			cache[passId] = true
		end
	end)

	local function owns(player: Player, passId: number): boolean
		local cache = ownsCache[player] or {}
		ownsCache[player] = cache
		if cache[passId] == nil then
			local ok, result = pcall(function()
				return MarketplaceService:UserOwnsGamePassAsync(player.UserId, passId)
			end)
			if not ok then
				return false -- do not cache failures; try again next time
			end
			cache[passId] = result
		end
		return cache[passId]
	end

	return function(player: Player, name: unknown): Result
		local def = if type(name) == "string" then defs[name] else nil
		if def == nil then
			return "unknown"
		end
		if def.passId and not owns(player, def.passId) then
			return "locked"
		end
		local now = os.clock()
		local last = lastPlayed[player]
		if last and now - last < COOLDOWN then
			return "cooldown"
		end
		local character = player.Character
		local humanoid: Humanoid? = if character then character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid") else nil
		local animator: Animator? = if humanoid then humanoid:FindFirstChildOfClass("Animator") else nil
		if humanoid == nil or animator == nil or humanoid.Health <= 0 then
			return "no character"
		end
		lastPlayed[player] = now
		local previous = tracks[player]
		if previous then
			previous:Stop()
			previous:Destroy()
		end
		local track = animator:LoadAnimation(def.animation)
		tracks[player] = track
		track:Play()
		return "ok"
	end
end

return Emotes
```

- Animations played through the character's Animator on the server replicate to everyone, so the client never needs to send an id at all.
- Each new emote stops and destroys the previous track, so spamming emotes does not pile up AnimationTracks on the Animator.
- Keep the Animation objects in ServerStorage with their ids set in Studio; the wheel UI only needs names and icons.

Yes: any client can fire `StageDone` with any amount, as often as it likes. Remove the remote entirely. The server can see the touch itself: each stage-end part has a `Stage` number and a `Reward` attribute, and the server pays a player once per stage, only in order, only for a living character.

```lua
--!strict
-- Script: ServerScriptService.StageRewards
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local reachedStage: { [Player]: number } = {}

local function setupStats(player: Player)
	local stats = Instance.new("Folder")
	stats.Name = "leaderstats"
	local cash = Instance.new("IntValue")
	cash.Name = "Cash"
	cash.Parent = stats
	stats.Parent = player
	reachedStage[player] = 0
end

local function payStage(stagePart: BasePart, hit: BasePart)
	local character = hit.Parent
	local player = character and Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(character)
	if player == nil then
		return
	end
	local humanoid: Humanoid? = (character :: Model):FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	local stage = stagePart:GetAttribute("Stage")
	local reward = stagePart:GetAttribute("Reward")
	if humanoid == nil or humanoid.Health <= 0 or type(stage) ~= "number" or type(reward) ~= "number" then
		return
	end
	-- the stage table is the debounce: each stage pays once, and only right after the previous one
	if reachedStage[player] ~= stage - 1 then
		return
	end
	reachedStage[player] = stage
	local stats: Instance? = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
	local cash: Instance? = if stats then stats:FindFirstChild("Cash") else nil
	if cash and cash:IsA("IntValue") then
		(cash :: IntValue).Value += reward
	end
end

local function stageHandler(stagePart: BasePart): (BasePart) -> ()
	return function(hit: BasePart)
		payStage(stagePart, hit)
	end
end

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player)
	reachedStage[player] = nil
end)
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(setupStats)
for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
	setupStats(player)
end
for _, stagePart in CollectionService:GetTagged("StageEnd") do
	stagePart.Touched:Connect(stageHandler(stagePart))
end
```

- `Reward` and `Stage` are attributes you set in Studio on the parts tagged `StageEnd`; clients cannot change server-side attributes.
- Requiring stage N-1 before N stops teleport exploits from collecting the last stage's reward directly.
- Save `reachedStage` with the player's data if stages should stay completed between sessions.

Validate the arguments like any remote, rate-limit per player, keep the handler fast (no long yields), and never let it throw: wrap the work in `pcall` and always return a plain table with an `ok` flag, so errors are not shown to clients and the UI has one shape to handle. Return only data (strings, numbers, small tables), never Instances the client should not reach.

```lua
--!strict
-- Script: ServerScriptService.ShopQuery
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

type Entry = { id: string, name: string, price: number }
export type Response = { ok: boolean, reason: string?, items: { Entry }?, pages: number? }

local CATALOG: { Entry } = {
	{ id = "wood_sword", name = "Wood Sword", price = 50 },
	{ id = "iron_sword", name = "Iron Sword", price = 250 },
	{ id = "bow", name = "Bow", price = 180 },
	{ id = "shield", name = "Shield", price = 120 },
	{ id = "potion", name = "Potion", price = 25 },
}
local PAGE_SIZE = 2
local MIN_INTERVAL = 0.2

local getShopPage = Instance.new("RemoteFunction")
getShopPage.Name = "GetShopPage"
getShopPage.Parent = ReplicatedStorage

local lastCall: { [Player]: number } = {}

local function buildPage(page: number): Response
	local pages = math.ceil(#CATALOG / PAGE_SIZE)
	if page > pages then
		return { ok = false, reason = "no such page" }
	end
	local items: { Entry } = {}
	for i = (page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE + 1, math.min(#CATALOG, page * PAGE_SIZE) do
		local entry = CATALOG[i]
		table.insert(items, { id = entry.id, name = entry.name, price = entry.price })
	end
	return { ok = true, items = items, pages = pages }
end

local function onInvoke(player: Player, pageArg: unknown): Response
	local now = os.clock()
	local last = lastCall[player]
	if last and now - last < MIN_INTERVAL then
		return { ok = false, reason = "slow down" }
	end
	lastCall[player] = now
	if type(pageArg) ~= "number" or pageArg % 1 ~= 0 or pageArg < 1 or pageArg > 1000 then
		return { ok = false, reason = "bad page" }
	end
	local ok, response = pcall(buildPage, pageArg)
	if not ok then
		warn("shop page failed:", response)
		return { ok = false, reason = "server error" }
	end
	return response
end

getShopPage.OnServerInvoke = onInvoke
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player)
	lastCall[player] = nil
end)
```

Client side, the call itself goes in `pcall` too (the server may be shutting down or the remote may be gone):

```lua
--!strict
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local getShopPage = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("GetShopPage") :: RemoteFunction

local function fetchPage(page: number): { [string]: any }?
	local ok, response = pcall(function()
		return getShopPage:InvokeServer(page)
	end)
	if ok and type(response) == "table" and response.ok then
		return response
	end
	return nil
end

return fetchPage
```

- Copying entries into new tables means a later change to the response cannot reach the catalogue, and the client gets exactly the fields you chose.
- Assign `OnServerInvoke` exactly once; setting it again elsewhere silently replaces the first handler.
- Purchases still go through their own validated remote; prices shown here are for display, the buy handler reads the catalogue again.

answer:
Do not accept a CFrame at all. The client sends intent in grid terms (item id, cell x, cell z, rotation step 0-3), and the server checks the item exists, the cell is inside the player's plot, the cells are free in a server-side occupancy map, then builds the CFrame itself from the plot origin.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.PlotGrid
export type ItemDef = { width: number, depth: number }
export type Plot = {
	ownerId: number,
	origin: CFrame,       -- corner of the plot, Y at floor level
	cellsX: number,
	cellsZ: number,
	occupied: { [string]: boolean },
}

local CELL = 4 -- studs

local PlotGrid = {}

local function cellKey(x: number, z: number): string
	return x .. ":" .. z
end

local function isInt(n: unknown, lo: number, hi: number): boolean
	return type(n) == "number" and n % 1 == 0 and n >= lo and n <= hi
end

-- Returns the world CFrame for the placement, or nil and a reason. Marks the cells as used on success.
function PlotGrid.place(plot: Plot, userId: number, def: ItemDef?, xArg: unknown, zArg: unknown, rotArg: unknown): (CFrame?, string?)
	if plot.ownerId ~= userId then
		return nil, "not your plot"
	end
	if def == nil or not isInt(rotArg, 0, 3) then
		return nil, "bad request"
	end
	local rotation = rotArg :: number
	local width = if rotation % 2 == 0 then def.width else def.depth
	local depth = if rotation % 2 == 0 then def.depth else def.width
	if not isInt(xArg, 0, plot.cellsX - width) or not isInt(zArg, 0, plot.cellsZ - depth) then
		return nil, "out of bounds"
	end
	local x, z = xArg :: number, zArg :: number
	for dx = 0, width - 1 do
		for dz = 0, depth - 1 do
			if plot.occupied[cellKey(x + dx, z + dz)] then
				return nil, "blocked"
			end
		end
	end
	for dx = 0, width - 1 do
		for dz = 0, depth - 1 do
			plot.occupied[cellKey(x + dx, z + dz)] = true
		end
	end
	local center = Vector3.new((x + width / 2) * CELL, 0, (z + depth / 2) * CELL)
	return plot.origin * CFrame.new(center) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(90 * rotation), 0), nil
end

return PlotGrid
```

The remote handler looks the item up in a server table (`ITEMS[itemId]`) and the plot in a server map keyed by the player, then calls `place` and clones the model to the returned CFrame.

- The client can only choose among valid placements; no CFrame it could forge ever reaches the server.
- The occupancy map is the source of truth for overlap; it is faster and more exact than a physics query, and it is what you save.
- Rotation 1 and 3 swap width and depth, so a 2x1 table rotated 90 degrees still has to fit the plot.

Treat the Instance as an untrusted pointer: check it is an Instance, of the class you expect, and that it sits directly in that player's Backpack or Character. Then price it from a server table by its name, never from anything on the client or the tool.

```lua
--!strict
-- Script: ServerScriptService.SellTools
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local SELL_PRICES: { [string]: number } = { WoodSword = 10, IronSword = 40, Bow = 25 }

local sellTool = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
sellTool.Name = "SellTool"
sellTool.Parent = ReplicatedStorage

local function ownedTool(player: Player, value: unknown): Tool?
	local kind = typeof(value)
	if kind ~= "Instance" then
		return nil
	end
	local tool = value :: any
	if not tool:IsA("Tool") then
		return nil
	end
	local backpack = player:FindFirstChildOfClass("Backpack")
	local character = player.Character
	local parent = tool.Parent
	if parent ~= nil and (parent == backpack or parent == character) then
		return tool
	end
	return nil
end

local function onSell(player: Player, value: unknown)
	local tool = ownedTool(player, value)
	if tool == nil then
		return
	end
	local price = SELL_PRICES[tool.Name]
	if price == nil then
		return -- not a sellable item
	end
	local stats: Instance? = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
	local coins: Instance? = if stats then stats:FindFirstChild("Coins") else nil
	if coins == nil or not coins:IsA("IntValue") then
		return
	end
	tool:Destroy()
	local wallet = coins :: IntValue
	wallet.Value += price
end

sellTool.OnServerEvent:Connect(onSell)

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player: Player)
	local stats = Instance.new("Folder")
	stats.Name = "leaderstats"
	local coins = Instance.new("IntValue")
	coins.Name = "Coins"
	coins.Parent = stats
	stats.Parent = player
end)
for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
	if player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats") == nil then
		local stats = Instance.new("Folder")
		stats.Name = "leaderstats"
		local coins = Instance.new("IntValue")
		coins.Name = "Coins"
		coins.Parent = stats
		stats.Parent = player
	end
end
```

- Checking the direct parent (not `IsDescendantOf(workspace)`) is what stops "sell the map": a map part is never a Tool inside your own Backpack.
- Tool names can be renamed by nothing but the server, but your real inventory should live in server data; the Tool is only the visual, and the sale should remove the item from that data too.
- Destroy first, then pay: if anything errors in between, the player loses a tool instead of the server minting coins.
request: I have a "SellTool" RemoteEvent where the client passes the Tool they want to sell. An exploiter sold someone else's sword and even parts of the map. How do I check that the Instance a client sends is really theirs?

answer:
The client is deciding the result (who and how much). Let it send only the intent, "I swung at this character", and let the server decide the rest: the damage comes from the weapon's server config, the swing rate is limited by a cooldown, and the target must be a living character in reach and not the attacker.

```lua
--!strict
-- Script: ServerScriptService.SwordServer
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local SWORD = { damage = 20, range = 8, cooldown = 0.6 }

local swing = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
swing.Name = "SwordSwing"
swing.Parent = ReplicatedStorage

local lastSwing: { [Player]: number } = {}

local function livingHumanoid(model: Model): Humanoid?
	local humanoid: Humanoid? = model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if humanoid and humanoid.Health > 0 then
		return humanoid
	end
	return nil
end

local function onSwing(player: Player, targetArg: unknown)
	local now = os.clock()
	local last = lastSwing[player]
	if last and now - last < SWORD.cooldown then
		return
	end
	local kind = typeof(targetArg)
	if kind ~= "Instance" or not (targetArg :: any):IsA("Model") then
		return
	end
	local target = targetArg :: Model
	local character: Model? = player.Character
	if character == nil or target == character or livingHumanoid(character) == nil then
		return
	end
	local humanoid = livingHumanoid(target)
	local myRoot: BasePart? = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	local theirRoot: BasePart? = target:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	if humanoid == nil or myRoot == nil or theirRoot == nil then
		return
	end
	if (myRoot.Position - theirRoot.Position).Magnitude > SWORD.range then
		return
	end
	lastSwing[player] = now
	humanoid:TakeDamage(SWORD.damage)
end

swing.OnServerEvent:Connect(onSwing)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player)
	lastSwing[player] = nil
end)
```

- The cooldown is recorded only for valid swings, so a laggy miss does not eat the next real hit, but spam still cannot beat `SWORD.cooldown`.
- `range` should be a bit larger than the visual reach to absorb latency. Distance uses the positions the server sees, not a value in the request, but the attacker's character position still replicates from their own client, so pair this with server-side movement checks if teleport-and-hit matters.
- For teams, add a check that `Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(target)` is not on the attacker's team before applying damage.

answer:
The server checks that the argument is a real chest (a tagged Model in workspace), that the player has a living character close enough to it, and that the chest is not already opened or on cooldown for that player. Only then does the server roll and grant the reward.

```lua
--!strict
-- Script: ServerScriptService.Chests
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local MAX_DISTANCE = 12
local REOPEN_SECONDS = 300

local openChest = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
openChest.Name = "OpenChest"
openChest.Parent = ReplicatedStorage

local lastOpened: { [Model]: { [number]: number } } = {}

local function validChest(value: unknown): Model?
	local kind = typeof(value)
	if kind ~= "Instance" then
		return nil
	end
	local chest = value :: any
	if chest:IsA("Model") and CollectionService:HasTag(chest, "Chest") and chest:IsDescendantOf(workspace) then
		return chest
	end
	return nil
end

local function withinReach(player: Player, chest: Model): boolean
	local character: Model? = player.Character
	if character == nil then
		return false
	end
	local root: BasePart? = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	local humanoid: Humanoid? = character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if root == nil or humanoid == nil or humanoid.Health <= 0 then
		return false
	end
	local pivot: CFrame = chest:GetPivot()
	return (root.Position - pivot.Position).Magnitude <= MAX_DISTANCE
end

local function onOpen(player: Player, value: unknown)
	local chest = validChest(value)
	if chest == nil or not withinReach(player, chest) then
		return
	end
	local userId: number = player.UserId
	local openedBy = lastOpened[chest] or {}
	lastOpened[chest] = openedBy
	local now = os.clock()
	local last = openedBy[userId]
	if last and now - last < REOPEN_SECONDS then
		return
	end
	openedBy[userId] = now
	local reward = chest:GetAttribute("Coins")
	player:SetAttribute("Coins", (player:GetAttribute("Coins") or 0) + (if type(reward) == "number" then reward else 5))
end

openChest.OnServerEvent:Connect(onOpen)

CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal("Chest"):Connect(function(chest: Instance)
	lastOpened[chest :: any] = nil
end)
```

- Use the chest's pivot, not a client-sent position; the client only names which chest, the server measures.
- Allow a little slack in `MAX_DISTANCE` for latency (the server sees the character slightly behind where the client is).
- The reward comes from an attribute you set in Studio on the chest, so exploiters cannot change what a chest is worth.
request: My chests are opened with a RemoteEvent `OpenChest:FireServer(chestModel)`. Exploiters open every chest on the map from spawn. How should the server validate this request?

answer:
Wrap handlers in a guard that measures each argument with a bounded walk: it stops as soon as a string, table depth or total element count passes your limit, so a hostile payload costs only a small, fixed amount of work. Handlers connected through the guard only ever see arguments within those bounds, plus a per-player rate limit.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.RemoteGuard
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

export type Limits = { maxString: number, maxDepth: number, maxElements: number, perSecond: number }

local RemoteGuard = {}

-- Returns false as soon as any limit is exceeded; `budget` counts every element visited.
local function within(value: unknown, limits: Limits, depth: number, budget: { n: number }): boolean
	budget.n += 1
	if budget.n > limits.maxElements then
		return false
	end
	local kind = type(value)
	if kind == "string" then
		return #(value :: string) <= limits.maxString
	elseif kind == "table" then
		if depth >= limits.maxDepth then
			return false
		end
		for k, v in value :: { [any]: any } do
			if not within(k, limits, depth + 1, budget) or not within(v, limits, depth + 1, budget) then
				return false
			end
		end
	end
	return true
end

function RemoteGuard.check(limits: Limits, ...: any): boolean
	local budget = { n = 0 }
	for i = 1, select("#", ...) do
		if not within((select(i, ...)), limits, 0, budget) then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

function RemoteGuard.connect(remote: RemoteEvent, limits: Limits, handler: (Player, ...any) -> ()): RBXScriptConnection
	local last: { [Player]: { at: number, count: number } } = {}
	Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player)
		last[player] = nil
	end)
	return remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player: Player, ...: any)
		local now = os.clock()
		local window = last[player]
		if window == nil or now - window.at >= 1 then
			window = { at = now, count = 0 }
			last[player] = window
		end
		window.count += 1
		if window.count > limits.perSecond or not RemoteGuard.check(limits, ...) then
			return
		end
		handler(player, ...)
	end)
end

return RemoteGuard
```

Usage: `RemoteGuard.connect(saveOutfit, { maxString = 64, maxDepth = 3, maxElements = 200, perSecond = 5 }, onSaveOutfit)`; `onSaveOutfit` still validates the exact shape it expects.

- The walk visits at most `maxElements` values whatever the client sends, so the cost of rejecting a huge table is the same as checking a small one.
- Roblox already caps how much a single remote call can carry, but the server still deserialises it; the guard keeps your own code from doing more work than it must.
- Choose limits per remote: a chat-like remote needs longer strings, a "use ability" remote needs one short string and nothing else.
request: An exploiter lagged my server by firing a remote with a giant nested table. My handlers validate fields, but by then the server has already walked the whole thing. Can I reject oversized arguments before any handler logic runs?

answer:
Text written by one player and shown to others must go through `TextService:FilterStringAsync` on the server, using the broadcast result. Validate length and type first, rate-limit renames, and fail closed: if filtering errors, keep the old name instead of showing unfiltered text.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.PetNames
local TextService = game:GetService("TextService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

export type Result = "ok" | "invalid" | "cooldown" | "unavailable"

local MAX_LENGTH = 20
local RENAME_COOLDOWN = 10

local PetNames = {}
local lastRename: { [Player]: number } = {}

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player)
	lastRename[player] = nil
end)

local function clean(raw: unknown): string?
	if type(raw) ~= "string" or utf8.len(raw) == nil then
		return nil
	end
	local trimmed = string.match(raw, "^%s*(.-)%s*$") or ""
	trimmed = string.gsub(trimmed, "%s+", " ")
	local length = utf8.len(trimmed) or 0
	if length < 1 or length > MAX_LENGTH then
		return nil
	end
	return trimmed
end

local function filterForEveryone(text: string, fromUserId: number): string?
	local ok, filtered = pcall(function()
		local result = TextService:FilterStringAsync(text, fromUserId)
		return result:GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync()
	end)
	if ok and type(filtered) == "string" then
		return filtered
	end
	return nil
end

-- pet is a server-owned Model the caller already checked belongs to this player.
function PetNames.rename(player: Player, pet: Model, raw: unknown): Result
	local text = clean(raw)
	if text == nil then
		return "invalid"
	end
	local now = os.clock()
	local last = lastRename[player]
	if last and now - last < RENAME_COOLDOWN then
		return "cooldown"
	end
	lastRename[player] = now
	local filtered = filterForEveryone(text, player.UserId)
	if filtered == nil then
		return "unavailable"
	end
	pet:SetAttribute("PetName", filtered)
	return "ok"
end

return PetNames
```

- Store the raw name in your save data and filter again each time it is shown in a new session: filtering rules change, and a name that passed last year may not today.
- A name that comes back as `####` is still the right result; show it rather than letting the player retry until something slips through.
- Each `FilterStringAsync` is a web call, which is why renames are rate-limited before filtering.
