answer:
Divide by 1000 while the value is at least 1000 and a larger suffix exists, then truncate (not round) to the wanted decimals so a value never displays as the next tier's "1000". Strip a trailing ".0" and handle the sign, NaN and infinity separately.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.Abbreviate
local Abbreviate = {}

local SUFFIXES = { "", "K", "M", "B", "T", "Qa", "Qi" }

function Abbreviate.format(value: number, decimals: number?): string
	if value ~= value then
		return "0"
	elseif value == math.huge or value == -math.huge then
		return if value > 0 then "inf" else "-inf"
	end
	local places = decimals or 1
	local sign = if value < 0 then "-" else ""
	local n = math.abs(value)
	local tier = 1
	while n >= 1000 and tier < #SUFFIXES do
		n /= 1000
		tier += 1
	end
	if tier == 1 then
		return sign .. tostring(math.floor(n))
	end
	local factor = 10 ^ places
	local truncated = math.floor(n * factor + 1e-9) / factor
	local text = string.format("%." .. places .. "f", truncated)
	if places > 0 then
		text = string.gsub(text, "0+$", "")
		text = string.gsub(text, "%.$", "")
	end
	return sign .. text .. SUFFIXES[tier]
end

return Abbreviate
```

- Truncation keeps the label honest: a player with 999,999 coins has not got a million, so it reads "999.9K".
- The `1e-9` nudge absorbs float error: 1,150 with two decimals computes `1.15 * 100`, which is 114.99999999999999 and would otherwise read "1.14K".
- Only the label is abbreviated; the server keeps the exact integer and the shop compares against that.

answer:
Compute everything from the start time: remaining fraction = 1 - elapsed / duration. One Heartbeat connection per active cooldown sets the overlay height and text each frame and disconnects itself at zero, so nothing keeps running. Restarting mid-cooldown replaces the old connection.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.CooldownOverlay
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local CooldownOverlay = {}

export type Overlay = {
	start: (duration: number) -> (),
	isActive: () -> boolean,
}

function CooldownOverlay.remaining(now: number, startedAt: number, duration: number): number
	if duration <= 0 then
		return 0
	end
	return math.clamp(1 - (now - startedAt) / duration, 0, 1)
end

function CooldownOverlay.attach(button: GuiButton): Overlay
	local baseZ: number = button.ZIndex
	local shade = Instance.new("Frame")
	shade.Name = "CooldownShade"
	shade.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0, 1)
	shade.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0, 1)
	shade.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 0)
	shade.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.new(0, 0, 0)
	shade.BackgroundTransparency = 0.4
	shade.ZIndex = baseZ + 1
	shade.Parent = button

	local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	label.Name = "Seconds"
	label.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	label.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	label.TextScaled = true
	label.TextColor3 = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
	label.ZIndex = baseZ + 2
	label.Text = ""
	label.Parent = button

	local connection: RBXScriptConnection? = nil

	local function finish()
		if connection then
			connection:Disconnect()
			connection = nil
		end
		shade.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 0)
		label.Text = ""
	end

	local function start(duration: number)
		finish()
		local startedAt = os.clock()
		local function step()
			local left = CooldownOverlay.remaining(os.clock(), startedAt, duration)
			if left <= 0 then
				finish()
				return
			end
			shade.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, left)
			label.Text = tostring(math.ceil(left * duration))
		end
		connection = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(step)
		step()
	end

	return {
		start = start,
		isActive = function()
			return connection ~= nil
		end,
	}
end

return CooldownOverlay
```

- The shade is anchored at the bottom, so shrinking its height makes it recede downward as the ability fills back up.
- `math.ceil` shows "1" during the last second instead of "0" while it is still unusable.
- The overlay is display only; the server keeps its own cooldown per player and rejects early activations.

Clean the text as it is typed (digits only, limited length) and settle the final value when focus is lost: parse, clamp to 1..max, and write the clamped number back so what the player sees is what will be sent. The server still validates the amount it receives.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.AmountBox
local AmountBox = {}

export type Field = { value: () -> number, setMax: (max: number) -> () }

function AmountBox.digitsOnly(text: string, maxLength: number): string
	local digits = string.gsub(text, "%D", "")
	return string.sub(digits, 1, maxLength)
end

function AmountBox.settle(text: string, max: number): number
	local n = tonumber(text)
	if n == nil then
		return 1
	end
	return math.clamp(math.floor(n), 1, math.max(1, max))
end

function AmountBox.bind(box: TextBox, initialMax: number, onChanged: (amount: number) -> ()): Field
	local max = initialMax
	local amount = AmountBox.settle(box.Text, max)
	local maxLength = #tostring(max)
	box.ClearTextOnFocus = false
	box.Text = tostring(amount)

	box:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Text"):Connect(function()
		local cleaned = AmountBox.digitsOnly(box.Text, maxLength)
		if cleaned ~= box.Text then
			box.Text = cleaned
		end
	end)

	box.FocusLost:Connect(function()
		amount = AmountBox.settle(box.Text, max)
		box.Text = tostring(amount)
		onChanged(amount)
	end)

	return {
		value = function()
			return amount
		end,
		setMax = function(newMax: number)
			max = newMax
			maxLength = #tostring(newMax)
			amount = AmountBox.settle(tostring(amount), max)
			box.Text = tostring(amount)
		end,
	}
end

return AmountBox
```

- Writing the cleaned text back only when it differs avoids an endless Text-changed loop.
- Limiting length to the digits of `max` blocks pasting a 400-digit number before it is ever parsed.
- Set `max` from what the player owns; when the stack shrinks, `setMax` pulls the shown amount down with it.

answer:
Position places the frame's AnchorPoint, which defaults to its top-left corner, so your popup's corner sits at the centre. Set `AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)` and the frame's own centre lands there. A tiny helper that always sets the two together keeps every screen edge placement consistent.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.Place
local Place = {}

export type Spot = "center" | "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right" | "topLeft" | "topRight" | "bottomLeft" | "bottomRight"

local ANCHORS: { [Spot]: Vector2 } = {
	center = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5),
	top = Vector2.new(0.5, 0),
	bottom = Vector2.new(0.5, 1),
	left = Vector2.new(0, 0.5),
	right = Vector2.new(1, 0.5),
	topLeft = Vector2.new(0, 0),
	topRight = Vector2.new(1, 0),
	bottomLeft = Vector2.new(0, 1),
	bottomRight = Vector2.new(1, 1),
}

-- The anchor doubles as the scale position; the margin pushes inward from whichever edge the anchor touches.
function Place.at(gui: GuiObject, spot: Spot, margin: number?)
	local anchor = ANCHORS[spot]
	assert(anchor ~= nil, "unknown spot")
	local m = margin or 0
	local dx = if anchor.X == 0 then m elseif anchor.X == 1 then -m else 0
	local dy = if anchor.Y == 0 then m elseif anchor.Y == 1 then -m else 0
	gui.AnchorPoint = anchor
	gui.Position = UDim2.new(anchor.X, dx, anchor.Y, dy)
end

return Place
```

```lua
--!strict
local Place = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Place"))

local function placePopup(popup: Frame)
	popup.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.4, 0.35)
	Place.at(popup, "center")
end

return placePopup
```

- AnchorPoint also controls which way a frame grows when its size changes: a centred popup grows evenly in all directions.
- `bottom` with a margin is the usual spot for toasts, `topRight` for currency counters.
- The anchor works the same for Scale and Offset sizes, so the fix does not depend on how the popup is sized.

answer:
Compute an alpha from the camera distance (0 inside the fade start, 1 at the fade end) and drive the labels' transparency with it. Update all labels from one loop a few times per second rather than one connection per label per frame, and keep MaxDistance as the hard cut-off for rendering.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.DistanceFade
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local DistanceFade = {}

function DistanceFade.alpha(distance: number, fadeStart: number, fadeEnd: number): number
	if distance <= fadeStart then
		return 0
	elseif distance >= fadeEnd then
		return 1
	end
	return (distance - fadeStart) / (fadeEnd - fadeStart)
end

export type Fader = { add: (gui: BillboardGui, label: TextLabel) -> (), stop: () -> () }

function DistanceFade.start(fadeStart: number, fadeEnd: number, interval: number?): Fader
	local entries: { [BillboardGui]: TextLabel } = {}
	local every = interval or 0.1
	local elapsed = every

	local connection = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt: number)
		elapsed += dt
		if elapsed < every then
			return
		end
		elapsed = 0
		local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera
		if camera == nil then
			return
		end
		local eye: Vector3 = camera.CFrame.Position
		for gui, label in entries do
			local adornee = gui.Adornee
			if gui.Parent == nil or adornee == nil then
				entries[gui] = nil
				continue
			end
			local where: Vector3 = adornee.Position
			local a = DistanceFade.alpha((where - eye).Magnitude, fadeStart, fadeEnd)
			label.TextTransparency = a
			label.TextStrokeTransparency = 0.5 + a * 0.5
		end
	end)

	return {
		add = function(gui: BillboardGui, label: TextLabel)
			gui.MaxDistance = fadeEnd
			entries[gui] = label
		end,
		stop = function()
			connection:Disconnect()
		end,
	}
end

return DistanceFade
```

- Ten updates per second is smooth enough for a fade and costs a tenth of a per-frame loop.
- Entries whose gui was destroyed or lost its adornee are dropped during the loop, so the table does not grow forever.
- Setting MaxDistance to the fade end means the engine stops drawing exactly where the label becomes invisible.

```lua
end
```

answer:
Derive the look from a few booleans (enabled, hovering, pressing) through one `visual()` function and render from it, so the states cannot contradict each other. Turn `AutoButtonColor` off, treat gamepad selection like hover, and guard the click handler itself rather than relying on looks.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.StatefulButton
local StatefulButton = {}

export type Visual = "idle" | "hover" | "pressed" | "disabled"
export type Button = {
	instance: TextButton,
	setEnabled: (enabled: boolean) -> (),
	visual: () -> Visual,
	destroy: () -> (),
}

local FILL: { [Visual]: Color3 } = {
	idle = Color3.fromRGB(38, 99, 196),
	hover = Color3.fromRGB(52, 116, 216),
	pressed = Color3.fromRGB(30, 80, 160),
	disabled = Color3.fromRGB(64, 68, 76),
}

function StatefulButton.new(text: string, onActivated: () -> ()): Button
	local enabled, hovering, pressing = true, false, false

	local button = Instance.new("TextButton")
	button.AutoButtonColor = false
	button.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(180, 44)
	button.TextSize = 18
	button.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
	button.Text = text

	local function visual(): Visual
		if not enabled then
			return "disabled"
		elseif pressing then
			return "pressed"
		elseif hovering then
			return "hover"
		end
		return "idle"
	end

	local function render()
		local v = visual()
		button.BackgroundColor3 = FILL[v]
		button.TextTransparency = if v == "disabled" then 0.5 else 0
	end

	local function setHover(on: boolean)
		hovering = on
		if not on then
			pressing = false
		end
		render()
	end

	local connections = {
		button.MouseEnter:Connect(function()
			setHover(true)
		end),
		button.MouseLeave:Connect(function()
			setHover(false)
		end),
		button.SelectionGained:Connect(function()
			setHover(true)
		end),
		button.SelectionLost:Connect(function()
			setHover(false)
		end),
		button.MouseButton1Down:Connect(function()
			pressing = true
			render()
		end),
		button.MouseButton1Up:Connect(function()
			pressing = false
			render()
		end),
		button.Activated:Connect(function()
			if enabled then
				onActivated()
			end
		end),
	}

	local function setEnabled(value: boolean)
		enabled = value
		pressing = false
		button.Selectable = value
		render()
	end

	local function destroy()
		for _, connection in connections do
			connection:Disconnect()
		end
		button:Destroy()
	end

	render()
	return { instance = button, setEnabled = setEnabled, visual = visual, destroy = destroy }
end

return StatefulButton
```

- The disabled look is a muted fill plus faded text, not just a colour change, so it reads for colour-blind players too.
- `Selectable = false` while disabled stops the gamepad cursor landing on a button that cannot be used.
- Leaving the button cancels the press, which matches how a release outside a button does not click it.
- For buttons that send a request, disable on click and re-enable when the server answers.

answer:
Make the panel a CanvasGroup and tween its single `GroupTransparency`: the whole group is rendered together and faded as one image, so children keep their own transparency values untouched. Cancel the previous tween on each new fade and only hide the panel when a fade-out actually completes.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.Fader
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local Fader = {}

export type Fade = { show: () -> (), hide: () -> (), visible: () -> boolean }

function Fader.new(group: CanvasGroup, seconds: number?): Fade
	local info = TweenInfo.new(seconds or 0.2, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
	local current: Tween? = nil
	local wanted = group.Visible

	local function fadeTo(target: number, onDone: (() -> ())?)
		if current then
			current:Cancel()
		end
		local tween = TweenService:Create(group, info, { GroupTransparency = target })
		current = tween
		tween.Completed:Connect(function(state: Enum.PlaybackState)
			if state == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed and current == tween then
				current = nil
				if onDone then
					onDone()
				end
			end
		end)
		tween:Play()
	end

	return {
		show = function()
			wanted = true
			if not group.Visible then
				group.GroupTransparency = 1
				group.Visible = true
			end
			fadeTo(0)
		end,
		hide = function()
			wanted = false
			fadeTo(1, function()
				group.Visible = false
			end)
		end,
		visible = function()
			return wanted
		end,
	}
end

return Fader
```

- CanvasGroup renders its children into a texture; keep it for panels and dialogs, not for huge scrolling lists, which cost more memory as a group.
- Starting a show from fully transparent only when the panel was hidden means reversing a half-finished hide continues from the current value.
- Short fades (0.15 to 0.25 s) feel responsive; long ones make menus feel slow.

answer:
Bind the action with ContextActionService and pass `true` for `createTouchButton`: one handler then serves Left Shift, the controller's left stick click and an automatic mobile button. Make it a toggle, because holding a touch button while steering is awkward, and unbind when the character goes away.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: StarterPlayerScripts.Sprint
local ContextActionService = game:GetService("ContextActionService")

local Sprint = {}

local ACTION = "SprintToggle"
local WALK_SPEED = 16
local SPRINT_SPEED = 24

function Sprint.bind(humanoid: Humanoid): () -> ()
	local sprinting = false

	local function apply()
		humanoid.WalkSpeed = if sprinting then SPRINT_SPEED else WALK_SPEED
		ContextActionService:SetTitle(ACTION, if sprinting then "Walk" else "Run")
	end

	local function onAction(_name: string, state: Enum.UserInputState, _input: InputObject): Enum.ContextActionResult
		if state ~= Enum.UserInputState.Begin then
			return Enum.ContextActionResult.Pass
		end
		sprinting = not sprinting
		apply()
		return Enum.ContextActionResult.Sink
	end

	ContextActionService:BindAction(ACTION, onAction, true, Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonL3)
	ContextActionService:SetPosition(ACTION, UDim2.new(1, -150, 1, -150))
	apply()

	local diedConnection: RBXScriptConnection? = nil
	local function unbind()
		if diedConnection then
			diedConnection:Disconnect()
			diedConnection = nil
		end
		ContextActionService:UnbindAction(ACTION)
		sprinting = false
	end
	diedConnection = humanoid.Died:Connect(unbind)

	return unbind
end

return Sprint
```

answer:
Animate a UIScale rather than Size, and always pop from the rest scale: cancel any running tweens, snap to 1, then tween up and back. Because each pop starts from 1, rapid gains restart the pop instead of compounding it.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.Pop
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local Pop = {}

local UP = TweenInfo.new(0.08, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
local DOWN = TweenInfo.new(0.18, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)

export type Popper = { pop: () -> (), scale: UIScale }

function Pop.attach(gui: GuiObject, peak: number?): Popper
	local scale = gui:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIScale") or Instance.new("UIScale")
	scale.Scale = 1
	scale.Parent = gui
	local top = peak or 1.12
	local running: { Tween } = {}

	local function cancelAll()
		for _, tween in running do
			tween:Cancel()
		end
		running = {}
	end

	local function pop()
		cancelAll()
		scale.Scale = 1
		local up = TweenService:Create(scale, UP, { Scale = top })
		local down = TweenService:Create(scale, DOWN, { Scale = 1 })
		running = { up, down }
		up.Completed:Connect(function(state: Enum.PlaybackState)
			if state == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed then
				down:Play()
			end
		end)
		up:Play()
	end

	return { pop = pop, scale = scale }
end

return Pop
```

- UIScale scales around the element's AnchorPoint, so anchor the counter at its centre for a symmetric pop.
- Tweening the UIScale leaves the label's own Size untouched, so the pop never fights the code or constraints that size the counter.
- Respect reduced motion by skipping `pop` when the player has it enabled; the number change itself is the feedback.

answer:
Use the WCAG definition: convert each sRGB channel to linear light, compute relative luminance, and the contrast ratio is `(lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05)`, from 1 (none) to 21 (black on white). Pick whichever text colour gives the higher ratio and expose the ratio so a style check can flag pairs under 4.5.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.Contrast
local Contrast = {}

local function linear(channel: number): number
	if channel <= 0.04045 then
		return channel / 12.92
	end
	return ((channel + 0.055) / 1.055) ^ 2.4
end

function Contrast.luminance(color: Color3): number
	return 0.2126 * linear(color.R) + 0.7152 * linear(color.G) + 0.0722 * linear(color.B)
end

function Contrast.ratio(a: Color3, b: Color3): number
	local la, lb = Contrast.luminance(a), Contrast.luminance(b)
	local lighter, darker = math.max(la, lb), math.min(la, lb)
	return (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05)
end

local DARK = Color3.fromRGB(17, 17, 17)
local LIGHT = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)

function Contrast.textFor(background: Color3): Color3
	if Contrast.ratio(background, DARK) >= Contrast.ratio(background, LIGHT) then
		return DARK
	end
	return LIGHT
end

-- 4.5 is the WCAG AA minimum for body text; 3 is enough for large bold text.
function Contrast.meets(text: Color3, background: Color3, largeText: boolean?): boolean
	return Contrast.ratio(text, background) >= (if largeText then 3 else 4.5)
end

return Contrast
```

- Averaging R, G and B is not luminance: green looks far brighter than blue, which is why the weights differ.
- Near-black (17, 17, 17) reads softer than pure black and still passes on every light colour.
- Run `Contrast.meets` over your theme tokens in a test so a palette change cannot ship unreadable text.

answer:
Tween a NumberValue (TweenService cannot tween a label's text) and write the rounded value to the label whenever it changes. Keep the tween in a variable: a new target cancels the old tween and starts from the value currently displayed. On completion, set the exact target so rounding never leaves it one short.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.CountUp
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local CountUp = {}

export type Counter = { set: (target: number) -> (), shown: () -> number }

function CountUp.new(label: TextLabel, format: ((n: number) -> string)?, seconds: number?): Counter
	local fmt = format or function(n: number): string
		return tostring(n)
	end
	local info = TweenInfo.new(seconds or 1, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
	local value = Instance.new("NumberValue")
	value.Value = 0
	local current: Tween? = nil
	local target = 0

	local function show()
		local n: number = value.Value
		label.Text = fmt(math.floor(n + 0.5))
	end
	value.Changed:Connect(show)

	local function set(newTarget: number)
		target = newTarget
		if current then
			current:Cancel()
		end
		local tween = TweenService:Create(value, info, { Value = newTarget })
		current = tween
		tween.Completed:Connect(function(state: Enum.PlaybackState)
			if state == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed and current == tween then
				current = nil
				value.Value = target
				show()
			end
		end)
		tween:Play()
	end

	show()
	return {
		set = set,
		shown = function()
			local n: number = value.Value
			return math.floor(n + 0.5)
		end,
	}
end

return CountUp
```

- Tweening from the NumberValue's current value is what makes interruption seamless: TweenService always starts from the live property.
- Pass a formatter (separators or abbreviations) so the animation and the static label use identical text.
- Keep the NumberValue unparented; it only exists to be tweened on this client.

answer:
Format the whole part as digits, take the first group of 1-3 digits, then every following group of exactly three, and join them with the separator. Choose the separator from the player's locale (`LocalizationService.RobloxLocaleId`) with a small table, defaulting to a comma.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.NumberText
local NumberText = {}

local SEPARATORS: { [string]: string } = {
	["de-de"] = ".",
	["es-es"] = ".",
	["pt-br"] = ".",
	["it-it"] = ".",
	["id-id"] = ".",
	["fr-fr"] = "\u{202F}",
}

function NumberText.separatorFor(localeId: string): string
	return SEPARATORS[string.lower(localeId)] or ","
end

function NumberText.grouped(value: number, separator: string?): string
	if value ~= value or value == math.huge or value == -math.huge then
		return "0"
	end
	local sep = separator or ","
	local sign = if value < 0 then "-" else ""
	local digits = string.format("%d", math.floor(math.abs(value)))
	local head = #digits % 3
	if head == 0 then
		head = 3
	end
	local parts = { string.sub(digits, 1, head) }
	for i = head + 1, #digits, 3 do
		table.insert(parts, string.sub(digits, i, i + 2))
	end
	return sign .. table.concat(parts, sep)
end

return NumberText
```

```lua
return showBalance
```

- `%d` with `math.floor` always prints plain digits, while `tostring` switches to exponent form (such as `1e+16`) for very large balances.
- The label is display only; the server stores and compares the integer.

answer:
Derive them in HSV: hover raises the value (brightness) a fixed step, pressed lowers it, and very dark bases get a larger hover step so the change stays visible. Clamping keeps white and black bases sensible. One pure function gives every button the same feel.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.Shades
local Shades = {}

export type Set = { base: Color3, hover: Color3, pressed: Color3, disabled: Color3 }

local function shift(color: Color3, deltaValue: number, saturationScale: number?): Color3
	local h, s, v = color:ToHSV()
	return Color3.fromHSV(h, math.clamp(s * (saturationScale or 1), 0, 1), math.clamp(v + deltaValue, 0, 1))
end

function Shades.derive(base: Color3): Set
	local _, _, value = base:ToHSV()
	local hoverStep = if value < 0.3 then 0.12 else 0.07
	local hover = if value > 0.93 then shift(base, -0.06) else shift(base, hoverStep)
	return {
		base = base,
		hover = hover,
		pressed = shift(base, -0.1),
		disabled = shift(base, -0.15, 0.25),
	}
end

return Shades
```

- Changing value keeps the hue, so a blue button's hover is still the same blue, unlike lerping toward white.
- Near-white bases darken on hover instead, since they cannot get brighter.
- The disabled shade drops most of the saturation, so it reads as inactive for colour-blind players as well.

answer:
Combine `TextWrapped` with `TextTruncate = AtEnd` and a height of exactly N lines (`TextSize * LineHeight * N`): the engine wraps and puts the ellipsis on the last visible line. Expanding switches the label to `AutomaticSize = Y` without truncation; the "More" button only shows when the text does not fit (`TextFits`).

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.ClampedText
local ClampedText = {}

export type Clamped = {
	label: TextLabel,
	setText: (text: string) -> (),
	setExpanded: (expanded: boolean) -> (),
	isExpanded: () -> boolean,
}

function ClampedText.heightFor(textSize: number, lineHeight: number, lines: number): number
	return math.ceil(textSize * lineHeight * lines)
end

function ClampedText.new(maxLines: number, textSize: number): Clamped
	local expanded = false
	local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	label.Name = "Description"
	label.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	label.TextWrapped = true
	label.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
	label.TextYAlignment = Enum.TextYAlignment.Top
	label.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(200, 204, 212)
	label.TextSize = textSize
	label.LineHeight = 1.15

	local collapsedHeight = ClampedText.heightFor(textSize, label.LineHeight, maxLines)

	local function setExpanded(value: boolean)
		expanded = value
		if expanded then
			label.TextTruncate = Enum.TextTruncate.None
			label.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, collapsedHeight)
			label.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y
		else
			label.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.None
			label.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, collapsedHeight)
			label.TextTruncate = Enum.TextTruncate.AtEnd
		end
	end

	local function setText(text: string)
		label.Text = text
		setExpanded(false)
	end

	setExpanded(false)
	return {
		label = label,
		setText = setText,
		setExpanded = setExpanded,
		isExpanded = function()
			return expanded
		end,
	}
end

return ClampedText
```

```lua
--!strict
local ClampedText = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("ClampedText"))

local function mountDescription(parent: Frame, moreButton: TextButton, text: string)
	local clamped = ClampedText.new(3, 15)
	clamped.setText(text)
```

- Collapsed height is computed from the same TextSize and LineHeight the label uses, so changing the font size keeps exactly three lines.
- Expanding keeps the collapsed height as the minimum and lets AutomaticSize grow it, so short texts do not jump.
- Setting new text collapses again, which is what players expect when they select a different item.

answer:
Classify with two inputs: how the player is interacting (`UserInputService.PreferredInput`) and the viewport's short side. Map the class to a small table of metrics (text size, button height, margin) and rebuild or restyle when either input changes. Keep the classification pure so it is easy to test.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.LayoutProfile
local LayoutProfile = {}

export type Class = "phone" | "tablet" | "tv" | "desktop"
export type Metrics = { textSize: number, buttonHeight: number, margin: number }

local METRICS: { [Class]: Metrics } = {
	phone = { textSize = 16, buttonHeight = 52, margin = 12 },
	tablet = { textSize = 18, buttonHeight = 48, margin = 20 },
	tv = { textSize = 24, buttonHeight = 56, margin = 48 },
	desktop = { textSize = 16, buttonHeight = 36, margin = 16 },
}

function LayoutProfile.classify(preferred: Enum.PreferredInput, viewport: Vector2): Class
	if preferred == Enum.PreferredInput.Gamepad then
		return "tv"
	elseif preferred == Enum.PreferredInput.Touch then
		return if math.min(viewport.X, viewport.Y) < 500 then "phone" else "tablet"
	end
	return "desktop"
end

function LayoutProfile.metrics(class: Class): Metrics
	return METRICS[class]
end

-- Calls onChange(class) now and whenever the input method or the viewport changes class.
function LayoutProfile.watch(onChange: (class: Class) -> ()): () -> ()
	local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
	local current: Class? = nil
	local function evaluate()
		local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera
		local viewport: Vector2 = if camera then camera.ViewportSize else Vector2.new(1280, 720)
		local class = LayoutProfile.classify(UserInputService.PreferredInput, viewport)
		if class ~= current then
			current = class
			onChange(class)
		end
	end
	local connections = {
		UserInputService:GetPropertyChangedSignal("PreferredInput"):Connect(evaluate),
		workspace.CurrentCamera:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize"):Connect(evaluate),
	}
	evaluate()
	return function()
		for _, connection in connections do
			connection:Disconnect()
		end
	end
end

return LayoutProfile
```

- Touch targets of about 48 px or more are what thumbs hit reliably; desktop can be denser because a mouse is precise.
- TVs are viewed from a couch and may crop edges, hence the large text and wide margin.
- Notifying only when the class changes avoids rebuilding the HUD on every pixel of a window resize.

answer:
`string.sub` counts bytes, and many characters take two to four bytes in UTF-8, so a cut can land mid-character. Count and cut by code points with `utf8.len` and `utf8.offset`, add a single ellipsis character, and fall back to a byte cut only if the string is not valid UTF-8.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.ShortName
local ShortName = {}

local ELLIPSIS = "\u{2026}"

function ShortName.cut(text: string, maxChars: number): string
	assert(maxChars >= 1, "maxChars must be at least 1")
	local length = utf8.len(text)
	if length == nil then
		return string.sub(text, 1, maxChars)
	end
	if length <= maxChars then
		return text
	end
	-- Byte index where the code point after the kept ones starts.
	local stop = utf8.offset(text, maxChars)
	assert(stop ~= nil)
	return string.sub(text, 1, stop - 1) .. ELLIPSIS
end

return ShortName
```

```lua
--!strict
local ShortName = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("ShortName"))

local function setMemberName(label: TextLabel, player: Player)
	label.Text = ShortName.cut(player.DisplayName, 14)
	label.TextTruncate = Enum.TextTruncate.AtEnd
end

return setMemberName
```

- The kept text is `maxChars - 1` code points plus the ellipsis, so the result never exceeds `maxChars` characters.
- Combining accents count as separate code points; the worst case is an accent dropped from the last letter, never invalid text.
- `TextTruncate = AtEnd` is a second safety net for wide glyphs that need more room than the character count suggests.

answer:
AbsoluteSize and AbsolutePosition are computed by the layout pass, which runs before the next frame renders, not at the moment you set Size or Parent. Until the object is parented under a rendered ScreenGui and a layout pass has run, the values are zero or stale. Instead of guessing with waits, react to the property: run your code now if the size is already valid, and again whenever it changes.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.WhenSized
local WhenSized = {}

-- Calls `callback(size)` for the current valid size and for every later change. Returns the connection.
function WhenSized.watch(gui: GuiObject, callback: (size: Vector2) -> ()): RBXScriptConnection
	local function check()
		local size: Vector2 = gui.AbsoluteSize
		if size.X > 0 and size.Y > 0 then
			callback(size)
		end
	end
	local connection = gui:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(check)
	check()
	return connection
end

return WhenSized
```

- Layout objects (UIListLayout, UIGridLayout) have the same timing for `AbsoluteContentSize`; watch it the same way.
- Re-running on every change also handles window resizes and phone rotation, which a one-time wait never would.
- Prefer layout objects and Scale over manual pixel math when you can; then the engine does the timing for you.

answer:
By default a ScreenGui's area starts below the Roblox top bar, so Scale 1 means "the screen minus the top bar" and is offset down by it. For full-screen covers set `IgnoreGuiInset = true` (and `ScreenInsets = None` so device safe areas such as a notch are covered too). Keep interactive controls in a separate gui that respects the insets.

```lua
--!strict
-- LocalScript: ReplicatedFirst.LoadingCover
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedFirst = game:GetService("ReplicatedFirst")

local playerGui = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local cover = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
cover.Name = "LoadingCover"
cover.IgnoreGuiInset = true
cover.ScreenInsets = Enum.ScreenInsets.None
cover.DisplayOrder = 1000
cover.ResetOnSpawn = false

local backdrop = Instance.new("Frame")
backdrop.Name = "Backdrop"
backdrop.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
backdrop.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(14, 15, 18)
backdrop.BorderSizePixel = 0
backdrop.Parent = cover

local status = Instance.new("TextLabel")
status.Name = "Status"
status.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
status.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
status.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(300, 40)
status.BackgroundTransparency = 1
status.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(220, 222, 228)
status.TextSize = 20
status.Text = "Loading"
status.Parent = backdrop

cover.Parent = playerGui
ReplicatedFirst:RemoveDefaultLoadingScreen()
```

- Running from ReplicatedFirst shows the cover before the rest of the game replicates; removing the default screen avoids two loading screens.
- The high DisplayOrder keeps it above HUD guis that load while it is up.
- Positions inside an inset-ignoring gui are measured from the very top of the screen, which matters for anything aligned with `Camera:WorldToViewportPoint`.

StarterGui holds templates; at spawn each player gets copies in their own `Player.PlayerGui`, and those copies are what is on screen. Editing StarterGui changes the template, which nobody is looking at. Reach the player's copy through `Players.LocalPlayer.PlayerGui` (with WaitForChild, since it is created after your script may start).

```lua
--!strict
-- LocalScript: StarterPlayerScripts.CoinDisplay
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local playerGui = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local function coinsLabel(): TextLabel
	local hud = playerGui:WaitForChild("HUD")
	return hud:WaitForChild("Coins") :: TextLabel
end

local function setCoins(coins: number)
	coinsLabel().Text = tostring(coins)
end

return setCoins
```

- If HUD has `ResetOnSpawn = true`, the copy is replaced after each death; looking it up per update (as above) avoids holding a destroyed label.
- `game.StarterGui` also reaches the service by property; use `game:GetService("StarterGui")` when you genuinely need the template, for example `SetCoreGuiEnabled`.
- Server scripts should not write to PlayerGui text at all; send the value and let the client display it.

Every ScreenGui has `ResetOnSpawn`, true by default. When the character respawns, Roblox deletes those ScreenGuis from PlayerGui and copies fresh ones from StarterGui, so their state and the LocalScripts inside them start over. Set it to false for UI that should outlive a death, or create that UI from a LocalScript in StarterPlayerScripts, which does not rerun on respawn.

```lua
--!strict
-- LocalScript: StarterPlayerScripts.ShopBootstrap
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local playerGui = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local shopGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
shopGui.Name = "Shop"
shopGui.ResetOnSpawn = false
shopGui.ZIndexBehavior = Enum.ZIndexBehavior.Sibling

local window = Instance.new("Frame")
window.Name = "Window"
window.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
window.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
window.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.6)
window.Visible = false
window.Parent = shopGui

shopGui.Parent = playerGui
```

- Keep `ResetOnSpawn = true` for things tied to one life, such as a health bar wired to the old Humanoid; they then rebind to the new character for free.
- With `ResetOnSpawn = false`, anything that references the character must listen to `player.CharacterAdded`, because the old Humanoid is gone after a respawn.
- Setting the property on the StarterGui copy in Studio works too; the copy in PlayerGui inherits it.

answer:
StarterGui is only a template: its contents are copied into PlayerGui when a character spawns, so adding to it at runtime does nothing for players already playing. Parenting server-made UI into PlayerGui works, but the server then owns those instances, and replication of later changes can fight with client edits. Let the server send data (a RemoteEvent with the message) and let a LocalScript build and animate the UI.

```lua
--!strict
-- LocalScript: StarterPlayerScripts.Announcements
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local announce = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Announce") :: RemoteEvent
local playerGui = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local gui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
gui.Name = "Announcements"
gui.ResetOnSpawn = false

local banner = Instance.new("TextLabel")
banner.Name = "Banner"
banner.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0)
banner.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, 24)
banner.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(420, 48)
banner.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(24, 26, 31)
banner.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(240, 240, 240)
banner.TextSize = 22
banner.Visible = false
banner.Parent = gui
gui.Parent = playerGui

local shown = 0
announce.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(message: string, seconds: number)
	if type(message) ~= "string" or type(seconds) ~= "number" then
		return
	end
	shown += 1
	local token = shown
	banner.Text = message
	banner.Visible = true
	task.delay(math.clamp(seconds, 1, 15), function()
		if shown == token then
			banner.Visible = false
		end
	end)
end)
```

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.RoundAnnouncer (server side, sends data only)
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local announce = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
announce.Name = "Announce"
announce.Parent = ReplicatedStorage

local function announceAll(message: string)
	announce:FireAllClients(message, 4)
end

return announceAll
```

- The client keeps full control of its UI (animations, layout per device), and the server sends a few bytes instead of instances.
- The token check stops an older announcement's timer from hiding a newer one.
- Players who join mid-round can ask for the current state with a RemoteFunction or read replicated attributes when the UI starts.

answer:
It depends on the ScreenGui's `ZIndexBehavior`. With `Sibling` (the default for new ScreenGuis), ZIndex only orders an object against its siblings, and children always draw on top of their parent, so a tooltip deep inside the sidebar can never rise above a panel the sidebar is drawn under. With `Global`, every ZIndex in the gui is compared directly. The clean fix is structural: give overlays (tooltips, modals, dropdown lists) their own ScreenGui with a higher `DisplayOrder`.

```lua
--!strict
-- LocalScript: separate layer for overlays
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local playerGui = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local overlay = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
overlay.Name = "Overlay"
overlay.ZIndexBehavior = Enum.ZIndexBehavior.Sibling
overlay.DisplayOrder = 100
overlay.ResetOnSpawn = false

local tooltip = Instance.new("TextLabel")
tooltip.Name = "Tooltip"
tooltip.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.XY
tooltip.Visible = false
tooltip.Parent = overlay

overlay.Parent = playerGui
```

- Under Sibling, think of the tree: ZIndex sorts brothers and sisters; depth in the tree decides the rest.
- `DisplayOrder` sorts whole ScreenGuis, so the overlay gui wins over every HUD gui with a lower value regardless of their internal ZIndex.
- Switching an existing gui to Global often breaks other layering; moving the overlay out is safer.

answer:
Split it in two pure pieces: the drop index from the pointer's Y inside the list (clamped to the ends), and a `moveItem` that returns a new array with one element moved. The UI just feeds the pointer position in on release and redraws from the returned order.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.Reorder
local Reorder = {}

-- Index (1..count) of the slot under `localY`, measured from the top of the list.
function Reorder.dropIndex(localY: number, rowHeight: number, gap: number, count: number): number
	assert(rowHeight > 0 and count >= 1, "invalid list")
	local index = math.floor(localY / (rowHeight + gap)) + 1
	return math.clamp(index, 1, count)
end

function Reorder.moveItem<T>(list: { T }, from: number, to: number): { T }
	local out: { T } = {}
	local moving = list[from]
	assert(moving ~= nil, "from is out of range")
	for i, value in list do
		if i ~= from then
			out[#out + 1] = value
		end
	end
	local target = math.clamp(to, 1, #out + 1)
	for i = #out, target, -1 do
		out[i + 1] = out[i]
	end
	out[target] = moving
	return out
end

return Reorder
```

```lua
--!strict
-- LocalScript: drives the drag for a loadout list
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
local Reorder = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Reorder"))

local ROW, GAP = 44, 4

local function enableDrag(list: Frame, getOrder: () -> { string }, setOrder: (order: { string }) -> ())
	for _, row in list:GetChildren() do
		if not row:IsA("GuiButton") then
			continue
		end
		local connection = row.MouseButton1Down:Connect(function()
			local from = row.LayoutOrder
			local released: RBXScriptConnection
			released = UserInputService.InputEnded:Connect(function(input: InputObject)
				if input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 and input.UserInputType ~= Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
					return
				end
				released:Disconnect()
				local order = getOrder()
				local pointerY: number = input.Position.Y
				local top: number = list.AbsolutePosition.Y
				setOrder(Reorder.moveItem(order, from, Reorder.dropIndex(pointerY - top, ROW, GAP, #order)))
			end)
		end)
		row.Destroying:Once(function()
			connection:Disconnect()
		end)
	end
end

return enableDrag
```

- `moveItem` never mutates the input, so a cancelled drag simply keeps the old table and nothing is half-updated.
- Clamping the drop index means releasing above the first row or below the last one still lands at an end.
- Rows read their current position from `LayoutOrder`, so after `setOrder` redraws, the next drag uses the new order.
- If the order matters to the server (an equip order), send the new order as a list of item ids and validate that it is a permutation of what the player owns.

answer:
While the dropdown is open, listen to `UserInputService.InputBegan` for mouse and touch presses and test whether the press position lies inside the header or the option list, using their AbsolutePosition and AbsoluteSize. A press outside both closes it. The hit test is a tiny pure function.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.Dropdown
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

local Dropdown = {}

export type Dropdown = {
	open: () -> (),
	close: () -> (),
	isOpen: () -> boolean,
}

function Dropdown.contains(position: Vector2, size: Vector2, point: Vector2): boolean
	local px: number, py: number = point.X, point.Y
	local x: number, y: number = position.X, position.Y
	local w: number, h: number = size.X, size.Y
	return px >= x and px <= x + w and py >= y and py <= y + h
end

local function hit(gui: GuiObject, point: Vector2): boolean
	return gui.Visible and Dropdown.contains(gui.AbsolutePosition, gui.AbsoluteSize, point)
end

function Dropdown.new(header: GuiButton, list: GuiObject): Dropdown
	local outside: RBXScriptConnection? = nil

	local function close()
		list.Visible = false
		if outside then
			outside:Disconnect()
			outside = nil
		end
	end

	local function open()
		list.Visible = true
		if outside then
			return
		end
		outside = UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input: InputObject)
			local kind = input.UserInputType
			if kind ~= Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 and kind ~= Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
				return
			end
			local point = Vector2.new(input.Position.X, input.Position.Y)
			if not hit(list, point) and not hit(header, point) then
				close()
			end
		end)
	end

	header.Activated:Connect(function()
		if list.Visible then
			close()
		else
			open()
		end
	end)

	return {
		open = open,
		close = close,
		isOpen = function()
			return list.Visible
		end,
	}
end

return Dropdown
```

- Presses on the header are ignored by the outside check, so the header's own toggle is not fought by an immediate close.
- `gameProcessedEvent` is not checked on purpose: a press on another button still counts as "outside" and should close the list.
- If the option list sits inside a clipped or scrolling frame, also test against that frame, or presses on clipped-away options would count as inside.

answer:
Measure the text at a candidate size with `TextService:GetTextSize` and binary-search the largest integer size between min and max that fits the label's width. If even the minimum does not fit, set the minimum and turn on truncation. The measuring function is injectable so the fitting logic can be tested on its own.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.FitText
local TextService = game:GetService("TextService")

local FitText = {}

export type Measure = (text: string, size: number) -> number

function FitText.largestSize(text: string, width: number, minSize: number, maxSize: number, measure: Measure): number?
	if measure(text, minSize) > width then
		return nil
	end
	local lo, hi = minSize, maxSize
	while lo < hi do
		local mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
		if measure(text, mid) <= width then
			lo = mid
		else
			hi = mid - 1
		end
	end
	return lo
end

function FitText.apply(label: TextLabel, minSize: number, maxSize: number, measure: Measure?)
	local width: number = label.AbsoluteSize.X
	local font = label.Font
	local measureWith: Measure = measure or function(text: string, size: number): number
		local bounds: Vector2 = TextService:GetTextSize(text, size, font, Vector2.new(math.huge, math.huge))
		return bounds.X
	end
	local size = FitText.largestSize(label.Text, width, minSize, maxSize, measureWith)
	label.TextScaled = false
	label.TextWrapped = false
	label.TextSize = size or minSize
	label.TextTruncate = if size then Enum.TextTruncate.None else Enum.TextTruncate.AtEnd
end

return FitText
```

- Binary search needs only about four measurements for a 10 to 24 range, so it is cheap enough to run when the text changes.
- Re-run `apply` when the label's AbsoluteSize changes, since the width is what decides the size.
- Rich text and FontFace-only fonts measure differently; for those use `TextService:GetTextBoundsAsync` with GetTextBoundsParams in the measure function.

```lua
export type Toolbar = {

	return b
end

function SearchToolbar.build(): Toolbar
	local frame = Instance.new("Frame")
	frame.Name = "Toolbar"
	frame.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 48)
	frame.BackgroundTransparency = 1

	layout.VerticalAlignment = Enum.VerticalAlignment.Center

	back.LayoutOrder = 1

	back.Parent = frame

	search.Text = ""
	search.ClearTextOnFocus = false
```

answer:
`FontFace` takes a `Font` built from a font family plus any weight and style, so one family covers every weight. Define typography roles once (family, weight, size) and apply them by role, so menus never pick fonts directly.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.Typography
local Typography = {}

local FAMILY = "rbxasset://fonts/families/GothamSSm.json"

export type Role = "title" | "heading" | "body" | "caption" | "number"

type Spec = { weight: EnumItem, size: number }

local ROLES: { [Role]: Spec } = {
	title = { weight = Enum.FontWeight.Bold, size = 28 },
	heading = { weight = Enum.FontWeight.SemiBold, size = 20 },
	body = { weight = Enum.FontWeight.Regular, size = 16 },
	caption = { weight = Enum.FontWeight.Regular, size = 13 },
	number = { weight = Enum.FontWeight.Medium, size = 18 },
}

function Typography.font(role: Role): Font
	local spec = ROLES[role]
	return Font.new(FAMILY, spec.weight, Enum.FontStyle.Normal)
end

function Typography.apply(label: TextLabel | TextButton | TextBox, role: Role)
	local spec = ROLES[role]
	label.FontFace = Typography.font(role)
	label.TextSize = spec.size
end

return Typography
```

- Weight is just a field of the Font, so `heading` can move from SemiBold to Bold in one line for the whole game.
- Avoid setting the legacy `Font` property anywhere once you use FontFace; the last one written wins and mixes styles.
- Families are referenced by asset path; one family in the whole UI with two or three weights reads cleaner than several fonts.

answer:
When the menu opens with a gamepad, select its first button through `GuiService.SelectedObject`, and wire `NextSelectionUp`/`NextSelectionDown` explicitly with wrap-around so the cursor never leaves the menu. On close, clear the selection only if it is still inside the menu.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.MenuNavigation
local GuiService = game:GetService("GuiService")

local MenuNavigation = {}

export type Nav = {
	open: (usingGamepad: boolean) -> (),
	close: () -> (),
}

function MenuNavigation.new(menu: GuiObject, buttons: { GuiButton }): Nav
	assert(#buttons > 0, "menu needs at least one button")
	local count = #buttons
	for i, button in buttons do
		button.Selectable = true
		button.NextSelectionUp = buttons[(i - 2) % count + 1]
		button.NextSelectionDown = buttons[i % count + 1]
		-- Left and right point back at the button itself so sideways input cannot escape to the HUD.
		button.NextSelectionLeft = button
		button.NextSelectionRight = button
	end

	local function open(usingGamepad: boolean)
		menu.Visible = true
		if usingGamepad then
			GuiService.SelectedObject = buttons[1]
		end
	end

	local function close()
		menu.Visible = false
		local selected = GuiService.SelectedObject
		if selected ~= nil and selected:IsDescendantOf(menu) then
			GuiService.SelectedObject = nil
		end
	end

	return { open = open, close = close }
end

return MenuNavigation
```

```lua
--!strict
-- LocalScript: wires the pause menu
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
local MenuNavigation = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("MenuNavigation"))

local function isGamepad(inputType: Enum.UserInputType): boolean
	return inputType.Name:sub(1, 7) == "Gamepad"
end

local function setup(menu: Frame, resume: TextButton, settings: TextButton, leave: TextButton)
	local nav = MenuNavigation.new(menu, { resume, settings, leave })
	return function(show: boolean)
		if show then
			nav.open(isGamepad(UserInputService:GetLastInputType()))
		else
			nav.close()
		end
	end
end

return setup
```

- Only selecting with a gamepad avoids the selection highlight appearing for mouse players.
- `(i - 2) % count + 1` is the previous index with wrap-around (1 goes to the last button).
- For grids, set all four `NextSelection*` per cell from row and column math the same way.

answer:
Pick the column count from the container's real width, a minimum cell size and the gap, then divide the remaining width evenly. Keep the math in a pure function and re-run it when the container's AbsoluteSize changes.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.ResponsiveGrid
local ResponsiveGrid = {}

export type Fit = { columns: number, cell: number }

function ResponsiveGrid.fit(width: number, minCell: number, gap: number, maxColumns: number?): Fit
	assert(minCell > 0 and gap >= 0, "invalid grid sizes")
	local columns = math.max(1, math.floor((width + gap) / (minCell + gap)))
	if maxColumns then
		columns = math.min(columns, maxColumns)
	end
	local cell = math.floor((width - gap * (columns - 1)) / columns)
	return { columns = columns, cell = math.max(cell, 0) }
end

function ResponsiveGrid.attach(container: GuiObject, grid: UIGridLayout, minCell: number, gap: number): RBXScriptConnection
	grid.CellPadding = UDim2.fromOffset(gap, gap)
	grid.FillDirectionMaxCells = 0
	local function update()
		local width: number = container.AbsoluteSize.X
		local fit = ResponsiveGrid.fit(width, minCell, gap)
		grid.CellSize = UDim2.fromOffset(fit.cell, fit.cell)
	end
	update()
	return container:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteSize"):Connect(update)
end

return ResponsiveGrid
```

- `(width + gap) / (minCell + gap)` counts one gap fewer than cells, which is how the layout actually places them.
- Flooring the cell size avoids half-pixel cells that blur borders and icons.
- If the container is a ScrollingFrame with a vertical scrollbar, subtract `ScrollBarThickness` from the width first.
- Return value is the connection so the caller can disconnect it when the menu is destroyed.

answer:
Use two bars in a track: the fill snaps to the new fraction, the trail tweens to it after a short delay. Healing moves both up at once, so only losses leave a trail. Colour comes from the fraction through fixed thresholds, and the whole thing listens to `Humanoid.HealthChanged`.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.HealthBar
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local HealthBar = {}

local TRAIL_INFO = TweenInfo.new(0.35, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out, 0, false, 0.25)

function HealthBar.colorFor(fraction: number): Color3
	if fraction <= 0.25 then
		return Color3.fromRGB(214, 60, 60)
	elseif fraction <= 0.5 then
		return Color3.fromRGB(230, 170, 50)
	end
	return Color3.fromRGB(70, 190, 100)
end

function HealthBar.build(): (Frame, Frame, Frame)
	local track = Instance.new("Frame")
	track.Name = "HealthBar"
	track.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(240, 18)
	track.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(30, 32, 38)

	local trail = Instance.new("Frame")
	trail.Name = "Trail"
	trail.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	trail.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(240, 230, 220)
	trail.BorderSizePixel = 0
	trail.Parent = track

	local fill = Instance.new("Frame")
	fill.Name = "Fill"
	fill.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	fill.BorderSizePixel = 0
	fill.ZIndex = 2
	fill.Parent = track

	return track, fill, trail
end

function HealthBar.bind(humanoid: Humanoid, fill: Frame, trail: Frame): RBXScriptConnection
	local trailTween: Tween? = nil

	local function update(health: number)
		local maxHealth: number = humanoid.MaxHealth
		local fraction = if maxHealth > 0 then math.clamp(health / maxHealth, 0, 1) else 0
		local previous: number = fill.Size.X.Scale
		fill.Size = UDim2.fromScale(fraction, 1)
		fill.BackgroundColor3 = HealthBar.colorFor(fraction)
		if trailTween then
			trailTween:Cancel()
			trailTween = nil
		end
		if fraction >= previous then
			trail.Size = UDim2.fromScale(fraction, 1)
		else
			local tween = TweenService:Create(trail, TRAIL_INFO, { Size = UDim2.fromScale(fraction, 1) })
			trailTween = tween
			tween:Play()
		end
	end

	update(humanoid.Health)
	return humanoid.HealthChanged:Connect(update)
end

return HealthBar
```

- The trail tween has a 0.25 s delay, so quick successive hits extend one visible chunk instead of jittering.
- `MaxHealth` is read on every update, so the next health change after a buff shows the right fraction; also connect `humanoid:GetPropertyChangedSignal("MaxHealth")` if buffs can change it without a health change.
- Pair the colour with a number (e.g. "45 / 100") somewhere on the HUD so low health is not signalled by colour alone.

answer:
Track the press start time; while held, a Heartbeat connection fills the bar from elapsed / hold time and fires the action once it reaches 1. Releasing or sliding off the button cancels and empties the bar. The action fires exactly once per hold.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.HoldButton
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local HoldButton = {}

export type Hold = { progress: () -> number, destroy: () -> () }

function HoldButton.attach(button: GuiButton, holdSeconds: number, onConfirm: () -> ()): Hold
	assert(holdSeconds > 0, "holdSeconds must be positive")
	local baseZ: number = button.ZIndex
	local fill = Instance.new("Frame")
	fill.Name = "HoldFill"
	fill.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0, 1)
	fill.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(205, 64, 64)
	fill.BackgroundTransparency = 0.25
	fill.ZIndex = baseZ + 1
	fill.Parent = button

	local progress = 0
	local heartbeat: RBXScriptConnection? = nil

	local function reset()
		if heartbeat then
			heartbeat:Disconnect()
			heartbeat = nil
		end
		progress = 0
		fill.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0, 1)
	end

	local function begin()
		reset()
		local startedAt = os.clock()
		heartbeat = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
			progress = math.min((os.clock() - startedAt) / holdSeconds, 1)
			fill.Size = UDim2.fromScale(progress, 1)
			if progress >= 1 then
				reset()
				onConfirm()
			end
		end)
	end

	local connections = {
		button.MouseButton1Down:Connect(begin),
		button.MouseButton1Up:Connect(reset),
		button.MouseLeave:Connect(reset),
	}

	return {
		progress = function()
			return progress
		end,
		destroy = function()
			reset()
			for _, connection in connections do
				connection:Disconnect()
			end
			fill:Destroy()
		end,
	}
end

return HoldButton
```

- `MouseButton1Down` and `MouseButton1Up` also fire for touch, so the same code works on phones.
- Resetting before calling `onConfirm` means a slow handler cannot be triggered twice by the same hold.
- Show the hold time on the label ("Hold to delete") so players know a tap will not work.
- The server still checks that the player owns the pet before deleting it.

InputBegan passes a second argument, `gameProcessedEvent`, which is true when the engine already used the input (typing in chat or any TextBox, clicking a core button). Return early when it is set. While at it, accept the controller's Y button so the hotkey works on console too.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: StarterPlayerScripts.InventoryHotkey
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

local InventoryHotkey = {}

local KEYS = {
	[Enum.KeyCode.I] = true,
	[Enum.KeyCode.ButtonY] = true,
}

function InventoryHotkey.bind(inventory: GuiObject): RBXScriptConnection
	return UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input: InputObject, gameProcessedEvent: boolean)
		if gameProcessedEvent then
			return
		end
		if KEYS[input.KeyCode] then
			local visible: boolean = inventory.Visible
			inventory.Visible = not visible
		end
	end)
end

return InventoryHotkey
```

- `gameProcessedEvent` also covers your own TextBoxes, such as a search field inside the inventory, so typing "i" there no longer closes it.
- A lookup table of keys keeps rebinding in one place; add `Enum.KeyCode.Tab` or similar without touching the handler.
- For actions that should also get a mobile button, ContextActionService is the better fit; for a plain toggle this is enough.

answer:
The `task.wait` version cannot tell that the mouse left. Bump a per-button counter on every enter and leave, and when the delay ends, show the tooltip only if the counter still matches the value from that enter. Once one tooltip is showing, moving to a neighbour can show the next one immediately, which is how desktop toolbars feel.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.HoverTips
local HoverTips = {}

export type Tips = { attach: (button: GuiButton, text: string) -> () }

function HoverTips.new(tooltip: TextLabel, delaySeconds: number?): Tips
	local hoverDelay = delaySeconds or 0.4
	local generation = 0
	local warm = false
	local hovered: GuiButton? = nil

	local function hide()
		generation += 1
		tooltip.Visible = false
		local mine = generation
		task.delay(0.15, function()
			if mine == generation then
				warm = false
			end
		end)
	end

	local function attach(button: GuiButton, text: string)
		button.MouseEnter:Connect(function()
			hovered = button
			generation += 1
			local mine = generation
			local function show()
				if mine == generation then
					tooltip.Text = text
					tooltip.Visible = true
					warm = true
				end
			end
			if warm then
				show()
			else
				task.delay(hoverDelay, show)
			end
		end)
		button.MouseLeave:Connect(function()
			-- MouseLeave of the old button can arrive after MouseEnter of the next one; ignore it then.
			if hovered == button then
				hovered = nil
				hide()
			end
		end)
	end

	return { attach = attach }
end

return HoverTips
```

- The shared generation counter means any newer enter or leave invalidates older pending shows, across all buttons.
- Tracking which button is hovered makes a late MouseLeave from the previous button harmless.
- "Warm" mode lasts 0.15 s after leaving, enough to cross the gap between buttons without restarting the delay.
- Touch has no hover; show the same text on long-press (`TouchLongPress`) for mobile players.

answer:
Map every `UserInputType` to one of three families (keyboard and mouse, gamepad, touch), listen to `UserInputService.LastInputTypeChanged`, and only update labels when the family actually changes. Mouse movement and focus events then do not cause flicker.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.InputHints
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

local InputHints = {}

export type Family = "keyboard" | "gamepad" | "touch"

function InputHints.familyOf(inputType: Enum.UserInputType): Family?
	if inputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
		return "touch"
	elseif string.sub(inputType.Name, 1, 7) == "Gamepad" then
		return "gamepad"
	elseif inputType == Enum.UserInputType.Keyboard
		or inputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1
		or inputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton2
		or inputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseMovement
		or inputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseWheel then
		return "keyboard"
	end
	return nil
end

local HINTS: { [Family]: string } = {
	keyboard = "Press E to open",
	gamepad = "Press X to open",
	touch = "Tap to open",
}

function InputHints.bind(label: TextLabel): RBXScriptConnection
	local current: Family = InputHints.familyOf(UserInputService:GetLastInputType()) or "keyboard"
	label.Text = HINTS[current]
	return UserInputService.LastInputTypeChanged:Connect(function(inputType: Enum.UserInputType)
		local family = InputHints.familyOf(inputType)
		if family ~= nil and family ~= current then
			current = family
			label.Text = HINTS[current]
		end
	end)
end

return InputHints
```

- Types such as `Focus`, `Gyro` and `TextInput` return nil and are ignored, so alt-tabbing does not reset a controller player to keyboard hints.
- Keep the key in one place: if the interact key changes, edit the hint table together with the binding.
- ProximityPrompts already switch their own glyphs; use this for your custom hints and tutorials.

answer:
Keep one row per player keyed by UserId, update its text in place, and let the UIListLayout order rows by `LayoutOrder` set to the rank. Rows for players that are gone are destroyed. Sorting uses a deterministic tie-break so equal scores do not swap places every update.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.Scoreboard
local Scoreboard = {}

export type Entry = { userId: number, name: string, score: number }
export type Board = {
	update: (entries: { Entry }) -> (),
	rowFor: (userId: number) -> TextLabel?,
}

function Scoreboard.rank(entries: { Entry }): { Entry }
	local sorted: { Entry } = {}
	for i, entry in entries do
		sorted[i] = entry
	end
	table.sort(sorted, function(a: Entry, b: Entry): boolean
		if a.score ~= b.score then
			return a.score > b.score
		end
		return a.userId < b.userId
	end)
	return sorted
end

function Scoreboard.new(list: GuiObject): Board
	local rows: { [number]: TextLabel } = {}

	local layout = Instance.new("UIListLayout")
	layout.SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder
	layout.Padding = UDim.new(0, 2)
	layout.Parent = list

	local function update(entries: { Entry })
		local seen: { [number]: boolean } = {}
		for rank, entry in Scoreboard.rank(entries) do
			seen[entry.userId] = true
			local row = rows[entry.userId]
			if row == nil then
				local newRow = Instance.new("TextLabel")
				newRow.Name = tostring(entry.userId)
				newRow.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 28)
				newRow.BackgroundTransparency = 1
				newRow.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
				newRow.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(235, 235, 240)
				newRow.TextSize = 16
				newRow.Parent = list
				rows[entry.userId] = newRow
				row = newRow
			end
			assert(row)
			row.LayoutOrder = rank
			row.Text = string.format("%d. %s  %d", rank, entry.name, entry.score)
		end
		for userId, row in rows do
			if not seen[userId] then
				row:Destroy()
				rows[userId] = nil
			end
		end
	end

	return {
		update = update,
		rowFor = function(userId: number): TextLabel?
			return rows[userId]
		end,
	}
end

return Scoreboard
```

- Rows are never recreated for existing players, so nothing flickers and a row being hovered keeps its state.
- Ties fall back to UserId; any stable key works, the point is that equal scores do not shuffle between updates.
- Removing entries while iterating with `pairs`-style generalised iteration is allowed for the current key, which is what the cleanup loop does.

answer:
Keep a `following` flag that is re-evaluated whenever the player scrolls: true while the view is at the bottom (within a small tolerance). When the canvas size changes after a new line is laid out, scroll to the new bottom only if the flag is set. The decision is a pure function of canvas position, window height and canvas height.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.StickyLog
local StickyLog = {}

local TOLERANCE = 4

function StickyLog.atBottom(scrollY: number, windowHeight: number, canvasHeight: number): boolean
	return scrollY + windowHeight >= canvasHeight - TOLERANCE
end

function StickyLog.bottomOffset(windowHeight: number, canvasHeight: number): number
	return math.max(0, canvasHeight - windowHeight)
end

export type Log = { push: (text: string) -> (), destroy: () -> () }

function StickyLog.new(scroller: ScrollingFrame, maxLines: number): Log
	local count = 0
	local lines: { TextLabel } = {}

	local function measure(): (number, number, number)
		local y: number = scroller.CanvasPosition.Y
		local window: number = scroller.AbsoluteWindowSize.Y
		local canvas: number = scroller.AbsoluteCanvasSize.Y
		return y, window, canvas
	end

	local following = StickyLog.atBottom(measure())

	local function scrollToBottom()
		local _, window, canvas = measure()
		scroller.CanvasPosition = Vector2.new(0, StickyLog.bottomOffset(window, canvas))
	end

	local connections = {
		-- Player scrolling (and our own scrollToBottom) decides whether new lines are followed.
		scroller:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CanvasPosition"):Connect(function()
			following = StickyLog.atBottom(measure())
		end),
		-- AbsoluteCanvasSize changes after the layout pass, so react to it instead of guessing when it is ready.
		scroller:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteCanvasSize"):Connect(function()
			if following then
				scrollToBottom()
			end
		end),
	}

	local function push(text: string)
		count += 1
		local line = Instance.new("TextLabel")
		line.Name = "Line"
		line.LayoutOrder = count
		line.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 20)
		line.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		line.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
		line.TextSize = 15
		line.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(225, 225, 230)
		line.Text = text
		line.Parent = scroller
		table.insert(lines, line)
		if #lines > maxLines then
			local oldest = lines[1]
			for i = 1, #lines do
				lines[i] = lines[i + 1]
			end
			oldest:Destroy()
		end
	end

	local function destroy()
		for _, connection in connections do
			connection:Disconnect()
		end
	end

	return { push = push, destroy = destroy }
end

return StickyLog
```

- The scroller needs a UIListLayout sorted by LayoutOrder and `AutomaticCanvasSize = Y`.
- Capping the log at `maxLines` keeps a long fight from creating thousands of labels.
- The 4 px tolerance absorbs sub-pixel scroll positions on touch devices, where "at the bottom" is rarely exact.

answer:
Build the modal as one root frame holding a full-screen backdrop button and a centred panel. Bind ButtonB at high priority only while the modal is open, under an action name unique to that modal, and sink it so nothing underneath also reacts; every close path goes through one idempotent `close`.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.Modal
local ContextActionService = game:GetService("ContextActionService")
local GuiService = game:GetService("GuiService")

local Modal = {}

export type Handle = {
	root: Frame,
	close: () -> (),
	isOpen: () -> boolean,
}

local ACTION_PREFIX = "CloseModal"
local opened = 0

local function makeLabel(text: string, size: UDim2, position: UDim2, textSize: number): TextLabel
	local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	label.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	label.Size = size
	label.Position = position
	label.TextSize = textSize
	label.TextWrapped = true
	label.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(236, 236, 240)
	label.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left
	label.Text = text
	return label
end

function Modal.open(screenGui: ScreenGui, title: string, body: string, onClose: (() -> ())?): Handle
	local open = true
	opened += 1
	-- One name per modal: with a shared name, closing a stacked modal would unbind the one still open.
	local action = ACTION_PREFIX .. opened
	local previousSelection = GuiService.SelectedObject
	local connections: { RBXScriptConnection } = {}

	local root = Instance.new("Frame")
	root.Name = "Modal"
	root.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	root.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	root.ZIndex = 50

	-- A button, not a Frame, so clicks land here instead of on the HUD below.
	local backdrop = Instance.new("TextButton")
	backdrop.Name = "Backdrop"
	backdrop.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	backdrop.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.new(0, 0, 0)
	backdrop.BackgroundTransparency = 0.45
	backdrop.AutoButtonColor = false
	backdrop.Selectable = false
	backdrop.Text = ""
	backdrop.Parent = root

	local panel = Instance.new("Frame")
	panel.Name = "Panel"
	panel.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
	panel.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
	panel.Size = UDim2.new(0.4, 0, 0, 200)
	panel.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(32, 34, 40)
	panel.Parent = root

	makeLabel(title, UDim2.new(1, -32, 0, 28), UDim2.fromOffset(16, 14), 22).Parent = panel
	makeLabel(body, UDim2.new(1, -32, 1, -110), UDim2.fromOffset(16, 50), 16).Parent = panel

	local closeButton = Instance.new("TextButton")
	closeButton.Name = "Close"
	closeButton.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 1)
	closeButton.Position = UDim2.new(1, -16, 1, -16)
	closeButton.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(110, 40)
	closeButton.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(58, 62, 72)
	closeButton.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(240, 240, 240)
	closeButton.TextSize = 18
	closeButton.Text = "Close"
	closeButton.Parent = panel

	local function close()
		if not open then
			return
		end
		open = false
		ContextActionService:UnbindAction(action)
		for _, connection in connections do
			connection:Disconnect()
		end
		root:Destroy()
		if previousSelection ~= nil and previousSelection.Parent ~= nil then
			GuiService.SelectedObject = previousSelection
		else
			GuiService.SelectedObject = nil
		end
		if onClose then
			onClose()
		end
	end

	local function onBack(_action: string, state: Enum.UserInputState, _input: InputObject): Enum.ContextActionResult
		if state ~= Enum.UserInputState.Begin then
			return Enum.ContextActionResult.Pass
		end
		close()
		return Enum.ContextActionResult.Sink
	end

	connections = { backdrop.Activated:Connect(close), closeButton.Activated:Connect(close) }
	ContextActionService:BindActionAtPriority(action, onBack, false, Enum.ContextActionPriority.High.Value, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonB)

	root.Parent = screenGui
	GuiService.SelectedObject = closeButton

	return {
		root = root,
		close = close,
		isOpen = function()
			return open
		end,
	}
end

return Modal
```

- Give the modal's ScreenGui a higher `DisplayOrder` than the HUD so it draws on top regardless of creation order.
- Escape belongs to the Roblox menu, so keyboard players close with the button or the backdrop; ButtonB is the console convention for "back".
- A stacked modal binds after the one below it at the same priority, so B closes the top one first; each modal unbinds only its own action.
- Returning `Pass` for the release keeps the binding from swallowing input it did not use.
- Restoring the old selection only if it still exists avoids pointing the gamepad at a destroyed button.

answer:
If the point is on screen and in front, use it directly. Otherwise take the direction from the screen centre to the projected point (flipped when the point is behind the camera), and scale that direction until it touches a rectangle inset from the edges. The angle of the direction rotates the arrow.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.EdgeMarker
local EdgeMarker = {}

export type Placement = { position: Vector2, onScreen: boolean, angle: number }

function EdgeMarker.place(projected: Vector2, inFront: boolean, screen: Vector2, margin: number): Placement
	local px: number, py: number = projected.X, projected.Y
	local sw: number, sh: number = screen.X, screen.Y
	local inside = px >= margin and px <= sw - margin and py >= margin and py <= sh - margin
	if inFront and inside then
		return { position = Vector2.new(px, py), onScreen = true, angle = 0 }
	end
	local cx, cy = sw / 2, sh / 2
	local dx, dy = px - cx, py - cy
	if not inFront then
		dx, dy = -dx, -dy
	end
	if dx == 0 and dy == 0 then
		dy = 1
	end
	local halfW, halfH = cx - margin, cy - margin
	local scale = math.min(halfW / math.max(math.abs(dx), 1e-6), halfH / math.max(math.abs(dy), 1e-6))
	return {
		position = Vector2.new(cx + dx * scale, cy + dy * scale),
		onScreen = false,
		angle = math.deg(math.atan2(dy, dx)),
	}
end

return EdgeMarker
```

```lua
--!strict
-- LocalScript: drives the marker every frame
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local EdgeMarker = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("EdgeMarker"))

local function track(marker: ImageLabel, target: BasePart)
	return RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(function()

return track
```

- `WorldToViewportPoint` mirrors points behind the camera, which is why the direction is flipped when `inFront` is false.

answer:
Keep the page as a number and derive everything else: page count from the total, the slice for the current page, and the button states. Clamp the page whenever the data changes, so a shrinking list can never leave the player on a page that no longer exists.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.Pager
local Pager = {}

export type Pager = {
	setItems: (items: { string }) -> (),
	go: (delta: number) -> (),
	page: () -> number,
}

function Pager.pageCount(total: number, perPage: number): number
	return math.max(1, math.ceil(total / perPage))
end

function Pager.slice(items: { string }, page: number, perPage: number): { string }
	local out = {}
	for i = (page - 1) * perPage + 1, math.min(#items, page * perPage) do
		table.insert(out, items[i])
	end
	return out
end

local function setEnabled(button: GuiButton, enabled: boolean)
	button.Interactable = enabled
	button.BackgroundTransparency = if enabled then 0 else 0.6
end

function Pager.new(perPage: number, prev: GuiButton, nextButton: GuiButton, label: TextLabel, render: (pageItems: { string }) -> ()): Pager
	local items: { string } = {}
	local page = 1

	local function refresh()
		local count = Pager.pageCount(#items, perPage)
		page = math.clamp(page, 1, count)
		label.Text = string.format("Page %d of %d", page, count)
		setEnabled(prev, page > 1)
		setEnabled(nextButton, page < count)
		render(Pager.slice(items, page, perPage))
	end

	local function go(delta: number)
		page += delta
		refresh()
	end

	prev.Activated:Connect(function()
		go(-1)
	end)
	nextButton.Activated:Connect(function()
		go(1)
	end)

	return {
		setItems = function(newItems: { string })
			items = newItems
			refresh()
		end,
		go = go,
		page = function()
			return page
		end,
	}
end

return Pager
```

- `Interactable = false` stops clicks and gamepad activation; the faded background tells players why.
- An empty list still reports "Page 1 of 1", which reads better than "Page 1 of 0".
- Fetch pages from the server lazily if the full listing is large; the same clamp applies to the server's total.

answer:
Drive the ScrollingFrame's height from its UIListLayout's `AbsoluteContentSize`: height = min(content, max). The canvas height always matches the content, so scrolling only kicks in once the cap is reached. One small function, re-run whenever the content size changes.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.GrowingList
local GrowingList = {}

function GrowingList.heightFor(contentHeight: number, padding: number, maxHeight: number): number
	return math.min(contentHeight + padding, maxHeight)
end

function GrowingList.bind(scroller: ScrollingFrame, layout: UIListLayout, maxHeight: number, padding: number?): RBXScriptConnection
	local pad = padding or 0
	scroller.AutomaticCanvasSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.None
	scroller.ScrollingDirection = Enum.ScrollingDirection.Y

	local function update()
		local content: number = layout.AbsoluteContentSize.Y
		local height = GrowingList.heightFor(content, pad, maxHeight)
		scroller.Size = UDim2.new(scroller.Size.X.Scale, scroller.Size.X.Offset, 0, height)
		scroller.CanvasSize = UDim2.fromOffset(0, content + pad)
		scroller.ScrollBarThickness = if content + pad > maxHeight then 6 else 0
	end

	update()
	return layout:GetPropertyChangedSignal("AbsoluteContentSize"):Connect(update)
end

return GrowingList
```

- `padding` is the sum of the frame's top and bottom UIPadding, which AbsoluteContentSize does not include.
- Hiding the scrollbar until it is needed stops a scrollbar appearing on a list that fits.
- Width is preserved from the existing Size, so the panel's horizontal layout is untouched.
