answer:
Use collision groups on the server: each team gets a player group and a door group, and a team's players do not collide with their own team's door. Character parts are assigned to their team's group on spawn and again whenever the player switches teams. That makes the door work for every honest player, but each client simulates its own character, so an exploiter can still noclip through; a server check of the room behind each door catches that.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.TeamDoors
local PhysicsService = game:GetService("PhysicsService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local TeamDoors = {}

local function register(name: string)
	if not PhysicsService:IsCollisionGroupRegistered(name) then
		PhysicsService:RegisterCollisionGroup(name)
	end
end

function TeamDoors.groupFor(team: Team?): string
	return if team then "Players_" .. team.Name else "Default"
end

function TeamDoors.setup(teams: { Team }, doors: { [Team]: { BasePart } })
	for _, team in teams do
		register("Players_" .. team.Name)
		register("Door_" .. team.Name)
	end
	for _, team in teams do
		for _, other in teams do
			PhysicsService:CollisionGroupSetCollidable("Players_" .. team.Name, "Door_" .. other.Name, team ~= other)
		end
		for _, door in doors[team] or {} do
			door.CollisionGroup = "Door_" .. team.Name
		end
	end
end

function TeamDoors.applyCharacter(player: Player)
	local character = player.Character
	if character == nil then
		return
	end
	local group = TeamDoors.groupFor(player.Team)
	for _, part in character:GetDescendants() do
		if part:IsA("BasePart") then
			part.CollisionGroup = group
		end
	end
end

-- Server-side enforcement: anyone not on `team` whose root is inside the `room` box is sent to `exit`.
function TeamDoors.enforce(team: Team, room: BasePart, exit: CFrame): number
	local moved = 0
	local half = room.Size / 2
	for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
		local character = player.Character
		local root = if character then character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") else nil
		if character and root and player.Team ~= team then
			local offset = room.CFrame:PointToObjectSpace(root.Position)
			if math.abs(offset.X) <= half.X and math.abs(offset.Y) <= half.Y and math.abs(offset.Z) <= half.Z then
				character:PivotTo(exit)
				moved += 1
			end
		end
	end
	return moved
end

function TeamDoors.track(player: Player)
	player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function()
		TeamDoors.applyCharacter(player)
	end)
	player:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Team"):Connect(function()
		TeamDoors.applyCharacter(player)
	end)
	TeamDoors.applyCharacter(player)
end

function TeamDoors.trackAll()
	Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(TeamDoors.track)
	for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
		TeamDoors.track(player)
	end
end

return TeamDoors
```

Setup on the server: `TeamDoors.setup({ Teams.Red, Teams.Blue }, { [Teams.Red] = { workspace.RedBase.Door }, [Teams.Blue] = { workspace.BlueBase.Door } })`, then `TeamDoors.trackAll()`, then a loop that calls `TeamDoors.enforce(Teams.Red, workspace.RedBase.Inside, workspace.RedBase.Outside.CFrame)` (and the same for Blue) every half second. `Inside` is an invisible, non-colliding box covering the room.

- The groups replicate, so honest clients get the right collisions without any LocalScript. They do not stop a cheater: the player's client owns its character's physics and the server accepts the positions it reports, which is why `enforce` checks the room on the server.
- Re-applying on `Team` changes covers team switches mid-life; on respawn the new character is assigned right away.
- Accessories and tools added after spawning keep the Default group; if they matter for collisions, also handle `character.DescendantAdded`.
request: Each team has a base with a door only that team can walk through. I tried making the door CanCollide false on the client for team members, but exploiters just do that for every door. How do I make team-only doors properly?

answer:
Drive the clock from elapsed time on the server (so lag never slows the day), write `ClockTime` only when it has moved a game minute, and switch the lamps once per dusk/dawn transition from one place. Lamps that stream in or get built later are set to the current state through the tag's added signal.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.DayNightCycle
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local Lighting = game:GetService("Lighting")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local LAMP_TAG = "StreetLamp"
local MINUTE = 1 / 60

export type Cycle = {
	stopCycle: () -> (),
	isNight: () -> boolean,
}

local DayNightCycle = {}

function DayNightCycle.clockAt(elapsed: number, dayLength: number, startClock: number): number
	return (startClock + elapsed / dayLength * 24) % 24
end

function DayNightCycle.isNightAt(clock: number, dusk: number, dawn: number): boolean
	return clock >= dusk or clock < dawn
end

local function setLamp(lamp: Instance, on: boolean)
	for _, descendant in lamp:GetDescendants() do
		if descendant:IsA("Light") then
			descendant.Enabled = on
		end
	end
end

function DayNightCycle.start(dayLength: number, startClock: number, dusk: number, dawn: number): Cycle
	local elapsed = 0
	local night = DayNightCycle.isNightAt(startClock, dusk, dawn)
	Lighting.ClockTime = startClock
	for _, lamp in CollectionService:GetTagged(LAMP_TAG) do
		setLamp(lamp, night)
	end

	local added = CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(LAMP_TAG):Connect(function(lamp: Instance)
		setLamp(lamp, night)
	end)

	local heartbeat = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt: number)
		elapsed += dt
		local clock = DayNightCycle.clockAt(elapsed, dayLength, startClock)
		-- Writing every frame would replicate 60 property changes a second for no visible gain.
		if math.abs(clock - Lighting.ClockTime) >= MINUTE then
			Lighting.ClockTime = clock
		end
		local nowNight = DayNightCycle.isNightAt(clock, dusk, dawn)
		if nowNight ~= night then
			night = nowNight
			for _, lamp in CollectionService:GetTagged(LAMP_TAG) do
				setLamp(lamp, night)
			end
		end
	end)

	return {
		stopCycle = function()
			added:Disconnect()
			heartbeat:Disconnect()
		end,
		isNight = function(): boolean
			return night
		end,
	}
end

return DayNightCycle
```

Starting it from a server Script: `DayNightCycle.start(20 * 60, 8, 18, 6)` (20-minute days, starting at 8 AM, lamps on from 18:00 to 06:00).

- Time comes from accumulated `dt`, so a server hitch skips ahead instead of stretching the day.
- The `% 24` wrap means the clock passes midnight cleanly; the `abs` check against the current value also handles the wrap because the jump from 23.99 to 0 is larger than a minute.
- One loop over tagged lamps twice per day replaces hundreds of per-lamp scripts polling the clock.
- If clients need smoother sun motion than one-minute steps, tween `ClockTime` locally between server updates.

answer:
Run one lightweight loop per light on the client: each step either holds near full brightness for a while or drops out briefly, chosen with that light's own `Random`. The loop exits when the light leaves the game or when the returned stop function is called, and restores the original brightness when stopped.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.LightFlicker
local LightFlicker = {}

function LightFlicker.start(light: Light, seed: number, dropoutChance: number?): () -> ()
	local base = light.Brightness
	local chance = dropoutChance or 0.15
	local random = Random.new(seed)
	local running = true

	task.spawn(function()
		while running and light.Parent ~= nil do
			if random:NextNumber() < chance then
				light.Brightness = base * random:NextNumber(0, 0.25)
				task.wait(random:NextNumber(0.04, 0.12))
			else
				light.Brightness = base * random:NextNumber(0.85, 1)
				task.wait(random:NextNumber(0.15, 0.6))
			end
		end
		if light.Parent ~= nil then
			light.Brightness = base
		end
	end)

	return function()
		running = false
	end
end

return LightFlicker
```

Starting every tagged light with its own seed, in a LocalScript:

```lua
--!strict
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local LightFlicker = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("LightFlicker"))

local stops: { [Instance]: () -> () } = {}

local function onAdded(light: Instance)
	if light:IsA("Light") then
		stops[light] = LightFlicker.start(light, math.random(1, 1e6))
	end
end

CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal("FlickerLight"):Connect(onAdded)
CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal("FlickerLight"):Connect(function(light: Instance)
	local stop = stops[light]
	if stop then
		stop()
		stops[light] = nil
	end
end)
for _, light in CollectionService:GetTagged("FlickerLight") do
	onAdded(light)
end
```

- Per-light seeds keep neighbouring lights out of sync, which reads far more natural than one shared pattern.
- The loop yields every step, so dozens of flickering lights cost a handful of property writes per second each.
- Doing it on the client keeps the server from replicating brightness changes; every player sees a different flicker, which is fine for ambience.

answer:
Poll instead of relying on touch events: a few times per second, find which zone contains the camera subject's position. Containment is a local-space box test (so rotated zones work), and when zones are nested the smallest containing one wins. The callback fires only when the zone actually changes.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.InteriorZones
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")

local InteriorZones = {}

function InteriorZones.contains(zone: BasePart, point: Vector3): boolean
	local localPoint = zone.CFrame:PointToObjectSpace(point)
	local half = zone.Size / 2
	return math.abs(localPoint.X) <= half.X and math.abs(localPoint.Y) <= half.Y and math.abs(localPoint.Z) <= half.Z
end

function InteriorZones.zoneAt(point: Vector3, zones: { Instance }): BasePart?
	local best: BasePart? = nil
	local bestVolume = math.huge
	for _, zone in zones do
		if zone:IsA("BasePart") and InteriorZones.contains(zone, point) then
			local volume = zone.Size.X * zone.Size.Y * zone.Size.Z
			if volume < bestVolume then
				best, bestVolume = zone, volume
			end
		end
	end
	return best
end

function InteriorZones.track(tag: string, getPoint: () -> Vector3?, onChange: (zone: BasePart?) -> (), interval: number?): () -> ()
	local running = true
	local current: BasePart? = nil
	task.spawn(function()
		while running do
			local point = getPoint()
			local zone = if point then InteriorZones.zoneAt(point, CollectionService:GetTagged(tag)) else nil
			if zone ~= current then
				current = zone
				onChange(zone)
			end
			task.wait(interval or 0.25)
		end
	end)
	return function()
		running = false
	end
end

return InteriorZones
```

answer:
Describe each preset as property tables per object (Lighting, Atmosphere, BloomEffect), make sure those objects exist, and tween each table with one TweenInfo. Cancel the running tweens before starting new ones so a quick weather change blends from wherever the scene currently is.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.LightingPresets
local Lighting = game:GetService("Lighting")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

export type Preset = {
	lighting: { [string]: any },
	atmosphere: { [string]: any },
	bloom: { [string]: any },
}

local LightingPresets = {}

LightingPresets.presets = {
	Clear = {
		lighting = { Brightness = 3, Ambient = Color3.fromRGB(110, 110, 120), ExposureCompensation = 0 },
		atmosphere = { Density = 0.3, Haze = 0.5, Color = Color3.fromRGB(199, 210, 225) },
		bloom = { Intensity = 0.4, Threshold = 1.2 },
	},
	Sunset = {
		lighting = { Brightness = 2, Ambient = Color3.fromRGB(120, 85, 70), ExposureCompensation = 0.2 },
		atmosphere = { Density = 0.38, Haze = 2, Color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 170, 120) },
		bloom = { Intensity = 0.8, Threshold = 0.9 },
	},
	Storm = {
		lighting = { Brightness = 0.8, Ambient = Color3.fromRGB(60, 65, 75), ExposureCompensation = -0.4 },
		atmosphere = { Density = 0.55, Haze = 3, Color = Color3.fromRGB(120, 125, 135) },
		bloom = { Intensity = 0.2, Threshold = 1.5 },
	},
} :: { [string]: Preset }

local active: { Tween } = {}

local function ensure(className: string): Instance
	local existing = Lighting:FindFirstChildOfClass(className)
	if existing then
		return existing
	end
	local created = Instance.new(className)
	created.Parent = Lighting
	return created
end

function LightingPresets.apply(name: string, duration: number): { Tween }
	local preset = LightingPresets.presets[name]
	assert(preset, string.format("unknown lighting preset %s", name))
	for _, tween in active do
		tween:Cancel()
	end
	local info = TweenInfo.new(duration, Enum.EasingStyle.Sine, Enum.EasingDirection.InOut)
	active = {
		TweenService:Create(Lighting, info, preset.lighting),
		TweenService:Create(ensure("Atmosphere"), info, preset.atmosphere),
		TweenService:Create(ensure("BloomEffect"), info, preset.bloom),
	}
	for _, tween in active do
		tween:Play()
	end
	return active
end

return LightingPresets
```

- Tweens start from the current property values, so cancelling and starting a new set mid-blend continues smoothly from the half-blended look.
- Keep `ClockTime` out of presets: tweening it from 23 to 1 goes the long way round through the whole day; drive time separately.
- Run this on the client when the server announces the weather (an attribute on ReplicatedStorage works well), so each player gets smooth frames and the server sends one value.

answer:
`Path.Blocked` fires with the index of the waypoint that became blocked. If that index is still ahead of the NPC, abandon the current walk and compute a new path from where it stands. A replan limit stops an NPC from spinning forever when the goal is truly unreachable.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.ReplanningWalker
local PathfindingService = game:GetService("PathfindingService")

export type Outcome = "Reached" | "Unreachable" | "Stuck"
export type Walker = {
	goTo: (goal: Vector3) -> Outcome,
	currentPath: () -> Path?,
	replans: () -> number,
}

local MAX_REPLANS = 5
local STEP_TIMEOUT = 4

local ReplanningWalker = {}

function ReplanningWalker.new(humanoid: Humanoid, root: BasePart, agent: { [string]: any }): Walker
	local path: Path? = nil
	local replanCount = 0

	-- Walks one computed path. Returns "Reached", "Blocked" or "Stuck".
	local function follow(current: Path): string
		local waypoints = current:GetWaypoints()
		local index = 2
		local thread = coroutine.running()
		local waiting = false
		local function wake(signal: string)
			if waiting then
				waiting = false
				task.spawn(thread, signal)
			end
		end
		local blocked = current.Blocked:Connect(function(blockedIndex: number)
			if blockedIndex >= index then
				wake("blocked")
			end
		end)
		local finished = humanoid.MoveToFinished:Connect(function(reached: boolean)
			wake(if reached then "moved" else "failed")
		end)

		local outcome = "Reached"
		while index <= #waypoints do
			humanoid:MoveTo(waypoints[index].Position)
			waiting = true
			local myStep = index
			task.delay(STEP_TIMEOUT, function()
				if index == myStep then
					wake("failed")
				end
			end)
			local signal = coroutine.yield()
			if signal == "blocked" then
				outcome = "Blocked"
				break
			elseif signal ~= "moved" then
				outcome = "Stuck"
				break
			end
			index += 1
		end
		waiting = false
		blocked:Disconnect()
		finished:Disconnect()
		return outcome
	end

	local function goTo(goal: Vector3): Outcome
		replanCount = 0
		while replanCount <= MAX_REPLANS do
			local newPath = PathfindingService:CreatePath(agent)
			local ok = pcall(function()
				newPath:ComputeAsync(root.Position, goal)
			end)
			if not ok or newPath.Status ~= Enum.PathStatus.Success then
				return "Unreachable"
			end
			path = newPath
			local result = follow(newPath)
			if result ~= "Blocked" then
				return if result == "Reached" then "Reached" else "Stuck"
			end
			replanCount += 1
		end
		return "Unreachable"
	end

	return {
		goTo = goTo,
		currentPath = function(): Path?
			return path
		end,
		replans = function(): number
			return replanCount
		end,
	}
end

return ReplanningWalker
```

- Blocks behind the NPC (an index it already passed) are ignored; only obstacles on the remaining route trigger a replan.
- Each replan starts from `root.Position`, so the new path begins where the NPC actually is, not where the old path started.
- Closed doors should be parts the pathfinder treats as obstacles (CanCollide on, or a PathfindingModifier with `PassThrough` off) so the new path routes around them.
- Call `goTo` from its own thread per NPC (`task.spawn`) because it yields while walking.
request: Doors in my map close on a timer, and NPCs that already computed a path walk straight into a closed door and stand there. I know `Path.Blocked` exists but I don't understand how to use it to recompute.

answer:
Mix two modes. When the zombie can see the target with nothing in between, skip pathfinding and `MoveTo` the target directly every update. Only when the view is blocked, compute a path, and recompute only if the target has moved far from the old goal or the path is getting old. Between recomputes the zombie keeps walking its current waypoints.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.Chaser
local PathfindingService = game:GetService("PathfindingService")

export type Options = { repathDistance: number, repathInterval: number, sightRange: number }
export type Mode = "Direct" | "Path" | "Idle"
export type Chaser = {
	update: (target: BasePart) -> Mode,
	pathsComputed: () -> number,
}

local Chaser = {}

function Chaser.new(npc: Model, options: Options): Chaser
	local humanoid = npc:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	local root = npc:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	assert(humanoid and root and root:IsA("BasePart"), "NPC needs a Humanoid and HumanoidRootPart")

	local path = PathfindingService:CreatePath({ AgentRadius = 2, AgentHeight = 5, AgentCanJump = true })
	local waypoints: { PathWaypoint } = {}
	local waypointIndex = 0
	local lastGoal: Vector3? = nil
	local lastPathAt = -math.huge
	local lastFailed = false
	local computed = 0

	local function canSee(target: BasePart): boolean
		local offset = target.Position - root.Position
		if offset.Magnitude > options.sightRange or math.abs(offset.Y) > 6 then
			return false
		end
		local params = RaycastParams.new()
		params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
		params.FilterDescendantsInstances = { npc, target.Parent or target }
		return workspace:Raycast(root.Position, offset, params) == nil
	end

	local function repath(goal: Vector3)
		lastGoal = goal
		lastPathAt = os.clock()
		computed += 1
		local ok = pcall(function()
			path:ComputeAsync(root.Position, goal)
		end)
		lastFailed = not (ok and path.Status == Enum.PathStatus.Success)
		waypoints = if lastFailed then {} else path:GetWaypoints()
		waypointIndex = 2
	end

	local function update(target: BasePart): Mode
		if humanoid.Health <= 0 then
			return "Idle"
		end
		if canSee(target) then
			waypoints = {}
			lastFailed = false
			humanoid:MoveTo(target.Position)
			return "Direct"
		end
		local stale = os.clock() - lastPathAt > options.repathInterval
		local moved = lastGoal == nil or (target.Position - lastGoal).Magnitude > options.repathDistance
		-- An unreachable target (no waypoints after a failed compute) is retried once per interval, not every update.
		local needPath = if #waypoints == 0 then not lastFailed or stale else stale and moved
		if needPath then
			repath(target.Position)
		end
		local current = waypoints[waypointIndex]
		if current == nil then
			return "Idle"
		end
		local flat = current.Position - root.Position
		if Vector3.new(flat.X, 0, flat.Z).Magnitude < 2 and waypoints[waypointIndex + 1] then
			waypointIndex += 1
		end
		local waypoint: PathWaypoint = waypoints[waypointIndex]
		if waypoint.Action == Enum.PathWaypointAction.Jump then
			humanoid.Jump = true
		end
		humanoid:MoveTo(waypoint.Position)
		return "Path"
	end

	return {
		update = update,
		pathsComputed = function(): number
			return computed
		end,
	}
end

return Chaser
```

A single loop drives every zombie at a modest rate, staggered so they don't all path on the same frame:

```lua
--!strict
local Chaser = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Chaser"))

local function runZombie(zombie: Model, getTarget: () -> BasePart?)
	local chaser = Chaser.new(zombie, { repathDistance = 6, repathInterval = 1, sightRange = 80 })
	task.wait(math.random() * 0.25)
	while zombie.Parent do
		local target = getTarget()
		if target then
			chaser.update(target)
		end
		task.wait(0.25)
	end
end

return runZombie
```

- Direct chasing covers most of the time a zombie is actually near a player, at the cost of one raycast instead of a path computation.
- Requiring both "stale" and "moved" means a stationary target never triggers recomputes, and a moving one at most once per interval.
- A failed compute (player on a roof the zombie cannot reach) is also retried only once per interval, so 30 zombies under one tower do not path every update.
- Reusing one Path object per NPC avoids allocating a new one per computation.
request: I have 30 zombies chasing players and each one recomputes a path every 0.1 seconds. The server is dying. But if I recompute less often they run to where the player used to be. What's the standard approach?

answer:
Sample candidate points on a ring around the critter, score each by how much farther from the threat it is (and prefer directions away from the threat), then try them best-first and keep the first one that has a valid path. If none is reachable the function returns nil and the critter can cower or fight back.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.FleePlanner
local PathfindingService = game:GetService("PathfindingService")

local FleePlanner = {}

export type Candidate = { position: Vector3, score: number }

function FleePlanner.candidates(position: Vector3, threat: Vector3, radius: number, samples: number): { Candidate }
	local away = Vector3.new(position.X - threat.X, 0, position.Z - threat.Z)
	local awayUnit = if away.Magnitude > 1e-3 then away.Unit else Vector3.xAxis
	local list: { Candidate } = {}
	for index = 1, samples do
		local angle = index / samples * 2 * math.pi
		local direction = Vector3.new(math.cos(angle), 0, math.sin(angle))
		local point = position + direction * radius
		local gain = (point - threat).Magnitude - (position - threat).Magnitude
		table.insert(list, { position = point, score = gain + direction:Dot(awayUnit) * radius * 0.5 })
	end
	table.sort(list, function(a: Candidate, b: Candidate): boolean
		return a.score > b.score
	end)
	return list
end

function FleePlanner.choose(position: Vector3, threat: Vector3, radius: number, maxTries: number): (Vector3?, Path?)
	local path = PathfindingService:CreatePath({ AgentRadius = 1.5, AgentHeight = 3, AgentCanJump = false })
	for index, candidate in FleePlanner.candidates(position, threat, radius, 12) do
		if index > maxTries then
			break
		end
		local ok = pcall(function()
			path:ComputeAsync(position, candidate.position)
		end)
		if ok and path.Status == Enum.PathStatus.Success then
			return candidate.position, path
		end
	end
	return nil, nil
end

return FleePlanner
```

- Trying only the best few candidates bounds the cost; each `ComputeAsync` is real work, so 3-4 tries per decision is plenty.
- Scoring by distance gained from the threat naturally rejects points behind the player, and the direction term breaks ties toward "straight away".
- A wall right behind the critter makes those candidates fail to path, so it slides sideways along the wall instead of pressing into it.
- Re-plan when the threat closes in, not every frame; a flee decision every half second looks natural.

answer:
`Humanoid:MoveTo` gives up after 8 seconds if the target has not been reached, and fires `MoveToFinished(false)`. For long walks, issue the MoveTo again before that limit. The helper below keeps re-issuing it until the NPC arrives, dies, or an overall deadline passes, and returns whether it arrived.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.LongMove
local REISSUE_EVERY = 6
local POLL = 0.1

local LongMove = {}

function LongMove.walk(humanoid: Humanoid, target: Vector3, deadline: number): boolean
	local reached = false
	local connection = humanoid.MoveToFinished:Connect(function(success: boolean)
		if success then
			reached = true
		end
	end)

	local started = os.clock()
	local lastIssue = -math.huge
	while not reached and humanoid.Health > 0 and os.clock() - started < deadline do
		if os.clock() - lastIssue >= REISSUE_EVERY then
			humanoid:MoveTo(target)
			lastIssue = os.clock()
		end
		task.wait(POLL)
	end

	connection:Disconnect()
	return reached
end

return LongMove
```

- Re-issuing at 6 seconds restarts the internal 8-second timer before it can expire, so the walk never stalls mid-way.
- `MoveToFinished(false)` (timed out or interrupted) is not treated as arrival; only `true` ends the walk successfully.
- The overall deadline is still needed: a straight line can be blocked by a wall the NPC cannot get around, and the caller decides what to do then.
- For anything that is not a clear straight line, use PathfindingService and walk the waypoints instead.
request: I call `npc.Humanoid:MoveTo(farAwayPoint)` and the NPC stops halfway across the map for no reason. The point is reachable in a straight line. Why does it stop?

answer:
Describe the NPC's size and abilities in the agent parameters so paths fit it, honour `Jump` waypoints, and wait for each waypoint with a timeout scaled to the distance instead of an unbounded `Wait()`. The function reports why it stopped, so the caller can retry or give up.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.PathFollower
local PathfindingService = game:GetService("PathfindingService")

export type Result = "Reached" | "NoPath" | "Stuck"

local PathFollower = {}

PathFollower.agent = {
	AgentRadius = 2.5,
	AgentHeight = 6,
	AgentCanJump = true,
	WaypointSpacing = 4,
	Costs = { Water = 20 },
}

function PathFollower.stepTimeout(distance: number, walkSpeed: number): number
	return distance / math.max(walkSpeed, 1) * 1.5 + 0.5
end

function PathFollower.moveToWaypoint(humanoid: Humanoid, waypoint: PathWaypoint)
	if waypoint.Action == Enum.PathWaypointAction.Jump then
		humanoid.Jump = true
	end
	humanoid:MoveTo(waypoint.Position)
end

-- Yields until MoveToFinished fires or the timeout passes; true only if the humanoid reached the point.
local function waitForMove(humanoid: Humanoid, timeout: number): boolean
	local thread = coroutine.running()
	local settled = false
	local connection = humanoid.MoveToFinished:Once(function(reached: boolean)
		if not settled then
			settled = true
			task.spawn(thread, reached)
		end
	end)
	task.delay(timeout, function()
		if not settled then
			settled = true
			connection:Disconnect()
			task.spawn(thread, false)
		end
	end)
	return coroutine.yield()
end

function PathFollower.walkTo(humanoid: Humanoid, root: BasePart, goal: Vector3): Result
	local path = PathfindingService:CreatePath(PathFollower.agent)
	local ok = pcall(function()
		path:ComputeAsync(root.Position, goal)
	end)
	if not ok or path.Status ~= Enum.PathStatus.Success then
		return "NoPath"
	end
	local waypoints = path:GetWaypoints()
	for index = 2, #waypoints do
		local waypoint = waypoints[index]
		local timeout = PathFollower.stepTimeout((waypoint.Position - root.Position).Magnitude, humanoid.WalkSpeed)
		PathFollower.moveToWaypoint(humanoid, waypoint)
		if not waitForMove(humanoid, timeout) or humanoid.Health <= 0 then
			return "Stuck"
		end
	end
	return "Reached"
end

return PathFollower
```

- The first waypoint is the starting position, so following starts at index 2.
- `AgentRadius`/`AgentHeight` should be a little larger than the NPC's real size; paths through gaps it can barely fit look like snagging in practice.
- `Costs` makes the path avoid materials or PathfindingModifier labels (here water) unless there is no alternative.
- "Stuck" with a distance-based timeout replaces the infinite `Wait()`; the caller can jump, re-path from the current position, or teleport after a few failures.

answer:
Read the points once, sort them by an `Order` attribute, and run the patrol in its own thread: move, wait for arrival (with a timeout so a blocked guard keeps going), pause, then pick the next index according to the mode. A stop function ends the thread cleanly so the guard can switch to chasing.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.Patrol
export type Mode = "Loop" | "PingPong"
export type Patrol = {
	stopPatrol: () -> (),
	targetIndex: () -> number,
}

local Patrol = {}

function Patrol.orderedPoints(folder: Instance): { BasePart }
	local points: { BasePart } = {}
	for _, child in folder:GetChildren() do
		if child:IsA("BasePart") and type(child:GetAttribute("Order")) == "number" then
			table.insert(points, child)
		end
	end
	table.sort(points, function(a: BasePart, b: BasePart): boolean
		return (a:GetAttribute("Order") :: number) < (b:GetAttribute("Order") :: number)
	end)
	return points
end

function Patrol.nextIndex(index: number, direction: number, count: number, mode: Mode): (number, number)
	if count <= 1 then
		return 1, direction
	end
	if mode == "Loop" then
		return index % count + 1, 1
	end
	local nextValue = index + direction
	if nextValue > count or nextValue < 1 then
		direction = -direction
		nextValue = index + direction
	end
	return nextValue, direction
end

function Patrol.start(humanoid: Humanoid, points: { BasePart }, mode: Mode, pause: number): Patrol
	assert(#points > 0, "patrol needs at least one point")
	local running = true
	local index, direction = 1, 1
	local arrived = false
	local connection = humanoid.MoveToFinished:Connect(function()
		arrived = true
	end)

	task.spawn(function()
		while running and humanoid.Health > 0 do
			arrived = false
			humanoid:MoveTo(points[index].Position)
			local waited = 0
			while running and not arrived and waited < 8 do
				waited += task.wait(0.1)
			end
			if not running then
				break
			end
			task.wait(pause)
			index, direction = Patrol.nextIndex(index, direction, #points, mode)
		end
		connection:Disconnect()
	end)

	return {
		stopPatrol = function()
			running = false
		end,
		targetIndex = function(): number
			return index
		end,
	}
end

return Patrol
```

Usage: `local patrol = Patrol.start(guard.Humanoid, Patrol.orderedPoints(workspace.GuardRoute), "PingPong", 2)`; call `patrol.stopPatrol()` when the guard spots someone and start a new patrol when it gives up the chase.

- Sorting by an attribute lets level designers insert a point between 2 and 3 by giving it Order 2.5, with no renaming.
- The 8-second cap mirrors Humanoid:MoveTo's own timeout, so a guard blocked by a crate moves on to the next point instead of freezing.
- `nextIndex` is pure, which makes the loop/ping-pong order easy to verify.

answer:
Sample every character a few times per second on the server: if linear or angular velocity is far beyond anything legitimate, zero both and pivot the character back to its last safe position; otherwise record the current position as safe. A strike counter per player tells you who triggers it constantly.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.AntiFling
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

export type Options = { maxLinear: number, maxAngular: number, interval: number }

local AntiFling = {}

function AntiFling.isFlung(linear: Vector3, angular: Vector3, options: Options): boolean
	return linear.Magnitude > options.maxLinear or angular.Magnitude > options.maxAngular
end

function AntiFling.start(options: Options, onStrike: ((player: Player, strikes: number) -> ())?): () -> ()
	local safe: { [Player]: CFrame } = {}
	local strikes: { [Player]: number } = {}
	local elapsed = 0

	local heartbeat = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt: number)
		elapsed += dt
		if elapsed < options.interval then
			return
		end
		elapsed = 0
		for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
			local character = player.Character
			local root = if character then character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") else nil
			if character and root and root:IsA("BasePart") then
				if AntiFling.isFlung(root.AssemblyLinearVelocity, root.AssemblyAngularVelocity, options) then
					root.AssemblyLinearVelocity = Vector3.zero
					root.AssemblyAngularVelocity = Vector3.zero
					local lastSafe = safe[player]
					if lastSafe then
						character:PivotTo(lastSafe)
					end
					local count = (strikes[player] or 0) + 1
					strikes[player] = count
					local callback = onStrike
					if callback then
						callback(player, count)
					end
				else
					safe[player] = character:GetPivot()
				end
			end
		end
	end)

	local removing = Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player)
		safe[player] = nil
		strikes[player] = nil
	end)

	return function()
		heartbeat:Disconnect()
		removing:Disconnect()
	end
end

return AntiFling
```

Starting it: `AntiFling.start({ maxLinear = 250, maxAngular = 40, interval = 0.2 })`, with an `onStrike` that logs or kicks after repeated strikes.

- Thresholds must sit well above your fastest legitimate movement (dashes, launch pads, vehicles); measure those first and add margin.
- The player's client simulates its own character, so the owner can overwrite the server's velocity write; the server `PivotTo` is what reliably reaches it. A determined exploiter can keep fighting the reset, which is why strikes are counted.
- Recording the safe position only on clean samples means the reset never puts someone back mid-fling.
- Pair this with a "Players" collision group that does not collide with itself; most player-on-player flings disappear entirely.

answer:
Both come from the constant-acceleration equation `p(t) = p0 + v0*t + 0.5*g*t^2` with `g = (0, -Gravity, 0)`. Landing on a flat ground height means solving the quadratic in Y for the later root; aiming for a fixed flight time rearranges the same equation for `v0`.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.Ballistics
local Ballistics = {}

function Ballistics.positionAt(origin: Vector3, velocity: Vector3, gravity: number, t: number): Vector3
	return origin + velocity * t + Vector3.new(0, -0.5 * gravity * t * t, 0)
end

-- Time when the projectile comes down to groundY, or nil if it never reaches it.
function Ballistics.timeToGround(originY: number, velocityY: number, gravity: number, groundY: number): number?
	local a = -0.5 * gravity
	local b = velocityY
	local c = originY - groundY
	local discriminant = b * b - 4 * a * c
	if discriminant < 0 then
		return nil
	end
	local root = math.sqrt(discriminant)
	local t = math.max((-b - root) / (2 * a), (-b + root) / (2 * a))
	return if t >= 0 then t else nil
end

function Ballistics.landingPoint(origin: Vector3, velocity: Vector3, gravity: number, groundY: number): Vector3?
	local t = Ballistics.timeToGround(origin.Y, velocity.Y, gravity, groundY)
	return if t then Ballistics.positionAt(origin, velocity, gravity, t) else nil
end

function Ballistics.launchVelocity(origin: Vector3, target: Vector3, gravity: number, flightTime: number): Vector3
	assert(flightTime > 0, "flightTime must be positive")
	return (target - origin) / flightTime + Vector3.new(0, 0.5 * gravity * flightTime, 0)
end

return Ballistics
```

Firing the mortar shell on the server with the computed velocity:

```lua
--!strict
local Ballistics = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("Ballistics"))

local function fireShell(template: BasePart, muzzle: Vector3, target: Vector3)
	local shell = template:Clone()
	shell.Position = muzzle
	shell.Parent = workspace
	shell:SetNetworkOwner(nil)
	shell.AssemblyLinearVelocity = Ballistics.launchVelocity(muzzle, target, workspace.Gravity, 2.5)
end

return fireShell
```

- The later root of the quadratic is the descent; the earlier one is the moment it would cross the same height on the way up (or a time in the past).
- A fixed flight time keeps the arc predictable for the target, and the velocity grows with distance, which suits mortars; for a fixed speed you would solve for the angle instead.
- Default Roblox physics applies no air drag, so these predictions match the simulation as long as nothing else acts on the part (collisions, constraints, or fluid forces if you enable them).
request: I'm making a mortar and a grenade throw. I need two things: show a marker where a grenade will land given its launch velocity, and for the mortar, compute the launch velocity that lands on a clicked target after a fixed flight time. Gravity is `workspace.Gravity`.

answer:
Apply an upward `VectorForce` proportional to how much of the crate is under the water line (Archimedes), plus a damping term against vertical velocity so it settles instead of bouncing forever. Choosing a buoyancy factor above 1 at full submersion makes the crate float partly above the surface.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.Buoyancy
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local Buoyancy = {}

function Buoyancy.submergedFraction(centerY: number, height: number, waterLevel: number): number
	local bottom = centerY - height / 2
	return math.clamp((waterLevel - bottom) / height, 0, 1)
end

-- Upward force in world space: weight * floatiness * submerged fraction, minus vertical damping.
function Buoyancy.force(mass: number, gravity: number, fraction: number, floatiness: number, verticalVelocity: number, damping: number): number
	if fraction <= 0 then
		return 0
	end
	return mass * gravity * floatiness * fraction - verticalVelocity * damping * mass * fraction
end

function Buoyancy.attach(part: BasePart, waterLevel: number, floatiness: number): () -> ()
	local attachment = Instance.new("Attachment")
	attachment.Parent = part
	local vectorForce = Instance.new("VectorForce")
	vectorForce.Attachment0 = attachment
	vectorForce.RelativeTo = Enum.ActuatorRelativeTo.World
	vectorForce.ApplyAtCenterOfMass = true
	vectorForce.Force = Vector3.zero
	vectorForce.Parent = part

	local connection = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
		local fraction = Buoyancy.submergedFraction(part.Position.Y, part.Size.Y, waterLevel)
		local up = Buoyancy.force(part.AssemblyMass, workspace.Gravity, fraction, floatiness, part.AssemblyLinearVelocity.Y, 2)
		vectorForce.Force = Vector3.new(0, up, 0)
	end)

	return function()
		connection:Disconnect()
		vectorForce:Destroy()
		attachment:Destroy()
	end
end

return Buoyancy
```

Usage: `Buoyancy.attach(crate, waterPart.Position.Y + waterPart.Size.Y / 2, 1.6)`.

- With floatiness 1.6, the crate is in balance when 1 / 1.6 (about 62%) of it is submerged, so it rides visibly above the surface.
- Damping scales with the submerged fraction, so a crate in the air falls freely and only slows once it hits the water.
- Use `AssemblyMass`, not the part's own mass, so crates welded to other parts get enough lift for the whole assembly.
- Run it wherever the crate is simulated; for crates players push around, ownership may move to a client, in which case the same code belongs in a client script for those parts.
request: I have a water plane made of a transparent part (not terrain water) and I want crates to float on it and bob a little instead of sinking or shooting up. How would I do buoyancy with constraints?

answer:
Register a "Players" group once with `RegisterCollisionGroup`, make it non-collidable with itself, and set each character part's `CollisionGroup` property. Characters gain parts after spawning (accessories, tools), so new descendants are assigned too.

```lua
--!strict
-- Script: ServerScriptService.PlayerCollisions
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local PhysicsService = game:GetService("PhysicsService")

local GROUP = "Players"

if not PhysicsService:IsCollisionGroupRegistered(GROUP) then
	PhysicsService:RegisterCollisionGroup(GROUP)
end
PhysicsService:CollisionGroupSetCollidable(GROUP, GROUP, false)

local function assign(instance: Instance)
	if instance:IsA("BasePart") then
		instance.CollisionGroup = GROUP
	end
end

local function onCharacter(character: Model)
	for _, descendant in character:GetDescendants() do
		assign(descendant)
	end
	-- Connected on the character itself, so it is cleaned up when the character is destroyed.
	character.DescendantAdded:Connect(assign)
end

local function onPlayer(player: Player)
	player.CharacterAdded:Connect(onCharacter)
	if player.Character then
		onCharacter(player.Character)
	end
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayer)
for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
	onPlayer(player)
end
```

- `CollisionGroup` is a plain property now; setting it replaces `SetPartCollisionGroup`.
- The group still collides with "Default", so the map, doors and moving platforms behave as before.
- Registering is limited to a fixed number of groups per place; register them once at startup, never per player.
- Collision groups only change physical collisions; raycasts and spatial queries still see the parts unless their params name a group.
request: I want players to walk through each other (my obby gets clogged at checkpoints), but they should still collide with the map. Old tutorials use `PhysicsService:CreateCollisionGroup` and `SetPartCollisionGroup`, which give deprecation warnings. What's the current way?

answer:
Player characters are simulated by their own client (it owns the assembly), so a velocity the server writes is immediately overwritten by the owner. A short-lived `LinearVelocity` constraint created on the server does replicate and is obeyed by whoever simulates the character, so the same code works for players and NPCs. The push direction is computed from attacker to target, flattened, with an upward component.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.Knockback
local Debris = game:GetService("Debris")

local Knockback = {}

function Knockback.velocity(from: Vector3, to: Vector3, horizontalSpeed: number, upSpeed: number, fallback: Vector3): Vector3
	local flat = Vector3.new(to.X - from.X, 0, to.Z - from.Z)
	local direction = if flat.Magnitude > 1e-3 then flat.Unit else Vector3.new(fallback.X, 0, fallback.Z).Unit
	return direction * horizontalSpeed + Vector3.new(0, upSpeed, 0)
end

function Knockback.apply(targetRoot: BasePart, velocity: Vector3, duration: number): LinearVelocity
	local old = targetRoot:FindFirstChild("KnockbackVelocity")
	if old then
		old:Destroy()
	end
	local attachment = targetRoot:FindFirstChild("RootAttachment") or Instance.new("Attachment")
	attachment.Parent = targetRoot

	local push = Instance.new("LinearVelocity")
	push.Name = "KnockbackVelocity"
	push.Attachment0 = attachment
	push.RelativeTo = Enum.ActuatorRelativeTo.World
	push.VelocityConstraintMode = Enum.VelocityConstraintMode.Vector
	push.VectorVelocity = velocity
	push.MaxForce = targetRoot.AssemblyMass * 4000
	push.Parent = targetRoot
	Debris:AddItem(push, duration)
	return push
end

return Knockback
```

From the hit handler: `Knockback.apply(targetRoot, Knockback.velocity(attackerRoot.Position, targetRoot.Position, 60, 25, attackerRoot.CFrame.LookVector), 0.2)`.

- The fallback direction (the attacker's facing) covers attacker and target standing at the same spot, where `Unit` of a zero vector would be NaN.
- A new hit replaces the previous push instead of stacking two constraints fighting each other.
- `MaxForce` scales with the assembly's mass, so heavy bosses and light players react to the same speed instead of the same force.
- Keep the duration short (0.15-0.3 s); after the constraint is removed, normal physics and the Humanoid take over and the target lands naturally.

answer:
Let the physics engine move the pet: an `AlignPosition` and `AlignOrientation` in one-attachment mode pull the pet toward a target that you update on the server a few times per second. The target is an offset in the player's root space, so the pet stays behind and to the side whichever way the player faces; a ray from the player to that point pulls the target back in front of any wall. Network ownership goes to the pet's owner so the motion is smooth for them.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.PetFollow
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local PetFollow = {}

function PetFollow.targetFor(rootCFrame: CFrame, offset: Vector3): CFrame
	local flatLook = Vector3.new(rootCFrame.LookVector.X, 0, rootCFrame.LookVector.Z)
	local facing = if flatLook.Magnitude > 1e-3 then CFrame.lookAt(rootCFrame.Position, rootCFrame.Position + flatLook) else rootCFrame
	return facing * CFrame.new(offset)
end

function PetFollow.attach(pet: BasePart, owner: Player, offset: Vector3): () -> ()
	local attachment = Instance.new("Attachment")
	attachment.Parent = pet

	local alignPosition = Instance.new("AlignPosition")
	alignPosition.Mode = Enum.PositionAlignmentMode.OneAttachment
	alignPosition.Attachment0 = attachment
	alignPosition.Responsiveness = 25
	alignPosition.MaxForce = 1e5
	alignPosition.Parent = pet

	local alignOrientation = Instance.new("AlignOrientation")
	alignOrientation.Mode = Enum.OrientationAlignmentMode.OneAttachment
	alignOrientation.Attachment0 = attachment
	alignOrientation.Responsiveness = 20
	alignOrientation.Parent = pet

	pet.Anchored = false
	pet.CanCollide = false
	pet.Massless = true
	pet:SetNetworkOwner(owner)

	local params = RaycastParams.new()
	params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
	params.RespectCanCollide = true

	local sinceUpdate = 0
	local heartbeat = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt: number)
		sinceUpdate += dt
		if sinceUpdate < 0.1 then
			return
		end
		sinceUpdate = 0
		local character = owner.Character
		local root = if character then character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") else nil
		if root and root:IsA("BasePart") then
			local target = PetFollow.targetFor(root.CFrame, offset)
			params.FilterDescendantsInstances = { character, pet }
			-- Keep the goal on the player's side of any wall between them and the offset point.
			local wall = workspace:Raycast(root.Position, target.Position - root.Position, params)
			alignPosition.Position = if wall then wall.Position + wall.Normal * 1.5 else target.Position
			alignOrientation.CFrame = target
		end
	end)

	return function()
		heartbeat:Disconnect()
		attachment:Destroy()
		alignPosition:Destroy()
		alignOrientation:Destroy()
	end
end

return PetFollow
```

Usage when a pet is equipped: `local detach = PetFollow.attach(petPart, player, Vector3.new(3, 1, 4))` (right, up, behind), and call `detach()` when it is unequipped.

- Constraints are interpolated by the physics engine on every client, which removes the jitter of server-side CFrame writes arriving at network rate.
- Only the target is updated, and only 10 times per second; `Responsiveness` handles the smoothing between updates.
- Flattening the look vector keeps the pet level when the player looks up or down in first person.
- The pet stays non-colliding so it never shoves its owner; the wall ray keeps its goal out of walls instead.
- Giving the owner network ownership makes the pet's motion smooth for them; the target still comes from the server's view of the player, so it trails by about one round trip.

answer:
Have the client send only an aim direction; the server checks it is a finite, roughly unit vector, applies its own fixed speed, and spawns the snowball in front of the thrower's root. Set the network owner to the server before giving it velocity: the "hang" is ownership being handed over to a nearby client mid-flight.

```lua
--!strict
-- Script: ServerScriptService.SnowballServer
local Debris = game:GetService("Debris")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")

local throwRemote = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ThrowSnowball")
local template = ServerStorage:WaitForChild("Snowball")

local SPEED = 90
local COOLDOWN = 0.5
local LIFETIME = 6
local MAX_INHERIT = 40
local lastThrow: { [Player]: number } = {}

throwRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player: Player, aim: any)
	if typeof(aim) ~= "Vector3" or aim.Magnitude ~= aim.Magnitude or math.abs(aim.Magnitude - 1) > 0.05 then
		return
	end
	local now = os.clock()
	if now - (lastThrow[player] or -math.huge) < COOLDOWN then
		return
	end
	local character = player.Character
	local root = if character then character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") else nil
	local humanoid = if character then character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid") else nil
	if root == nil or humanoid == nil or humanoid.Health <= 0 then
		return
	end
	lastThrow[player] = now

	local direction: Vector3 = aim.Unit
	local snowball = template:Clone()
	snowball.CFrame = CFrame.new(root.Position + direction * 3 + Vector3.new(0, 1.5, 0))
	snowball.Parent = workspace
	snowball:SetNetworkOwner(nil)
	-- The character's velocity is reported by its own client, so only a plausible running speed is inherited.
	local inherited = root.AssemblyLinearVelocity
	if not (inherited.Magnitude <= MAX_INHERIT) then
		inherited = Vector3.zero
	end
	snowball.AssemblyLinearVelocity = direction * SPEED + inherited
	snowball:SetAttribute("ThrowerUserId", player.UserId)
	Debris:AddItem(snowball, LIFETIME)
end)

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player)
	lastThrow[player] = nil
end)
```

- The client controls only the direction; speed, spawn point and lifetime are server constants, so a modified client cannot launch a snowball across the map.
- `SetNetworkOwner(nil)` keeps the server simulating the projectile, which also makes its collisions authoritative for hit detection.
- Adding the thrower's own velocity makes throws while running feel right instead of the ball lagging behind; it is capped (and NaN dropped) because an exploiter can set their own character's velocity to anything.
- If you prefer client-smooth visuals, render a cosmetic copy on the thrower's client and keep this server part invisible.

answer:
Give the vehicle's assembly to the driver while they sit in the seat, so their inputs are simulated locally with no round trip, and give it back to the server when they get out so a parked car does not drift to whichever client is nearest. Watch the seat's `Occupant` property for both transitions.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.VehicleOwnership
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local VehicleOwnership = {}

function VehicleOwnership.bind(seat: VehicleSeat): RBXScriptConnection
	local function refresh()
		local occupant = seat.Occupant
		local character = if occupant then occupant.Parent else nil
		local driver = if character then Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(character) else nil
		-- SetNetworkOwner affects the whole assembly the seat is welded into.
		if seat:CanSetNetworkOwnership() then
			seat:SetNetworkOwner(driver)
		end
	end
	refresh()
	return seat:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Occupant"):Connect(refresh)
end

return VehicleOwnership
```

Binding every car seat at startup and for cars spawned later:

```lua
--!strict
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local VehicleOwnership = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("VehicleOwnership"))

local function onSeat(seat: Instance)
	if seat:IsA("VehicleSeat") then
		VehicleOwnership.bind(seat)
	end
end

CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal("CarSeat"):Connect(onSeat)
for _, seat in CollectionService:GetTagged("CarSeat") do
	onSeat(seat)
end
```

- `SetNetworkOwner(nil)` hands ownership to the server, which is what a parked car wants; NPC drivers also return nil from `GetPlayerFromCharacter`, keeping NPC cars server-simulated.
- `CanSetNetworkOwnership` is false when a part of the assembly is anchored (for example a car still locked in place at the spawner), and calling `SetNetworkOwner` then would error.
- The driver's client now has authority over the car's physics: validate anything gameplay-relevant (lap times, ramming damage) on the server from positions over time.

answer:
Cast a short ray straight down from the root, just past where the feet are, excluding the character. The result gives the part, material and surface normal; the slope angle is the angle between that normal and world up. Reuse one RaycastParams per character instead of building it every frame.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.GroundCheck
export type Ground = { part: BasePart, material: Enum.Material, normal: Vector3, slope: number, distance: number }

local GroundCheck = {}

function GroundCheck.slopeAngle(normal: Vector3): number
	return math.deg(math.acos(math.clamp(normal.Unit:Dot(Vector3.yAxis), -1, 1)))
end

function GroundCheck.newProbe(character: Model, hipToFeet: number, tolerance: number): () -> Ground?
	local root = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	assert(root and root:IsA("BasePart"), "character needs a HumanoidRootPart")
	local params = RaycastParams.new()
	params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
	params.FilterDescendantsInstances = { character }
	params.RespectCanCollide = true

	return function(): Ground?
		local result = workspace:Raycast(root.Position, Vector3.new(0, -(hipToFeet + tolerance), 0), params)
		if result == nil then
			return nil
		end
		return {
			part = result.Instance,
			material = result.Material,
			normal = result.Normal,
			slope = GroundCheck.slopeAngle(result.Normal),
			distance = result.Distance,
		}
	end
end

return GroundCheck
```

Using it to gate a slide ability on the client:

```lua
--!strict
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local GroundCheck = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("GroundCheck"))

local character = Players.LocalPlayer.Character or Players.LocalPlayer.CharacterAdded:Wait()
local probe = GroundCheck.newProbe(character, 3, 0.6)

local function canSlide(): boolean
	local ground = probe()
	return ground ~= nil and ground.slope <= 40
end

return canSlide
```

- `hipToFeet` is the distance from the root's centre to the bottom of the feet (3 studs for a default R15 character); the tolerance lets small steps and bumps still count as grounded.
- `RespectCanCollide` stops the probe from "standing" on non-collidable decorations such as grass meshes or trigger zones.
- A single ray can miss when the character stands on an edge with the centre over a gap; use `workspace:Spherecast` with a radius of about the root's half width if that matters for your game.

answer:
Build the ray yourself from the camera with `ViewportPointToRay`, cast it with your own RaycastParams, and when it hits nothing return a point at a fixed distance along the ray so aiming at the sky still gives a sensible direction. The casting part is a plain function, so it can be reused for touch input or a gamepad crosshair.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.CursorRay
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

export type Target = { position: Vector3, instance: BasePart?, normal: Vector3? }

local CursorRay = {}

function CursorRay.cast(origin: Vector3, direction: Vector3, maxDistance: number, params: RaycastParams): Target
	local unit = direction.Unit
	local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, unit * maxDistance, params)
	if result then
		return { position = result.Position, instance = result.Instance, normal = result.Normal }
	end
	return { position = origin + unit * maxDistance, instance = nil, normal = nil }
end

function CursorRay.fromScreen(camera: Camera, screenX: number, screenY: number, maxDistance: number, params: RaycastParams): Target
	local ray = camera:ViewportPointToRay(screenX, screenY)
	return CursorRay.cast(ray.Origin, ray.Direction, maxDistance, params)
end

function CursorRay.underMouse(maxDistance: number, params: RaycastParams): Target
	local location = UserInputService:GetMouseLocation()
	return CursorRay.fromScreen(workspace.CurrentCamera, location.X, location.Y, maxDistance, params)
end

return CursorRay
```

Setting up the filter once on the client:

```lua
--!strict
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local CursorRay = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):WaitForChild("CursorRay"))

local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.RespectCanCollide = true

local function aimPoint(): Vector3
	params.FilterDescendantsInstances = { Players.LocalPlayer.Character, workspace:FindFirstChild("PlacementPreview") }
	return CursorRay.underMouse(1000, params).position
end

return aimPoint
```

- `GetMouseLocation` includes the top bar inset, which is exactly what `ViewportPointToRay` expects; `ScreenPointToRay` is the variant for coordinates that exclude the inset.
- `RespectCanCollide` skips invisible non-collidable parts such as triggers and zones; parts that should never be hit can also set `CanQuery = false`.
- The fallback point at `maxDistance` keeps weapons firing toward the crosshair when aiming at the sky instead of toward a point near the world origin.

answer:
Cast, and if the hit part is a mirror, reflect the direction about the surface normal with `d - 2(d·n)n` and cast again from the hit point (nudged off the surface so it does not re-hit the same face). Stop at a non-mirror, when the remaining length runs out, or at a bounce limit. The result is the list of points, ready for drawing beams between them.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.LaserTrace
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")

export type Trace = { points: { Vector3 }, finalHit: BasePart? }

local LaserTrace = {}

function LaserTrace.reflect(direction: Vector3, normal: Vector3): Vector3
	return direction - 2 * direction:Dot(normal) * normal
end

function LaserTrace.trace(origin: Vector3, direction: Vector3, maxLength: number, maxBounces: number, params: RaycastParams): Trace
	local points = { origin }
	local position = origin
	local heading = direction.Unit
	local remaining = maxLength
	local finalHit: BasePart? = nil

	for bounce = 0, maxBounces do
		local result = workspace:Raycast(position, heading * remaining, params)
		if result == nil then
			table.insert(points, position + heading * remaining)
			break
		end
		table.insert(points, result.Position)
		remaining -= result.Distance
		finalHit = result.Instance
		if not CollectionService:HasTag(result.Instance, "Mirror") or bounce == maxBounces or remaining <= 0 then
			break
		end
		heading = LaserTrace.reflect(heading, result.Normal)
		position = result.Position + result.Normal * 0.01
	end
	return { points = points, finalHit = finalHit }
end

return LaserTrace
```

Checking the puzzle on the server: `local trace = LaserTrace.trace(emitter.Position, emitter.CFrame.LookVector, 500, 8, params)` and the puzzle is solved when `trace.finalHit == receiver`.

- The reflection formula needs a unit normal; raycast normals already are.
- Nudging the new origin along the normal avoids the next ray starting exactly on the mirror's surface and hitting it again at distance 0.
- The bounce limit protects against two parallel mirrors trapping the beam forever.
- Run the trace on the server to decide whether the puzzle is solved, and draw the beams on clients from the same point list.

answer:
Cast, and if the hit is something bullets should pass through (an accessory handle, or a nearly transparent or non-collidable part that is not a character's body), add it to the exclude list and cast again from the same origin. A small iteration cap keeps the cost bounded. A shot through a hat goes on to hit the head behind it, so it still counts on the player.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.ShotRay
local ShotRay = {}

local MAX_PASSES = 6

function ShotRay.passesThrough(part: BasePart): boolean
	if part:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Accessory") then
		return true
	end
	-- Body parts always count: the Humanoid turns CanCollide off on R15 arms and legs.
	local model = part:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
	if model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid") then
		return false
	end
	return part.Transparency >= 0.95 or not part.CanCollide
end

function ShotRay.cast(origin: Vector3, direction: Vector3, ignore: { Instance }): RaycastResult?
	local exclude = table.clone(ignore)
	local params = RaycastParams.new()
	params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
	for _ = 1, MAX_PASSES do
		params.FilterDescendantsInstances = exclude
		local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, direction, params)
		if result == nil or not ShotRay.passesThrough(result.Instance) then
			return result
		end
		table.insert(exclude, result.Instance)
	end
	return nil
end

return ShotRay
```

- Recasting from the same origin keeps distances and positions exact; only the blocking cosmetic is removed from consideration.
- `FilterDescendantsInstances` is copied when assigned, so the table must be reassigned after each insert for the new exclusion to apply.
- The cap stops a shot through a forest of invisible parts from costing dozens of casts; six passes covers a hat, hair and a barrier with room to spare.
- Collision groups are the zero-cost alternative for barriers you control: put them in a group and set `params.CollisionGroup` so the ray never sees them.

answer:
Do the cheap tests first: distance, then the angle between the guard's look direction and the direction to the target (a dot product against the cosine of half the cone). Only if both pass, cast a ray from the guard's eyes to the target's head; anything hit other than the target means it is hidden. Glass is excluded by putting see-through parts in a tagged list that the ray ignores.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.Vision
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")

export type Eye = { range: number, fovDegrees: number }

local Vision = {}

function Vision.inCone(eyeCFrame: CFrame, point: Vector3, eye: Eye): boolean
	local offset = point - eyeCFrame.Position
	local distance = offset.Magnitude
	if distance > eye.range then
		return false
	end
	if distance < 1e-3 then
		return true
	end
	return eyeCFrame.LookVector:Dot(offset / distance) >= math.cos(math.rad(eye.fovDegrees / 2))
end

function Vision.canSee(guard: Model, eyeCFrame: CFrame, target: Model, eye: Eye): boolean
	local head = target:FindFirstChild("Head")
	if head == nil or not head:IsA("BasePart") or not Vision.inCone(eyeCFrame, head.Position, eye) then
		return false
	end
	local ignore: { Instance } = { guard }
	for _, glass in CollectionService:GetTagged("SeeThrough") do
		table.insert(ignore, glass)
	end
	local params = RaycastParams.new()
	params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
	params.FilterDescendantsInstances = ignore
	local result = workspace:Raycast(eyeCFrame.Position, head.Position - eyeCFrame.Position, params)
	return result ~= nil and result.Instance:IsDescendantOf(target)
end

return Vision
```

- Raycasts are the expensive part, so the distance and cone checks run first and reject most players for free.
- Casting to the head means a player crouching behind a low wall is hidden; cast to the torso as well if you want partially visible players to count.
- Requiring the ray to hit the target (rather than "hit nothing") also catches the case where the target is standing inside a wall the cone check cannot know about.
- Guards should use their Head's CFrame (`guard.Head.CFrame`) as the eye, so animations that turn the head also turn the view.

answer:
Put an Attachment in the torch where the hand should grip it, then move the whole model so that attachment lands exactly on the hand's `RightGripAttachment` and only then create the WeldConstraint. The offset between the model's pivot and its grip point is measured once with `ToObjectSpace`, so it works for any prop shape.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.PropAttach
local PropAttach = {}

function PropAttach.attach(prop: Model, gripName: string, target: Attachment): WeldConstraint
	local primary = prop.PrimaryPart
	assert(primary, "prop needs a PrimaryPart")
	local grip = prop:FindFirstChild(gripName, true)
	assert(grip and grip:IsA("Attachment"), string.format("prop has no Attachment named %s", gripName))
	local targetPart = target.Parent
	assert(targetPart and targetPart:IsA("BasePart"), "target attachment must be inside a BasePart")

	-- Where the pivot sits relative to the grip, then place the pivot so the grip meets the target.
	local pivotFromGrip = grip.WorldCFrame:ToObjectSpace(prop:GetPivot())
	prop:PivotTo(target.WorldCFrame:ToWorldSpace(pivotFromGrip))

	for _, descendant in prop:GetDescendants() do
		if descendant:IsA("BasePart") then
			descendant.Anchored = false
			descendant.CanCollide = false
			descendant.Massless = true
		end
	end

	local weld = Instance.new("WeldConstraint")
	weld.Part0 = targetPart
	weld.Part1 = primary
	weld.Parent = primary
	prop.Parent = targetPart.Parent
	return weld
end

return PropAttach
```

Usage: `PropAttach.attach(torchTemplate:Clone(), "Grip", npc.RightHand.RightGripAttachment)`.

- A WeldConstraint freezes the offset that exists when it is created, so the alignment has to happen first; that is the bug in welding first.
- The torch's other parts must already be welded to its PrimaryPart (weld them once in Studio), otherwise only the PrimaryPart follows the hand.
- `Massless` keeps a heavy prop from tipping the NPC over, and `CanCollide = false` stops it from shoving into walls and other characters.

Join the weapon to the hand with a Motor6D instead of the automatic grip weld. Name the weapon part something other than "Handle" and turn `RequiresHandle` off so Roblox does not create its own RightGrip weld, then create the Motor6D on the server when the tool is equipped. Animations that key that motor will now move the sword.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.WeaponMotor
local MOTOR_NAME = "WeaponMotor"

local WeaponMotor = {}

function WeaponMotor.connect(character: Model, weaponPart: BasePart): Motor6D?
	local hand = character:FindFirstChild("RightHand")
	if hand == nil then
		return nil
	end
	local old = hand:FindFirstChild(MOTOR_NAME)
	if old then
		old:Destroy()
	end
	local handGrip = hand:FindFirstChild("RightGripAttachment")
	local weaponGrip = weaponPart:FindFirstChild("GripAttachment")

	local motor = Instance.new("Motor6D")
	motor.Name = MOTOR_NAME
	motor.Part0 = hand
	motor.Part1 = weaponPart
	motor.C0 = if handGrip then handGrip.CFrame else CFrame.identity
	motor.C1 = if weaponGrip then weaponGrip.CFrame else CFrame.identity
	motor.Parent = hand
	return motor
end

function WeaponMotor.disconnect(character: Model)
	local hand = character:FindFirstChild("RightHand")
	local motor = if hand then hand:FindFirstChild(MOTOR_NAME) else nil
	if motor then
		motor:Destroy()
	end
end

return WeaponMotor
```

Server Script inside the tool (the sword part is named "BodyAttach"):

```lua
--!strict
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")
local WeaponMotor = require(ServerScriptService:WaitForChild("WeaponMotor"))

local tool = script.Parent
tool.RequiresHandle = false
local blade = tool:WaitForChild("BodyAttach")
-- Remembered on equip: by the time Unequipped fires the tool is already back in the Backpack.
local holder: Model? = nil

tool.Equipped:Connect(function()
	local character = tool.Parent
	if character and character:IsA("Model") then
		holder = character
		WeaponMotor.connect(character, blade)
	end
end)

tool.Unequipped:Connect(function()
	if holder then
		WeaponMotor.disconnect(holder)
		holder = nil
	end
end)
```

- When animating, add the same Motor6D (Part0 RightHand, Part1 BodyAttach, same name) to the rig in the Animation Editor, otherwise the editor has no joint to key.
- C0/C1 come from attachments so the rest pose matches the grip you set up in Studio, and the animation only adds rotation on top.
- Creating the motor on the server makes it replicate to everyone, which the animation needs to show the sword moving for other players.
- The blade must be unanchored and its other parts welded to BodyAttach.

Attach it attachment-to-attachment with a `RigidConstraint`: the jetpack's mount attachment snaps onto the character's `BodyBackAttachment`, so there is no CFrame maths at all. Make every part massless and non-colliding so the character controller does not feel the extra parts.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.BackItem
local BackItem = {}

function BackItem.attach(character: Model, template: Model, mountName: string): Model?
	local torso = character:FindFirstChild("UpperTorso") or character:FindFirstChild("Torso")
	local bodyBack = if torso then torso:FindFirstChild("BodyBackAttachment") else nil
	if bodyBack == nil then
		return nil
	end

	local old = character:FindFirstChild(template.Name)
	if old then
		old:Destroy()
	end

	local backItem = template:Clone()
	local mount = backItem:FindFirstChild(mountName, true)
	assert(mount and mount:IsA("Attachment"), string.format("template needs an Attachment named %s", mountName))

	for _, descendant in backItem:GetDescendants() do
		if descendant:IsA("BasePart") then
			descendant.Anchored = false
			descendant.CanCollide = false
			descendant.CanTouch = false
			descendant.CanQuery = false
			descendant.Massless = true
		end
	end

	local rigid = Instance.new("RigidConstraint")
	rigid.Attachment0 = bodyBack
	rigid.Attachment1 = mount
	rigid.Parent = mount.Parent
	backItem.Parent = character
	return backItem
end

return BackItem
```

Hooking it to spawns on the server:

```lua
local jetpack = ServerStorage:WaitForChild("Jetpack")

end

local function onPlayer(player: Player)

	if player.Character then
		onCharacter(player.Character)
	end
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayer)
for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
	onPlayer(player)
end
```

- `CanQuery = false` keeps raycasts and hitboxes from treating the cosmetic as part of the body, which matters for headshot and hit checks.

answer:
`CFrame.new(pos, lookAt)` has no idea which way is "up" when the normal points straight up or down, so the result is degenerate. Build the axes yourself with cross products and switch to a fallback up direction (the player's facing) when the normal is nearly vertical. The poster's front then faces out of the surface and it is pushed out by half its thickness so it never z-fights.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ReplicatedStorage.SurfaceAlign
local SurfaceAlign = {}

-- CFrame at `position` whose LookVector is `normal`; `upHint` decides the roll.
function SurfaceAlign.fromNormal(position: Vector3, normal: Vector3, upHint: Vector3): CFrame
	local unitNormal = normal.Unit
	local right = unitNormal:Cross(upHint)
	if right.Magnitude < 1e-3 then
		-- upHint is parallel to the normal; any perpendicular axis gives a valid frame.
		right = unitNormal:Cross(Vector3.xAxis)
		if right.Magnitude < 1e-3 then
			right = unitNormal:Cross(Vector3.zAxis)
		end
	end
	local up = right.Unit:Cross(unitNormal)
	return CFrame.fromMatrix(position, right.Unit, up.Unit)
end

function SurfaceAlign.place(result: RaycastResult, thickness: number, facing: Vector3): CFrame
	-- Walls keep world up; floors and ceilings use the player's facing so the poster reads upright for them.
	local upHint = if math.abs(result.Normal.Y) > 0.98 then facing else Vector3.yAxis
	return SurfaceAlign.fromNormal(result.Position, result.Normal, upHint):ToWorldSpace(CFrame.new(0, 0, -thickness / 2))
end

return SurfaceAlign
```

- `CFrame.fromMatrix(pos, right, up)` derives the back vector as `right:Cross(up)`, so building right from `normal x upHint` makes the LookVector equal the normal.
- Moving along local -Z (forward) by half the thickness keeps the poster on the surface instead of half inside it.
- Do the placement on the server with the server's own raycast; trust only the client's click direction, not its hit position.

answer:
Run the countdown in one thread you keep a reference to, tick once per second, and call `task.cancel` on it when the round ends early. The timer object reports whether the cancel actually stopped something, so double endings are easy to detect.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.Countdown
export type Countdown = {
	cancelTimer: () -> boolean,
	isRunning: () -> boolean,
}

local Countdown = {}

function Countdown.start(seconds: number, onTick: (remaining: number) -> (), onExpired: () -> ()): Countdown
	local running = true
	local thread = task.spawn(function()
		for remaining = seconds, 1, -1 do
			onTick(remaining)
			task.wait(1)
		end
		running = false
		onTick(0)
		onExpired()
	end)

	return {
		cancelTimer = function(): boolean
			if not running then
				return false
			end
			running = false
			task.cancel(thread)
			return true
		end,
		isRunning = function(): boolean
			return running
		end,
	}
end

return Countdown
```

Using it for a round, with the UI reading an attribute:

```lua
--!strict
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Countdown = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Countdown"))

local roundTimer: { cancelTimer: () -> boolean }? = nil

local function endRound(reason: string)
	if roundTimer then
		roundTimer.cancelTimer()
		roundTimer = nil
	end
	ReplicatedStorage:SetAttribute("RoundEndReason", reason)
end

local function startRound()
	roundTimer = Countdown.start(120, function(remaining)
		ReplicatedStorage:SetAttribute("TimeLeft", remaining)
	end, function()
		roundTimer = nil
		endRound("Time")
	end)
end

return { startRound = startRound, endRound = endRound }
```

- `task.cancel` stops the thread wherever it is waiting, so neither the remaining ticks nor `onExpired` run after an early win.
- A fire-and-forget `task.delay` cannot be told apart from the next round's timer; holding the handle in `roundTimer` ties each timer to its round.
- Ticking with `task.wait(1)` can drift by a frame per tick; for long timers compute `remaining` from `os.clock()` against an end time instead.

Keep one loader that owns the current map: loading always destroys the previous one first, picks randomly among the maps other than the last one played, and parents the clone in a single step. Spawn points come from a folder inside each map, so the round code never searches the whole workspace.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.MapRotation
export type Rotation = {
	loadNext: () -> Model,
	unload: () -> (),
	spawnPoints: () -> { BasePart },
	current: () -> Model?,
}

local MapRotation = {}

function MapRotation.new(library: Instance, container: Instance, random: Random): Rotation
	local currentMap: Model? = nil
	local lastName: string? = nil

	local function unload()
		if currentMap then
			currentMap:Destroy()
			currentMap = nil
		end
	end

	local function loadNext(): Model
		local candidates: { Model } = {}
		for _, child in library:GetChildren() do
			if child:IsA("Model") and (child.Name ~= lastName or #library:GetChildren() == 1) then
				table.insert(candidates, child)
			end
		end
		assert(#candidates > 0, "the map library has no Models")
		unload()
		local chosen = candidates[random:NextInteger(1, #candidates)]
		local map = chosen:Clone()
		map.Name = "CurrentMap"
		map:SetAttribute("MapName", chosen.Name)
		map.Parent = container
		currentMap = map
		lastName = chosen.Name
		return map
	end

	return {
		loadNext = loadNext,
		unload = unload,
		spawnPoints = function(): { BasePart }
			local points: { BasePart } = {}
			local folder = if currentMap then currentMap:FindFirstChild("Spawns") else nil
			if folder then
				for _, child in folder:GetChildren() do
					if child:IsA("BasePart") then
						table.insert(points, child)
					end
				end
			end
			return points
		end,
		current = function(): Model?
			return currentMap
		end,
	}
end

return MapRotation
```

Usage: `local maps = MapRotation.new(ServerStorage.Maps, workspace, Random.new())`, then `maps.loadNext()` at round start and `maps.unload()` after results.

- Excluding only the last map keeps rotation random while guaranteeing no back-to-back repeats; with a single map it is still allowed.
- Destroying before cloning means a crash mid-load leaves at most one map, never two overlapping.
- Parenting the fully built clone once replicates it in one batch instead of part by part.
- The original map name is kept as an attribute for the UI and analytics, since the clone is always called CurrentMap.

answer:
Hold the vote on the server as a map from player to choice. A vote is accepted only if it is one of the offered option strings, re-voting replaces the old vote, and leaving removes it. The winner is the option with most votes, ties broken randomly, and an empty vote picks randomly among all options.

```lua
--!strict
-- ModuleScript: ServerScriptService.MapVote
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

export type Vote = {
	cast: (player: Player, choice: any) -> boolean,
	tally: () -> { [string]: number },
	winner: (random: Random) -> string,
	close: () -> (),
}

local MapVote = {}

function MapVote.new(options: { string }): Vote
	assert(#options > 0, "a vote needs at least one option")
	local votes: { [Player]: string } = {}
	local open = true
	local valid: { [string]: boolean } = {}
	for _, option in options do
		valid[option] = true
	end

	local removing = Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player)
		votes[player] = nil
	end)

	local function tally(): { [string]: number }
		local counts: { [string]: number } = {}
		for _, option in options do
			counts[option] = 0
		end
		for _, choice in votes do
			counts[choice] += 1
		end
		return counts
	end

	return {
		cast = function(player: Player, choice: any): boolean
			if not open or type(choice) ~= "string" or not valid[choice] then
				return false
			end
			votes[player] = choice
			return true
		end,
		tally = tally,
		winner = function(random: Random): string
			local counts = tally()
			local best = -1
			local leaders: { string } = {}
			for _, option in options do
				if counts[option] > best then
					best = counts[option]
					leaders = { option }
				elseif counts[option] == best then
					table.insert(leaders, option)
				end
			end
			return leaders[random:NextInteger(1, #leaders)]
		end,
		close = function()
			open = false
			removing:Disconnect()
		end,
	}
end

return MapVote
```

Wiring the remote during intermission:

```lua
--!strict
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local MapVote = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("MapVote"))

local voteRemote = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("MapVoteRemote")

local function runVote(options: { string }, seconds: number): string
	local vote = MapVote.new(options)
	ReplicatedStorage:SetAttribute("VoteOptions", table.concat(options, ","))
	local connection = voteRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player: Player, choice: any)
		vote.cast(player, choice)
	end)
	task.wait(seconds)
	connection:Disconnect()
	vote.close()
	return vote.winner(Random.new())
end

return runVote
```

- Options are compared against the server's own list, so a client sending "AdminMap" or a table gets nothing.
- Keying votes by Player makes "one vote each" automatic, and changing your mind just overwrites your entry.
- Iterating `options` (an array) instead of the counts table keeps the order deterministic, so with a seeded Random the tie-break is reproducible.
